with the colour of pure liquid lac, Vibh-a 245,5 (sarii-
saraṇa-lohitaṁ) = Vism 261,30.

accha-vasā, f. (3accha + vasā), bear's grease;
pañca vasāni bhesajjāni: ~aṁ maccha-vasaṁ susukā-°
sūkara-° gadrabha-°, Vin I 200,23; V 129,5 (cf. Sp
II 255,16).

Accha-vihāra, m. Npr. of a monastery in Ceylon
Mhv-ṭ ad Mhv XXI 6.

Accha-sela, m. Npr. of a hill, Mhv XLVIII 94
cf. Accha-galla and °giri.

acchādana, n. [sa. ācchādana], covering, pro-
tection, shelter; clothes, mantle, cloak; Abh 290; 1104;
as a verbal noun giving the sense of √kap & √3vas,
Dhātup & Dhãtum; Th 698 (ghāsaṁ ~aṁ); Ja I
307,3-io (itthiyā sāmiko ~aṁ nãma); Mil 279,12; Ja
III 302,5*; VI 118,20* (= Vv 208); 316,26* = 320,25*
— AN III 50,19*; SN V 150,14 (v. l. acchāda);
DN III 160,11*; Dhp-alI 79,4; As 210,3 (pāna-
bhojana-sayana-°); pṝ.~āni, MhvXXXIV 6(—=cīvara-
sāṭakāni, Mhv-ṭ). — Ifc. v. ghāsa°, bhatta°, vattha°,
sātnika°.

acchādanā, f., 'covering, concealing', i. e. deceit,
Pp 19,30 = 23,30 ≠ Vibh 358,3 (+ vañcanā,
nikati, etc.); most likely a w. r. for accāsarā (q. v.),
see the explication in Vibh-a 493,17.

acchādāpeti, 3. sg. (caus. of acchādeti), to let
somebody put on (clothes), abs. ~etvā (vatthāni), Vin
I 22,12 (quoted Pj I 14,10 = Ss 69,12).

acchādita, mfn. (pp. of acchādeti), clad in
(with instr.), DN II 134,18*.

acchādeti, 3. sg. (sa. ā-cchādayati, ā + √chad),
to cover (acc), to clothe or present (a monk [acc] with
clothes [instr.J; to put on (clothes: acc); imper. ~ehi,
DN II 133,15 (mam ekena, scil. siṅgi-vaṇṇena yu-
gena; Sv); —- [pot. ~eyyaṁ (aggaḷaṁ), Vin I 290,2
v. l.]; — aor. ~esi, DN II 133,18 (with instr.); MN
I 353,14 (ticīvarena; Ps); Vin III 11,20 (do.); pl.
~esuṁ, Pv-a 50,9 (dvīhi vatthehi); —- fut. ~essāmi
= dassāmi, Vin III 216,14**, 29'; ~essasi, Ja IV 172,3
(vattha-yugāni); — abs. ~etvā, Vin II 253,23 =
AN IV 274,31 (kāsāyāni vatthāni); do.: DN I 60,18;
63,7; 115,20; 131,32; MN II 55,31; AN I 107,4; It
75,7; Pp 57,15; — Ja I 254,6 (ahata-vatthāni);
III 189,5 (dibba-vatthehi); IV 318,20 (ticīvarena).
Mil 88,3 (kambalena); — ~ayitvāna. Pv 61; 62;
Pv-a 49,19; 50,7. — pp. acchãdita & acchanna (q. v.);
caus. acchādāpeti (q. v.) — [Obs. the aor. a(c)chādesi
with different meanings: from chādeti, to please, DN
III 85,21, and from chādeti, to cover [ ˇ - - ˇ ], Ja
VI 581,21*].

acchāpeti (~ayati), 3. sg., caus. of acchati, to
get seated, Pay VI (ad Mogg V, 20?).

acchi, n. [sa. akṣi, cf. 1accha], eye, also mesh
(in a net), Abh 149. — Ifc. v. ubhayacchi-kāṇa,
ekacchi-kāṇa, kakkaṭaka° (cf. gavacchita & next).
[Note the Burmese spelling acchi for acci, SN IV
290,27 (see Sv (Ee) I p. XIII), and acchi, aor. of
acchati.]

acchijjati, 3. sg. (pass, of acchindati), to be
robbed; part. loc. ~ante, Nidd I 50,22 (Nidd-a).

a-cchidda, mfn. [sa. a-cchidra], uninjured,
without flows or defects; solid, compact, dense; AN V
79,17 = Vin II 248,22 (parisuddha + ~ appaṭi-
maṁsa); sīlāni akhaṇdāni (q. v.) +, DN III 245,25;
MN I 322,21 (Ps); ÁNIII 36,10; IV 54,6; SN IV
272,17 (= yesaṁ vemajjhe ekam pi na bhinnaṁ,
Vism 222,2); Dhp-a III 329,8 (sikkhā, jīvitavutti);
pabbato ~o asusiro ekaghano, Vin I 184,28; SN II
181,26; — SN IV 316,9 (udakamaṇiko, ~o hārī pari-
hārī).

acchiddaka, mfn. (from acchidda), unbroken,
uninterrupted; °-gaṇanā f., counting (of numbers) in
unbroken series, Sv I 95,20 (Sv-pṭ, Sv-nṭ; = 'ga-
ṇanā').

acchidda-kāri(n), mfn., doing something per-
fectly (i. e. without break or defects), akhanda-kārī +,
AN II 187,30; 243,19.

acchidda-pāṭhaka, m., a counter (of numbers)
in unbroken series, Sv I 157,19 (Sv-pṭ, Sv-nṭ; =
'gaṇaka').

acchidda-vacana, mfn., of reliable speech, v. r.
for advejjha-vacana, Bv II 110 (= niddosa-vacana,
Bv-a).

acchidda-vutti, mfn., leading a faultless mode
of life, Dhp 229 (Dhp-a III 329,9); DN III 192,13* (Sv
III 187,20 (Se writing acchinna-) = akhaṇḍa-vutti).

acchindati, 3. sg. [sa. ā + √chid], to tear off,
tear from, rob, plunder, deprive of; Vinl V 247,13;
pot. ~eyya, Vin IV 247,21**, 28'; Ps III 327,9 (yaṁ am-
hākaṁ deti taṁ ~); aor. acchindi, Vin IV 247,7;
Ja III 384,17; IV 343,1 (gāmaṁ); pl. ~iṁsu, Vin I
88,34 = III 212,2 (corā bhikkhū; Sp); Ps II 313,21
(ath'assa corā vatthāni ~), — Sv I 142,25; fut.
acchindissati, Vin IV 247,10 (cīvaraṁ); abs. (a) ~itvā,
MN II 109,30 (tassā sāmikaṁ); Ja II 422,5 (aññe-
saṁ yasaṁ); III 179,7 (hatthato kumāraṁ); 386,1
(yasaṁ datvā . . . sabbam ~); III 487,18 (rañño
rajjaṁ); Dhp-a I 56,6 (do.); Mil 20,14 (paresaṁ
bhoge); Dhp-a I 349,1 (parihāraṁ); ~itvā ganhati
- to tear from: Vin IV 245,9'; Jal V 358,10'; Pv-a
241.,5; Ps III 252,19; Ja VI 544,30' (~itvã gahaṇassa
bhāyāmi); (b) ~itvãna, Saddh 122; (c) acchejja (or
acchijja), SN I 127,3*-6* (Spk); —- pp. acchinna;
caus. acchindāpeti; pass, acchijjati (q. v.).

acchindana, n. (nom. act. from prec), depriving,
abolishing, Dhp-a III 70,22' (senāpati-ṭṭhānâdi-°,
= 'rājato upassaggaṁ'). — Ifc. v. cīvara-°.

acchindāpeti, 3. sg. (caus. of acchindati), to
cause to rob or deprive; pot. ~eyya, Vin IV 247,21**;
fut. ~essanti, Vin IV 224,6; aor. ~esi, Ps III 57,10
(taṁ ṭhãnantaraṁ ~, abolished that office (Tr.)).

1a-cchinna, mfn. [ts.], (a) not cut off, Ja II
78,7* (Ct.); in the phrase ~e theve (i. e. before it has
ceased to drop), Vin I 50,11 (Sp) — 53,25 = 286,32 =
II 227,11 = 230,35. (cf. acchinna-dhārã below). —
(b) not torn, not ragged (of cloth), v. °-dasa & a-cchin-
naka below.

2acchinna, mfn. [sa. ā-cchinna,pp. of acchindati],
robbed, plundered, Vin I 343,35 (balaṁ . . . koṭṭhā-
gāraṁ); IV 245,22 (bhikkhuniyo ~ā); Nidd I 50,23
(n. loc. ~e; Nidd-a). — Ifc. v. matthakâ°(?).

acchinna-cīvara, mfn., who has been robbed of
his garment, Vin III 212,17; 213,4 (Sp); Ja V
212,10-12.

a-cchinna-taṭa, mfn., having no abrupt banks,
Ja V 406,25' (= 'apabbhāra').

a-cchinna-dasa, mfn. 1acchinna + dasā), with
fringe or border of untorn cloth, Vin I 306,25 (~āni
cīvarāni).

a-cchinna-dhāra, mfn. (1a-cchinna + dhārā),
uninterruptedly streaming, with continual streams of
water, loc. ~e deve vassante: Ja II 269,10; III 37,6;
73,12. — °-dhārā, f. (or ~aṁ; adv.1), an uninter-
rupted stream (of water,); Ja I 330,21 (~aṁ devo vas-
santo); Ps II 342,6 (~aṁ katvā nadīsoto viya pavat-
teti . . . nirantaraṁ kathaṁ pavatteti).

acchinna-raṭṭha, mfn. (2acchinna + raṭṭha),
who is deprived of his kingdom, Ja VI 397,2*; 398,21'.

acchinna-lajjitā, f. (2acchinna + *lajjitã, see
lajji(n)), absence of bashfulness, Dhp-a I 188,13 (vipat-
tiyā ~āya alajjamānā).

acchinna-sadda, m., the noise made of one who
has been (or pretends to have been) robbed, Ja IV 45,19.

acchiva, m. [sa. akṣība, Hyperanthera Moringa],
a certain kind of tree, Ja VI 535,19*, 29' (v. l. Cks ac-
civa, Lk acchipa); Sp II 418,4 (Ce accīva).

acchupīyati, 3. sg. pass of next, to be inserted,
Vin II 112,36 (bahalāni maṇḍalāni na ~anti).

acchupeti, 3. sg. (ā + √chup, to touch), to insert
(aggalaṁ, q. v., a patch in a garment); pr. 1. sg.
~emi, Vin I 290,8; 2. sg. ~esi, ib. 9; part. ~entaṁ,
ib. 5; pot. ~eyyaṁ, ib. 2; aor. ~esi, ib. i; pass.
~īyati, q. v.

a-ccheka, mfn. (neg. of cheka), 1. not clever,
not skilful, Mil 250,30 (~ā a-sikkhitā a-sippino mati-
vippahīnā). — 2. not genuine, false (of coins), Ps II
464,15 (ayaṁ kūṭo, ayaṁ accheko [or read cheko(?),
cf. Vism 437,16]).'

2a-cchejja, mfn. (neg. grd. of chindati), not to
be severed or divided, Ps II 546,18 (nicca, etc.,
+ akkhaya).

a-cchetvā, neg. abs. = not having cut off, MN I
434,30 (see chindati).

acchedana, n. [sa. ā-cchedana], robbing, plun-
dering, Ja VI 544,27* (~assa bhāyāmi).

accheda-sarhki(n), mfn., in fear of being rob-
bed, Nidd I 50,22 (Nidd-a).

acchera, mfn. = acchariya (q. v. and cf. ācera,
macchera); ~o (dhammo) Th 552; ~aṁ lomahaṁ-
sanaṁ, Bv I 27; ~aṁ vata, Th 1085; Ja VI 97,14*;
513,28*; °-sata-maṇḍita, Saddh 244, 298; Kacc 633.

accheraka, (mf)n. (from prec.) — acchariya; ac-
cherakam maiii paṭibhāti, Ja VI 24,25* (= mama
acchariyaṁ upaṭṭhāti, Ct ; Ed. accherakammaṁ
paṭ°); Ja VI 275,23'; 513,26*; ~aṁ pātihīraṁ, Bv
I 9 (Bv-a); Vv 965. — Ifc. v. ati-°.

accheratara, mfn. compar. of acchera; ito pi
~aṁ, Vv 966.

acchera-rūpa, mfn. = acchariya; SN I 181,5*
(~aṁ paṭibhāti mam idaṁ); Pv 444 (Pv-a 197,20).
cf. acchariya-rūpa.

acchôdaka, mfn. ( accha + udaka), with clear
water; in the formula: ~, sātḍdaka, sītḍdaka, setaka,
sūpatittha, ramaṇīya: MN I 76,27 (pokkharanī) —
283,36 = SN I 91,6 = AN III 190,5 (Mp); 238,11;
DN II 128,28 (Kakutthā nadī ~ikā [not ~akã] =
pasannḍdakā, Sv); — Vin III 108,15 (daho ~o, etc.
— pasannḍdako, Sp), quoted Ps III 645,15; — f. ~ā
Vv 901 (pokkharaṇī); f. pl. ~ā (pokkharañño), Vv
482. (Rem.: Kakutthaṁ acchôdi-sãtôdika-vippa-
sannaṁ, DN II 135,4*, haplology as in somana-
domanassaṁ, Sn 67, see Sadd III 158).

acchôdika, mfn., = acchḍdaka; m. pl. ~ikā
(selā), Th 113 = 601 ('acchḍdaka' ti vattabbe liṅga-
vipallāsena acchodikā ti vuttaṁ, Th-a).

a-citta, mfn. [ts.], without understanding, Ja IV
254,3* (sabbo loko para-citte ~o); senseless, ~aṁ
kaliṅgara-kaṇḍaṁ, Ja III 273,19 (Cks ~aṁ apitta-
kaṁ, cf. Rt sit-pit næti = 'acetana', Dhp-a II 249,12);
opp. sa-cittaka, ib. 20.

a-cittaka, mfn., without mind, senseless, uncon-
scious, Mil 77,28; Dhp-a II 142,8; Ja IV 58,3' ( =
'aceta(s)') ; Dhp-a III 356,21 (= 'acetasā') ; Ps II
493,6; III 49,13; °-kāla, m., the time of uncon-
sciousness, Ps II 493,4; °-saraṇa-gamana, n., taking
the refuge without consciousness (before the birth),
Ps III 303,20; °-âpatti, f., unconscious offence, Ps
II 540,21, —- Cf. sa-cittaka.

a-citta-kāya, m(fn.), (having) a body without
intelligence, Ja VI 210,1' (an-indriya-baddhaṁ ~aṁ
= 'a-sañña-kāya').

a-citta-vasika, mfn., not in the power of the
mind, controlling the mind, Ps II 345,17 (cittaṁ
attano vase vattetvā).

a-citti-kata, mfn. (cf. citti-karoti), disregarded,
discarded, considered insignificant, despised, Vin IV
6,17' (oñāta + ; = agarukata, Sp); Mil 288,14 (do.);
DN II 356,2 (~aṁ dānaṁ; see asakkaccaṁ) ≠ MN III
22,20 (abs. acitti-katvā) ≠ AN III 171,30 (do., v. l.
acittiṁ katvã; = acittīkārena agārava-vasena, Mp).

a-cittī-kāra, m. (cf. prec), disregard, Vibh 371,9
(Vibh-a 499,30); Mp III 63,11. —- °-kata, mfn., Nidd I
228,12, etc. (= bahumānakiriyā-rahita, Ct.).

a-cintaka, mfn., not thinking (or sorrowing),
Pj II 82,21 (nâhaṁ cintemi, ~o 'mhi jāto).

a-cintita, mfn. [ts.], never thought of, °-pubbaṁ
(before), Dhp-a III 71,1 (adiṭṭha-assuta-°).

a-cintiya, mfn. [sa. a-cintya], — acintanīya,
Vv 972; Sp I 89,8*; Mil 189,1; = °-ânubhāva, mfn.,
Vv-a 340,25 (of unimaginable magnificence, v. l. acin-
teyya°).

a-cinteyya, mfn. = do., ~āni (cattāri), AN II
80,15 (Mp); Dhp-a II 199,3 (cf. 288,11 = Mp ad AN
II 80,15: cintetuṁ ayuttāni, na cintetabbāni). —
a-cinteyyatta, n. abstr., Mp ib.

a-cira, mfn. [ts.], not of long duration, ~aṁ
(adv.), soon, shortly, quickly, Ja VI 573,13*; Thī 468;
Dhp 41. Cf. acirā, acirena. — Ifc. cirâciraṁ.

a-cira-arahattappatta, mfn., who has lately
attained arhatship, SN I 196,8.

a-cira-kārita, mfn., lately built, navaṁ ~aṁ
(santhāgāraṁ), SN IV 182,16 (= adhunā nitthāpitaṁ,
Spk) = MN I 353,21.

a-cira-ṭṭhitīka, mfn., of no long permanence,
Ja V 507,28* (an-addhaneyya +, scil. vāri (thale
vaṭṭaṁ)).

a-cira-pakkanta, mfn., lately gone away, Sn
p. 124,23 (~assa Kokāliyassa = pakkantassa sato
naciren' eva, Pj); SN I 153,27 (~e Devadatte = naci-
rass' eva gate); MN I 68,6 (imasmā dhammavinayā);
II 253,26 (gāmā, abl.); AN IV 360,25; SN V 346,6.

a-cira-pabbajita, mfn., who has lately entered
the fraternity; navako ~o, SN I 185,7; navo ~o adhu-
nāgato imaṁ dhamma-vinayaṁ, Vin I 40,20, quoted
Dhp-a I 92,11; pl. MN I 458,1; AN III 138,11; ~ānaṁ
bhikkhūnaṁ, Dhp-a III 424,2.

a-cira-parinibbuta, mfn., having lately attained
Nibbāna, Sn p. 59,17 (scil. Nigrodhakappa); SN V
163,27 (scil. Sāriputta-Moggallānā); MN III 7,14 (scil.
Bhagavā); DN I 204,3 (do.; Sv, pt, at).

Aciravata, m. Npr. of a novice (sāmaṇera),
MN III 128,10 foll. (~o samaṇuddeso); also called
Aggivessana, ib. n foll.

Aciravatī, f. [sa. Ajirăvatī, Pāṇ VI 3,119; c:j,
cf. aggiparijita, vijeyya: viceyya] Npr. of a river (prob,
the present Rāptī), Abh 682 (one of the five great
rivers, acirarḥ sīgham gamanam etissam atthī ti A.,
Abh-sūci); SN II 135,2 (Gaṅgā+); V 38—40 (do.);
AN IV 101,6 (do.); V 22,19 (etc. do.); Vin II 237,35
(do.); Mil 87,13 (do., quoted As 142,25); Pj II 439,20
(do); DN I 235,6 (on its shore the village Manasākaṭa
in the Kosala-country); AN III 402,15 (Daṇḍakappaka,
do.); Vin I 191,1 (at Sāvatthī); Vin III 63,17; IV
111,33; 259,33; Ja I 418,8; II 96,5; 366,2; III 137,8;
IV 167,3 (°-tīre); Pj II 19,11; 308,4; 511,5 (°nadī-
tīre); Dhp-a I 336,9; II 264,4 (°-nadim); III 449,22;
IV 41,2; 87,3; 160,7; Thī-a 54,6; Vv-a 248,17. —
°-tittha, n., a ferry place on the A., Ja III 228,8.

a-cira-vibbhanta, mfn., who has lately seceded
from the Saṁgha, f. ~ā, Vin IV 216,8.

a-cira-vuṭṭhita, mfn., who has lately got up
(after a sickness), DN II 99,15 (Bhagavā gilānā
vuṭṭhito ~o gelaññā) - SN V 153,3; Ja V 424,15.

a-cirā, (abl.) ind. [sa. acirāt], soon, shortly;
Ja VI 153,27* (= a-cirena).

a-cirūpasampanna, mfn., who has lately received
ordination (upasampadā), Sn p. 16,4; DN I 177,1 (Sv);
II 153,2; MN II 49,10; 60,31; Vin III 15,2 (Sp).

a-cirena, (instr.) ind. [sa. acireṇa], = 'acirā',
Ja VI 154,17'; 573,14'. Cf. nacirena.

a-cīvaraka, m(fn)., who has not a monk's dress
(cf. cīvara), ~o, Vin I 90,18 (na upasampādetabbo).

a-ceta(s), mfn. [ts.], — prec. (or subst, n.); instr.
~asã, Ja IV 57,5* (= acittakena, ib. 58,3').

a-cetana, mfn. [ts.], unconscious, senseless;
(and rarely: thoughtless); MN I 296,8 (kaṭṭham; Ps);
Mil 96,10 (aggikkhandho); 97,11 (vāyodhātu); 173,4
(rukkho); 179,8 (mahā-pathavī); 268,5 (opp. sa-
cetana); Ja VI 311,9 (rukkho); Ja III 24,1*, quoted
Mil 172,24*; Ja I 46,18*-20 (for -âbhãva read acetana-
bhāva m., = the being unconscious); Dhp-a II 249,12
(opp. sa-cetana; = sit-pit næti, Rt); Ja III 92,7*
(ajānanatāya ~am, Ct.); VI 210,1'; Thī 453 (bālā
duppaññā ~ā; Thī-a); Vibh-a 57,20 etc. [Ja VI
12,27', misprint for acetaso, Ck].

a-cetasa, mfn., = acetana, Dhp 248 (v. r. for
asaññata, Dhp-a III 356,21 = acittaka); Ja V 66,12*
(mūḷho ~o); VI 12,24* (mūgo pakkho ~o; = acit-
tako); SN I 198,30* (appapaññaṁ ~am; Spk =
kāraṇa-jānana-samatthena cittena rahitaṁ).

a-cetasika, mfn. [a + cetasika, q. v.], uncon-
scious, 'automatic', 'not involved in the life of sense',
Dhs p. 5,12 and §§584, 1190, 1513 (dhammā ~ā);
Kv 433,29 (sīlam ~aṁ; Kv-a); Vibh 12,24; 67,5.

a-cela, m., 'unclothed', a naked ascetic, Ja V 16,3*;
77,20*; Ud 65,5 (jatilā, niganthā, etc.) ≠ SN I 78,2;
— DN I 161,3 (Kassapa); III 6,9 (Korakkhattiya);
III 9,16 (Ed. Kandaramasuka, ɔ: prob. Kaḷāramaḍḍu-
ka); III 12,15 (Pāṭika-putta); MN I 387,10 (Seniya);
— ifc. Karambiya-° Ja V 75,20 (cf. Kārambhiya).

a-celaka, m. = acela; Abh 440, 1110; Vin IV
92,4**, 8'; Ja V 18,25'(= 'acela');pZ.~ā,Dhp-a I 400,13;
Ja III 246,18; Dhp-a III 489,17 (apaṭicchannehi ~ehi);
— Dhp-a I 309,3 (+ ājīvako, nigaṇṭhako, tāpaso);
Ja VI 229,7' (Kassapa-gotta); Mil 201,30 (Kāram-
bhiyo, cf. Ja V 86,2* & Karambiya-°, ib. 76,28 ); — adj.
~o hoti muttâcāro hatthâpalekhano, MN I 307,23 =
342,25 = 412,4 = II 161,26 = DN I 166,2 (Sv; tt); III
40,27 = AN I 295,8 = II 206,7; do. pl. MN I 238,15 (cf.
AN III 384,5: scil. Nando Vaccho, Kiso Saṅkicco,
Makkhali Gosālo); — nâhaṁ ~assa °-mattena sāmañ-
ñaṁ vadāmi, MN I 281,33. — °-laddhi, f., the doc-
trine of the naked ascetics, Ps III 254,4. — °-vagga,
m., title of AN I 295—299; Vin IV 91—108; V 19—21;
39_40. — °-vāda, m. = °-laddhi, Ja III 246,19. —
°-sāvaka, m., a lay devotee of the A.s, pl. ~ā, AN
III 384,2 (gihī odātavasanā+). — °-sikkhāpada,
n. = Pācittiya 41 (Vin IV 91—92).

Acela-Kassapa, m., Npr. of a naked ascetic,
converted by the Buddha, DN I 161,3 foll, (acelo Kas-
sapo); MN III 124,28 foll. (Mp I 310,1); SN II 19,3
foll.; IV 300,8 foll. Cf. Kassapa.

a-cora, m., not a thief, Ja I 385,16; °-bhāva, m.
abstr. ib. 386,13. — a-corikā, adj. f., Vv 295 (cf. v. r.).

a-corāharaṇa, mfn., not to be carried off by
thieves, Khp VIII 9 (nidhi, v. l. a-cora-haraṇa, Pj I
224,20, cf. App. p. 255); Mil 320,30 (duppasaho+,
scil. ākāso).

a-ch°, sometimes spelt instead of the more frequent
acch°, e. g. a-chatta, a-chambhi(n), a-chinna.

aja, m. [ts.], a (he-)goat, Abh 502, cf. Sadd II 188;
+ urabbha, DN I 127,12 (°-satāni thūnūpanītāni
yaññatthāya) = AN IV 41,13; MN I 344,7 (~ā hañ-
ñantu yaññatthāya) = AN II 207,29 = IV 42,22 =
Pp 56,24; urabbha + ~ + miga, SN II 188,17;
MN III 167,24; ~ā pasū manussã, Mil 100,6; — Ja
V 241,24* (ajiyaṁ ajañ ca); III 278,1 (opp. ajikā);
Pv-a 80,21 (~go-mahisâdi); Ja III 278,13'( = 'bhasta').
Cf. ajā, ajī, ajāmiga, ajeḷaka, urabbha, chakala(ka),
meṇḍa, 2vassa.

ajaka, m. [ts.] = prec. (dimin.), Vin II 154,10
(~ā pi pasukā pi); Ud-a 82,2 (~e viya satte lāpetī
ti Ajaka-lāpako). Cf. ajikā, f.

ajakara, m. (= ajagara, q. v.); ~aṁ medaṁ,
acc, Ja III 484,16* (= ajakara-medaṁ, Ct., = pim-
buru-mas, Ja-pota), the fat of serpents [a split-com-
pound like timiraṁ pupphaṁ, mūlā akusalā, q. v.].

Ajakalāpaka, m. Npr. of a yakkha, Ud 4,30
(Ud-a 81,17, with two etymm.). — Do. n. Npr. of a
cetiya, ii.

aja-kotthāsa, m., goats as a part (of the offering),
Ud-a 81,18."

ajagara, m. [ts.; see also ajakara], the Python
or rock snake (= pimburu, Ja-pota, Bt, IIīnaṭ, cf.
Mil Trsl II 349, n. 2); Abh 651; Ap 129,3;.pl. ~ā, Ja
VI 507,2* (avisā mahabbalā); Mil 364,11 (~assa ekaṁ
aṅgaṁ gahetabbaṁ) = 406,17; As 375,19 (mahā, cf.
Dhp-a III 60,12). — °-parivārita, mfn., surrounded
by snakes, Mil 23,21. —- °-peta, m., a peta in the
shape of that, Dhp-a III 60,12; ~assa vatthu, n., title
of Dhp-a III 60—-64. — °-mukha, n., the mouth of
a snake, Mil 303,15 (~en'eva ~aṁ parivattitvā).

a-jaggita, mfn. (cf. jaggati), not taken care of,
Ps II 362,12 (°-ṭṭhānaṁ jagganto).

aja-camma, n., the skin of a goat, Vin I 196,5
(eḷaka-camma +, cf. attharaṇa).

a-jacca, mfn., of low birth, Ja VI 100,9* (= hīna-
jacca, Ct.; opp. jātiva(t), which is w. r. for jātima(t));
Ja III 19,22* (used as a Npr., cf. Ct.).

a-jajjara, mfn., not decaying; n. = Nibbāna,
SN IV 369,23 (v. l. ajjaraṁ), cf. the uddāna ib. 373,20*
= Nett 55,8* (uppāda-jarãhi anabbhāhatattā ~aṁ,
Ct.); also title of the sutta SN IV 369 — °-gāmi(n),
mfn., leading to N°, SN IV 369,23.

a-jañña, mfn. [sa. a-janya, see jaññajañña],
(unfit for men), disgusting, dangerous, Ja II 437,17*
(= paṭikkūla, amanāpa, Ct., cf. Ps ad MN I 30,29),
quoted Ja III 244,6*. — n., aportent, bad omen, Abh 401.

a-jaṭâkāsa, m., the open space (of the universe),
Ps II 249,2 (~aṁ pakkhannā, scil. rasmiyo); As 14,25
(~aṁ pakkhandiṁsu, scil. rasmiyo); Mhbv 55,16,23;
As 314,21 (opp. kaṇṇacchiddâkāsa); 315,4; 346,21.

a-jaddhuka, n. or °kā, f. (?, cf. next), the practice
of abstaining from food, MN I 245,13 (= abhojanaṁ,
Ps); cf. Tr. ib. p. 550 and Ps II 391, note [the v. l.
ajajjitaṁ may mean *ajajjhitaṁ, with jjh << kṣ,
cf. Pischel § 326, Geiger § 56, if not eyen~ikaṁ from
*a-jajjhikā, f., cf. a-jānikā, HS].

a-jaddhu-māri (and °-mārikā), f. (a+ *jagdhu
[cf. sa. jagdhvā, √jakṣ] + māri), death from starvation,
Ja VI 63,15* (°-māri(ṁ) va khudāya mīye ṣ= anāsaka-
maraṇam eva, Ct.); — °-mārikaṁ marissati (cf.
°-khādikā, °-cārikā, etc., paronom.), AN IV 283,6 =
287,14 = 324,10 (— anātha-maraṇaṁ, Mp). — Cf. E.
Leumann, Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen, 1.899 p. 594.

ajana, n. [ts., cf. √aj], the act of instigating or
moving, Sadd III 1259 (— 'acchā', cf. ajjhā, Kacc-v
640, where Mmd (Ce) has acchā).

a-janapada, m., not-country (see 3a, 2); MN II
98,1 (janapadā pi ~ā katā, depopulated) ≠ AN I 160,2.

a-janayamāna, mfn. (neg. part, of janeti), not
producing, Nidd I 51,23 (Nidd-a).

a-janetabba, mfn. (neg. grd. of janeti), that
cannot be produced, Mp II 480,8 (°-kukkucca, see
akukkuccaka-j āta).

a-japa, mfn. (see japati), not muttering prayers,
Ud-a 65,16 (in etym, of Ajapāla-nigrodha).

aja-patha, m. [ts.], a goat-track, Mil 280,23
(+ saṅku-patha, vetta-patha); Mp II 73,2 (°-saṅku-
pathâdayo); Nidd I 155,6 (= ajehi gantabba-mag-
gaṁ, Nidd-a).

aja-pada, mfn. [ts.], Utt. goat-footed, said of a
forked stick, MN I 134,17 (~ena daṇḍena); Ja IV
457,17 (do.). — °-daṇda, m. [cf. Vyu 273,94], a stick
cleft like a goat's hoof,'As 173,22 = Vism 161,30 (cf.
Ja I 241,9*, but see Ct.). — °-saṇṭhāna, mfn., shaped
like a goat's hoof, Abhidh-av 66,27 (~e padese, the seat
of the smelling in the nose) ≠ As 310,29.

1aja-pāla, m. [ts.], a goatherd, or a breeder of
goats, Dhp-a I 176,23; Ja IV 250,4; °-brāhmano, Ja
III 401,13.

2Ajapāla, m. Npr. of a purohitaputta, Ja IV
476,8; 482,9 (°-kumāra); 491,4.

2aja-pālaka, n., a kind of bush, Costus speciosus,
Abh 303; 1120 (= 'kuṭṭha').

1aja-pālaka, m. = 1ajapāla, Dhp-a I 176,26;
Ja IV 476,8; f. ~ikā, q. v.

Ajapāla-nigrodha, m., a banyan tree near Uru-
velā on the Nerañjanī, where the Buddha passed (a) the
fifth and (b) the eighth week after the bodhi [according to
Ja I 78,1i—80,1; 81,5-13 ≠ Bv-a introd., As 35,9;
cf. Tuneld, Recherches (1915) p. 98 foll.]; here
lake place the interviews with (a) Mara, DN II 112,22;
SN II 03,2, 24 (104,18); (Mara and) his daughters, SN
I 122,27(—127,20); Ja l 469,15; Dhp-a I 201,1s; III
195,24; Pj II 544,20; the huhuṁkajātika-brāhmaṇa,
Ud 3,8 (Ud-a, three etymm.) ≠ Vin I 2,27 (Sp one
etym.); (b) with Brahma Sahampati (brahma-yācana):
Vin I 4,30 ≠ SN I 136,4 (138,31); SN V 167.~6; 185,5
(quoted Kv 559,29); 232,15; AN II 20,6 (Mp, one
etym.); Dhp-a I 86,15. See besides DN II 267,23 (Pan-'
casikha, 'in the eighth week', Sv); Bv II 63.

Ajapāla-saññi(n), m., 'named after Ajapāla' =
prec. (cf. saññi(n) & saññita), Dāṭh I 55,60 (~ino,
scil. vaṭassa).Ajapāla-saññi

Ajapāla-saññi(n), m., 'named after Ajapāla' =
prec. (cf. saññi(n) & saññita), Dāṭh I 55,60 (~ino,
scil. vaṭassa).Ajapāla-saññi

aja-bhūta, mfn., born as a goat, SN II 188,17
(gen. pl. ~ānaṁ, a paraphrase to ajānaṁ sataṁ).

aja-moja, m.(?) [cf. sa. ajamodã and the Sinhalese
spellings ajamojaka, ajamodaka; thus -j- may be a
Sinhalese hyperpalism, HS], name of a plant, Vv-a
186,24 (tikaṭuka-° -hiṅgu-jīraka-lasuṇâdīhi kaṭuka-
bhaṇḍehi).

aja-yuddha, n., a combat of goats, DN I 6,15
(hatthi-yuddha + . . .) quoted Nidd I 366,26 (v. l.).

aja-yūtha, n., a herd of goats, Ja III 401,14,2 3*;
V 241,23*.

a-jara, mfn. [ts.], not subject to old age or decay,
Ja VI 589,28* (~o tvaṁ amaro bhava); AN II 247,28
(~aṁ anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ nibbānaṁ); Thī
511—12; Th 32 (opp. jīramāna).

a-jara(s), n. [ts.], absence of decay, instr, ajarasā,
SN I 36,28* ; 37,1* (Spk = ajīraṇena avipattiyā);
also title of the sutta ib. 38,26 .a-jara

aja-ratha, m., a carriage drawn by goats, acc. pl.
~e, Ja VI 48,20*; 52,6'.

a-jara(s), n. [ts.], absence of decay, instr, ajarasā,
SN I 36,28* ; 37,1* (Spk = ajīraṇena avipattiyā);
also title of the sutta ib. 38,26 .a-jara

aja-rāja, m., lord of goats, Ja III 279,6*; Sīmāv
24,6 (Bodhisatto).

ajarâmara, mfn. [ts.], undecaying and immortal,
Ja III 515,23*; V 186,31'; 236,6; VI 82,28*; 300,6';
Thī 512 (read: idan tam ajarâmaraṁ padam asokaṁ,
see Thī-a 293,26); Mil 268,6; Dhp-a I 229,5.

a-jaḷa, mfn. [sa. ajaḍa], not stupid, DN III 265,16
(paññavā ~o aneḷamūgo); AN III 137,16; 175,22;
176,11; 437,4; IV 227,3 (do.); AN I 35,20 (do. pl. =
amūḷhā, Mp).

aja-laṇdikā, f., a ball of goat dung, Ja I 419,16 foll.
(nāḷimattā [sukkhā] ~ā, acc. pl.; = elu-beti, Ja-pota)
≠ Dhp-a II 70,11 foll.; Pv-a 283,3-7; Mp II 259,5.

aja-vata, mfn., living after the practice of goats
(as certain ascetics), in the comp. °-govatā, m. pl.,
Ja IV 318,8. Cf. ajasīla.

aja-visāṇa-baddhaka, mf(~ikā)n., with points
like goat's horns (said of a certain kind of shoes),
Vin I 186,12 (Sp, quoted Trsl II 15, note 6; B. reads
°-bandhikā).

aja-vīthi, f. [sa. ajavīthī], the part of the sun's
and the moon's path (from Mūlā to Uttarāsāḷhā) cor-
responding to the dry season; + nāgavīthi, govīthi,
Sp-ṭ ad Sp I 119,26.
aja-saṁgha, m., a crowd of goats, Ps III 453,11.
aja-sadda, m., the cry of a goat, Ud-a 82,3.

aja-sīla, n., the practice of goats (as a way of
tapas), PsII 19,10; Pj II 522,15 (°-gosīla-kukkura-
sīla-°); cf. ajavata.

a-jahita, mfn. (cf. jahāti, pp.), not abandoned,
not forsaken, Ja VI 14,19* (siriyā ~o hoti yo mit-
tānaṁ na dūbhati).

2ajja, n. [sa. ājya], clarified butter for sacrifices,
conjectured by Kern p. 66 in Ja VI 207,2* (see
ajjhena).

1ajja, ind. [sa. adya], to-day, now, at this day,
Abh 1155 (= atrâhe); Kacc-v 573 (— imasmiṁ kale);
Sadd III 1167—68; Sn 153 ≠ Vin I 102,34**; Dhp
326 (ajj'ahaṁ); Pv 78 (= idāni, Pv-a); DN II 134,10
(rattiyā pacchimayāme); 148,30 (do.); MN I 393,18
(akālo kho ~... sve dānâhaṁ . . .) ; Ja I 207,13
(ajjâpi tāva, until this day, with the verb in pr. 2 sg.);
279,8; 286,18 (~ ādiṁ katvā, from to-day); Dhp-a
IV 76,16 (do., cf. Pj II 157,7); ajja paṭṭhāya, Dhp-a
I 12,8 (cf. ajjappabhuti); Ja III 217,8 (ajjâpi . . . na
. . ., not yet); 425,27* (read with Cks tassa pahūnam
ajjã, cf. bahūna); VI 309,2*; 561,20*, 21* (ajj'eva
imaṁ rattirh); ajj'etarahi, Mil 144,10; 276,4; ajja
ajj'[eva], Dhp-a III 159,19 = PsI 277,1; opp. sve:
Ps I 57,30; I 115,15 (ajja vā sve vā). — Cf. apa-
rajju, alam dān' ajja, sajju.

ajjaka or ajjuka, n. (or m.) [sa. arjaka, m.],
name of a plant (Ocimum gratissimum), Abh 579
(= sitapaṇṇāsa, sinh, hela-aṅdu); n. ~aṁ, Vin IV
35,9' (-U-; no v. l.; + phaṇijjakaṁ hiriveraṁ =
'agga-bīja') = Sv I 81,21 ' (Ed. -u-, MSS -a-;
= setapaṇṇāsa, nṭ) ≠ Spk II 331,4 (Se ajjakaṁ);
cf. ajjukaṇṇa.ajjaka

[ajja-kāla, m.], this time; abl. ~ā (yāv'), Dhp-a
I 53,9; Bv-a introd. v. 4 (CP ~aṁ); As 32,22; this
morning, acc. ~aṁ (adv.), Ja VI 180,3* (= pāto va).

ajjuṇho (or ajjaṇho), ind., (only) this day (ɔ:
the rest of the present day-and-night), Vin I 25,19*
(viharemu ~ aggisālamhi); III 220,29 (~ bhante
āgamehi; Sp = bhante ajja ekadivasaṁ amhākaṁ
tiṭṭha, adhivāsehîti attho; Sp-ṭ: ~ ti pāṭhe ajjaṇho
ti pi paṭhanti; Vmv: ajjaṇho = ajja ekadivasaṁ;
cf. also Mogg III 118); Vin IV 80,2. According to Kern
p. 68 haplology for ajja + *juṇho 'this evening', but
more likely representing *adyu (= adya, cf. aparajju,
sajju) + ahnaḥ, cf. ved. idā(nīm) ahnaḥ- Cf. ajj'eka-
divasaṁ and see aṇha ifc.ajjuṇho

ajjatagge, v.r. ajjadagge, ind., from now, hence-
forth (t: d cf. s. v. kukkuṭa-sampātika, etc.); prob. —
*ajjato agge, see anamatagga, mfn., and daharatagge,
and cf., otherwise, āyatagga, ettāvatagga, tamatagge;
Ctt. take ajjatagge = ajjatā + agge; ajjataṁ ādiṁ
katvā (Sp I 173,14 = Sv I 236,6, etc.) and explain
-d- in ajjadagge as a sandhi consonant; gramm, regard
-t- as a sandhi cons., Kacc-v 35; Sadd III 56; Pay
ad Mogg I 45). — (a) in the usual formula upãsakaṁ
mam Bhagavā dhāretu ~ pāṇupetaṁ saranagataṁ:
Vin III 6,12 (Sp see above);' DN I 85,14 (Sv do.);
MN I 24,9 (Ps); SN I 70,13 (Spk); AN I 56,10 (Mp);
Sn2 p. 16 note 1 (Pj II 157,5); Ud 49,29 (Ud-a); simi-
larly: ~ maṁ āyasmanto brahmacāriṁ (etc.) dhāretha,
AN III 216,5—-217,1; ~ maṁ Bhagavā dāsīsamaṁ ...
dhāretu, ib. IV 94,1; — (b) in other phrases (with the
foll, verb in pres. or fut.): esâhaṁ ~, AN II 199,25;
III 392,19; ete mayaṁ ~ upavasissāma, ib. V 86,12;
~ āvarāmi dvāraṁ niganthānaṁ, MN I 380,17
(quoted Sp I 173,6; Sv I 235,81; Ps I 136,27; Mp II
28,4); ~ dãn' āhaṁ uposathaṁ karissāmi, Ud 60,21
= Vin II 198,21; cf. Dhp-a I 142,11 = III 154,11;
tâhaṁ ~ paṭikkhipãmi, Vin I 56,7 ; ~ maṁ dassa-
nāyôpasaṁkama, Th 485 (here the Ct. gives ajjadagge
as first reading, and ajjatagge as pi-pãṭha); ayaṁ
~ mama putto, Ja VI 344,18.

ajjatana, mfn. [sa. adyatana], referring to
to-day, modern; Mogg-v VI 5* (~o kālo); Th 552
(dhammo; = adhunâgato, Th-a); n. ~ām iva (in
sandhi for ~aṁ, opp. porāṇaṁ), Dhp 227 (= adhunā
uppannaṁ, Ct.); yãv'ajjatanā (abl.), until to-day,
Ja II 409,7; III 264,21; f. ~ī (q. v.). [For ajjatana,
Vin II 275,17, read ajj'attanā, cf. ib. 275,4,6 attanā
pavāretvā; ajjattanā ti ajjatana, Vjb]. — Ifc. v.
an-°.

ajjatanāya, ind. (dat. of ajjatana), for to-day;
adhivāsetu (adhivāsehi) ... me ~ bhattaṁ, DN I
109,23 (Sv); II 88,9; Vin I 17,29; Pv-a 171,13;
Dhp-a I 33,8. Cf. svātanãya.

ajjatanī, f. [sa. adyatanī], the aorist tense, Kacc
421 (its use; samīpe ~) ≠ Sadd III 887 sg., 891; Kacc
430 (its endings); Sadd 29,20; III 901; cf. Mogg
VI 4, Būp 452—3. — °-vibhatti, f., id., Kacc-v 421.

ajjatā, f. abstr. of ajja, the time of to-day, an
artificial word only used in the phrase ~taṁ ādiṁ
katvā, explaining the sense of ajjatagge (q. v.):
Sp I 173,14; Sv I 236,6; Spk I 159,20; PsI 137,1;
Mp II 28,12; Pj II 157,β; Ud-a 288,14; ajjatañ ca.
SN I 83,29 (no Ct.), is prob. w. r. (cf. v. l. ajj'eva),

[*ajjati], pr. 3 sg. [sa. √arj], to get, obtain, Ja III
263,4*, doubtful conjecture by Kern p. 67 for majjati,
q. v.]. Cf. √ajj.

ajjadagge, v. r. for ajjatagge (q. v.), cf. yadagge,
tadagge, and the v. l. daharadagge.

ajja-divasa, m. [sa. adya-divasa], the present
day, Ja IV 109,3' (opp. hiyyo-divasa): Ps TI 249,7
(yāv'~ã); III 378,5 (do.); MhvXXXII,23 (do.). Cf.
ajjekadivasaṁ.

ajjana, n. [sa. arjana], getting, acquiring, = √ajj
& √sajj2, Dhātup 73, 548; Dhātum 87, 769; Sadd II
189; Saddh 98 (~âdīni dukkhāni). — °-âraha, mfn.,
worthy of being acquired, Pj I 223,6 (= 'ajjeyya').

[ajj[ā/a]bhamu], prob, for *accabhamu, mfn.; see
acc°, ajjha°, and cf. sa. atibhrū, 'highbrowed', frown-
ing; Ja VI 476,12* (Ed. ajja bhamuṁ, Se accabha-
muṁ, Ja-pot ajjābhamuṁ; = evaṁ atikkamitvā
ṭhitabhamuṁ, Ct.).[ajjābhamu]

ajja-ratti, f., this night, last night; acc. ~iṁ
(cf. ajja-kālaṁ), Ja III 506,6; Dhp-a II 265,13; loc.
~iyaṁ (or ~iyā), Ja III 23,3 (~ paccūsasamaye, this
(coming) morning); cf. ajja . . . rattiyā, DN II 134,10;
148,30; ajja rattibhāge, Ja VI 370,25V

ajjava, m. n. [abstr. from uju, sa. ārjava; Kacc-v
404 ājjava (Ee ājava), criticized by Sadd III 857,
admitting ajjavo (cf. gārava, m.) and 'rarely' ajjavaṁ;
Mogg IV 139 only ajjavaṁ], straightness, rightness,
honesty: nom. sg. (a) ajjavo ca maddavo ca, Dhs
p. 7,29 (As 53,13; quoted Sadd III 857); Dhs 1339
(see Vyu 126,14-15, but also Mvu I 133,8-9); —
(b) ajjavañ ca maddavañ ca, khantī ca soraccañ ca,
AN I 94,24 (Mp, Mp-ṭ); Sn 292 (acc); Ja III 274,1*
(do.?); ajjavañ ca lajjavañ ca, khanti ca soraccañ ca,
DN III 213,1 (Sv) cf. Mhv LXXXIV, 23: addava . . .
lajjidhamma [addava blending of ajjava and mad-
dava]; instr, ajjavena javena maddavena khan-
tiyā soraccena, AN II 113,24 = III 248,10 (Mp III
94,3). — Ifc. v. an-°. — °-tā, f. id., Dhs 1339. —
°-maddava, n. (dvandva), honesty and kindness,
Sn 250 (~e rato, = ujubhāve ca mudubhãve ca rato,
Pj). — °-lakkhaṇa, mfn., characterized by straight-
ness, Abhidh-av 20,30 (cf. As 131,9).

ajja-saṭṭhiṁ, ind. (from ajja saṭṭhī, to-day is
the sixth day), six days ago, SN I 170,20*, 34* ( =
ajja cha-divasa-matthakā paṭṭhāya, Spk).

ajja-ssuve, ind. (i. e. ajja + sve (suve), two
words cf. Pāṇ V 2,13), to-day or to morrow, Ja III
260,12* (~ ti puriso sadatthaṁ nâvabujjhati); Ja V
66,9* (Ed. ajja suve ti saṁseyya); Pv 512 (ajja suve;
but--------).

[ajj[ā/a]bhamu], prob, for *accabhamu, mfn.; see
acc°, ajjha°, and cf. sa. atibhrū, 'highbrowed', frown-
ing; Ja VI 476,12* (Ed. ajja bhamuṁ, Se accabha-
muṁ, Ja-pot ajjābhamuṁ; = evaṁ atikkamitvā
ṭhitabhamuṁ, Ct.).[ajjābhamu]

ajjita, mfn. [pp. of √ajj; sa. arjita], acquired,
gained, Saddh 98 (cf. ajjana). — ajjitabba, mfn. [do.
ger.], Pj I 223,5 (synon, ajjanâraha).
Ajjuka, m. Npr. of a bhikkhu, Vin III 66,25 foll.

ajjaka or ajjuka, n. (or m.) [sa. arjaka, m.],
name of a plant (Ocimum gratissimum), Abh 579
(= sitapaṇṇāsa, sinh, hela-aṅdu); n. ~aṁ, Vin IV
35,9' (-U-; no v. l.; + phaṇijjakaṁ hiriveraṁ =
'agga-bīja') = Sv I 81,21 ' (Ed. -u-, MSS -a-;
= setapaṇṇāsa, nṭ) ≠ Spk II 331,4 (Se ajjakaṁ);
cf. ajjukaṇṇa.ajjaka

ajjukanna, m., name of a certain tree, Ja VI
535,15* (ajjukā ~ā ca, Se; Ee ajjunā °kannā; cf.
Ap 346,3). Cf. Kern p. 68.

Ajjuka-vatthu, n. — Vin III 66,25—67,8; Mp
I 311,15.

ajjuṇho (or ajjaṇho), ind., (only) this day (ɔ:
the rest of the present day-and-night), Vin I 25,19*
(viharemu ~ aggisālamhi); III 220,29 (~ bhante
āgamehi; Sp = bhante ajja ekadivasaṁ amhākaṁ
tiṭṭha, adhivāsehîti attho; Sp-ṭ: ~ ti pāṭhe ajjaṇho
ti pi paṭhanti; Vmv: ajjaṇho = ajja ekadivasaṁ;
cf. also Mogg III 118); Vin IV 80,2. According to Kern
p. 68 haplology for ajja + *juṇho 'this evening', but
more likely representing *adyu (= adya, cf. aparajju,
sajju) + ahnaḥ, cf. ved. idā(nīm) ahnaḥ- Cf. ajj'eka-
divasaṁ and see aṇha ifc.ajjuṇho

ajjuna, m. [sa. arjuna], the tree Terminalia
Arjuna, Abh 562; Ja VI 535,15* (cf. ajjukanna); Ap
328,28; 346,3; 450,20 (split comp.); — °-'rukkha,
m. id., the Bo-tree of Buddha Anomadassi(n), Bv
VIII 23; Ja I 36,6; Dhp-a I 105,25.

Ajjuna, m. Npr. 1. of the seventh son of Deva-
gabbhā, Ja IV 81,7 ≠ Pv-a 93,21; 111,18. — 2. of
the Pāṇḍu-son Arjuna, Ja V 424,20*; 426,10', 31'
(°-kumāra). — 3. of a king of the Kekakā (Arjuna
Kãrtavīrya, Mhbh), Ja V 135,24 (sahassabāhu);
143,12*-27* (≠ Mvu III 368,15*; 369,6*); 145,7' (sa-
hassabāhurājā . . . Mahiṁsakaraṭṭhe); 267,5* (Keka-
kâdhipo sahassabāhu); °-vatthu, n., Ja V 119,15'
(Mvu III 361,4—ll). — 4. of a thera, author of Th 88
(= Ajjuno isi, Uddāna ib.) ≠ Sālapupphadāyaka,
Ap 169,6-19. — 5. of a Buddha, Ap 446,19.

Ajjunapupphiya, m., designation of a thera,
Ap 450,16—451,3 (= Sambhūta, Th-a ad Th 291—
94). Cf. ajjunaṁ pupphaṁ, ib. 450,20.

ajj'-ekadivasaṁ, ind. (= ajja + ekadivasaṁ),
for to-day, only this day, Ps I 161,7; III 412,18. Cf.
ajjuṇho.

ajj'-ekarattiṁ, ind (= ajja 4- ekarattiṁ), for
this one night, Ps I 233,11

ajjeyya, mfn. (grd.), v. r. for ajeyya, Khp VIII 8
(= ajjitabba ajjanâraha Pj, but probably = *a-jyeya
(√jī), cf. sa. (brahma-)jyeya).

ajjha, [adhi + 2a] tends to independence: 1) [cf.
2a Rem. b] in ajjhagata ajjhapatta, °patvā; this and
other phenomena have contributed to the 'new set of
prefixes': acca-(yanti; -bhamuṁ, see ajjăbhamu),
ana-(bhāva), anva-(gū mfn.), antara-(hita, antara-
dhāyati), uda-(patta), nira-(ssajanti), pacca-(niyyāhi,-
cf. pacca-m-etha; PED's paccagū is w. r.), vya-
(mhita, vyasanna). — 2) in agāraṁ ajjha so vasi
('tmesis'), Bv [II 208 III 26 IV 19] V 22 [VI 17]
etc. (in V 22, Bv-a Ce prints agãra-majjhe so vasi,
against metre and CP), quoted Sadd III 132. — [ajjha,
AN I 279,26* (Ck ajjhā) w. r. (?) for addhā (Sc) q. v.].

[ajjhagacchi, Ja V 255,19*, read dīpam so n'
ajjhagā, 'gacchi agati yattha . . ., cf. adhigacchati.]

ajjhagata, pp. of adhigacchati (see ajjha above)
= adhigata (q. v.). Only ifc, v. veda°.

[ajjhagāhayi, (v. l. ajjhagāhāsi), Ja V 255,16*
(samuddaṁ ~, read: samudda-majjhagā 'hãsi, cf.
harati).] Cf. Mvu III 454,2.

ajjhatta, mfn., from ajjhattaṁ, ind. (q. v.),
attracted by nouns in certain formulas: pl ~ā dhammā,
bahiddhā dhammā, ajjhatta-bahiddhā dhammā, Dhs
p. 2,17 (As 46,3 foll.), 1044-46; ~ ā kāmā, Nidd I l,is;
vedanā~ā, Vibh 3,29; acc ~e dhamme, Vibh 327,42
(but bahiddhā dhamme, ib. 328,4); f. sg. sabbā va
paññā siyā ~ā, siyā bahiddhā . . ., Vibh 327,39
(Vibh 3,8); m. sg. vedanākkhandho atthi ~o, atthi
bahiddho . . . Vibh 17,22 (cf. ~aṁ saṁyojanaṁ, ib.
361,14), etc.; Abh 1040 takes ~aṁ as subst, n.,
~aṁ sasantāne visaye gocare. — Ifc. v. ajjhatta°,
gocara°, niyaka°, visaya°

ajjhattaṁ, ind [sa. adhyātmam], within one's
self [the ambiguous yaṁ rūpaṁ . . . ~ vā bahiddhā
vā, etc., gave rise to vedanā ~ā vā bahiddhā vā,
whence "ajjhatta, mfn"; Ct.s often gloss by an adj.,
but Vism 349,22 compares adhitthi (ɔ: sa. adhistri, see
Kāçikā ad Pãṇ II 1,6); gocarajjhatta, etc. are subst.s];
often used as an attribute to a subst, following, cf.
bāhirena nahānena . . . ajjhattaṁ nahānaṁ, SN V
390,21; ~ eva jalayāmi jotiṁ, SN I 169,21* (cf. ib.
27*); + paccattaṁ: MN I 185,16 (Vism 349,19);
Dhs 1044; Vibh 3,30 (cf. also ajjhāgāre). — Selected
passages to show various combinations: A. with verbal
forms: (a) of √ṭhā [sthā] in expressions of repose,
or balance of mind, ~ me cittaṁ ṭhitaṁ susaṇṭhitaṁ,
AN IV 299,22; ṭhito kayo hoti, ṭhitaṁ cittaṁ ~
susanthitaṁ, SN V 74,7; cittaṁ ~ yeva santiṭṭhati,
etc., 'AN I 254,29 (Mp) = II 157,22 (Mp); ~ eva
cittaṁ saṇṭhapemi ... ekodikaromi, MN I 116,14;
III 112,16 (quoted As 46,7); likewise: ~ sampasādanaṁ
cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ, Vin III 4,9 (Sp) = DN I 37,12
(Sv; Vism 156,9) = Dhs 161 (As 169,9) = Pp 59,30,
etc. ≠ Mvu I 228,5 (2nd jhāna); ~ susamāhito, AN
II 29,2l* (Mp); Th 431 (visayajjhatta-°, Th-a); 272
(gocarajjhatta-°, Th-a); — (b) with forms of √sam1
[cam], expressions of peace or tranquillity (cf. ajjhatta-
santi): ~ eva upasame . . . ~ upasantassa, Sn 919;
~ samayaṁ cittaṁ, It 82,7*; ~ vūpasantacitto,
AN IV 437,11; [~ avūpasantaṁ hoti, AN I 79,31
scil. taṁ adhikaranaṁ?]; ~ cetosamatham anuyutto,
MN I 33,10 (Ps) = AN V 133,2 (Mp) ≠ It 39,10;
nânuyuñjati ~ cetosamathaṁ, AN III 86,30 (Mp);
lābhī ~ cetosamathassa, AN II 92,14 ≠ IV 360,4;
— (c) with katḥaṁkathī, expressing 'doubt': MN
1 8,13 (Ps); SN II 27,5 (Spk); cf. Sn 7 (vitakkā . . .
~ suvikappitā); — (d) with manasi-karoti, ex-
pressing 'reflection, consideration': itthī ~ itthin-
driyaṁ manasikaroti, AN IV 57,5; ~ suññataṁ m°,
MN III II 2,1 (cf. ~ suññataṁ upasampajja vihari-
tuṁ, MN III 111,7, quoted As 46,14); — (e) with
upaṭṭhapeti, expressing 'carefulness, attention': pañca
dhamme . . . ~ upaṭṭhapetvā, AN V 79,9; maraṇa-
saññā ~ sñpaṭṭhitā, AN II 156,1; ānâpāna-sati ~
parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā, It 80,12; kãyagatāya satiyā
~ sūpa[ti]ṭṭhitāya, Ud 28,3 (Ud-a); pañcasu dham-
mesu ~ sati upaṭṭhapetabbā, AN V 335,30; cf.
~ payuttassa, Ja V 121,15*; — (f) with uppajjati,
atthi, etc. = something is met with: kati . . . purisassa
dhammā ~ uppajjamānā, SN I 70,21 (Spk); kāye
sati kāya-sañcetanā-hetu uppajjati~sukha-dukkhaṁ,
SN II 40,1 = AN II 158,1; yā kāci taṇhā ~, Sn 916;
~ kāmacchando, SN V 110,4; atthi me ~ (on my
body) aṅganan ti, MN I 24,18; atthi me ~ kãma-
cchando ti, AN I 272,16; atthi me ~ rāga-dosa-moho
ti, SN IV 139,14; ~ cakkhuṁ suññaṁ, Paṭis II 181,4;
~ dhamme vavattheti, Palis I 76,15; — (g) with
paṭisaṁvedeti, expressing 'enjoyment': ~ anavajja-
sukhaṁ (avyāseka-sukhaṁ) p°, DN I 70,5 (22) (Sv)
— MN I 180,26 = 269,1 = 346,10 = AN II 210,4
≠ DN I 70,22. — B. Next to instances like AN V
79,9-10 (pañca dhamme ~ paccavekkhitvā . . . paro
codetabbo) & AN II 92,14 (ajjhattaṁ : adhipaññā),
ajjhattaṁ stands opposed to bahiddhā (see also
ajjhatta, mfn.): [in āryā]: ~ athavā pi bahiddhā,
Sn 917; [in vaitālīya]: ~ bahiddhā ca, Sn 516—532;
[in çloka]: ~ ca bahiddhā ca, Sn 203; 738 (= SN IV
205,3*); Sn 1111; 1113; Th 172; 439; [triṣṭubh-stple]:
ajjhatta-cintī na mano bahiddhā nicchãraye, Sn 388,
and the like; —- more elaborate antitheta: ~ ca na
jānāti (ca pajānāti) bahiddhā ca na passati (ca
vipassati), AN II 71,18* (22*) = Th 470 (472);
~ saṁkhittaṁ . . . bahiddhā vikkhittaṁ, AN IV
32,21; SN V 263,21, cf. It 94,2; ~ rūpasaññī bahiddhā
rūpāni passati, AN I 40,11 (Mp); IV 305,9 = V 61,5;
MN II 12,32; DN II 110,7 (Sv). = III 260,8 (the
eight abhibhāyatanāni), cf. Vibh 342,33; ~ dhammesu
sati . . . bahiddhā dhammesu sati, Vibh 228,2; vivā-
damūlaṁ ~ vā bahiddhā vā, AN III 334,22 ; ~ vā
kāye kāyânupassī viharati bahiddhā vā . ., MN I
56,27; ~ vā dhammesu dhammânupassī . . ., ib.
60,28 (quoted As 46,10); SN V 143,14; 297,β; DN II
292,1 foll.; Vibh 193,3 (the four satipaṭṭhānāni); yaṁ
kiñci rūpaṁ ~ vā bahiddhā vā . . ., AN I 284,25
= II 171,12 = MN I 138,37 = 234,34 = 421,4 =
III 16,33 = SN II 252,19 = III 47,13 = IV 382,28;
Vibh 1,4.

ajjhatta(ṁ)-vimokkha, m., personal emanci-
pation, SN II 54,1 (abl. ~ā; = ajjhatta-saṁkhāre
pariggahetvā patta-arahattena . . ., Spk II 82,3—
83,18).ajjhatta-vimokkha

ajjhatta-cinti(n), mfn., having his thought oc-

ajjhatta-cinti(n), mfn., having his thought oc-
cupied with internal things, m. ~ī, Sn 174 (Pj: niya-
kajjhatta-cintana-sīlo); 388.ajjhatta-cinti

ajjhatt--ajjhatta, mfn., personal, in the strict

ajjhatta-ttika, n., the triplet beginning with
ajjhatta, = Dhs p. 2,17-18 (As 46,1-22) ≠ Tikap
335,28; Nidd-a ll 6,19 (ad Nidd II,is).

ajjhatta-pucchā, f., the question or theme of
'ajjhatta', Nidd I 340,27 (+ bahiddhā-p°, ajjhatta-
bahiddhā-p°).

ajjhatta-bahiddha, mfn. (cf. next, & ajjhatta,
mfn.), (partly) internal and (partly) external, Vibh
17,24; 327,40. — °-ā, ind., MN I 56,29 (Ps I
249,24); III 112,8; SN V 297,9; 315,4 (Spk); Vibh
193,5; 194,11 (Vibh-a 260,32); DN II 292,2 (Sv). —
°-ârammaṇa, mfn. (see ajjhattârammaṇa below), Dhs
p. 2,20; 1049; Vibh 328,7; Vism 430,1 . . . 435,8; —
°-pucchā, f., Nidd I 340,28 (ajjhatta-pucchā +,
q. v.). — °-rūpa, n., Vin III 112,31'; 113,9' (see
ajjhatta-rūpa). — °-vatthuka, mfn., having both an
internal and an external base, As 191,8 (°-esu kasiṇesu).

ajjhatta-bāhira, mfn. = ajjhatta-bahiddha
(dvandva), in the uddāna SN IV 6,22* (tayo ~ā, scil.
aniccaṁ dukkhaṁ anattā ca).

ajjhatta-bhātika, m., one's own brother, a full
brother, Mp I 226,14 (Se; Ce ajjhattika-bhātiko, see
ajjhattika (c)).

ajjhatta-rata, mfn., 'delighting in one's own self
i. e. in the practise of meditative exercise, ~o samāhíto,
Ud 64,30* ( = niyakajjhatta-rato, Ud-a) — DN II
107,5* (- do., Sv) = SN V 263,3* (= do., Spk)
= AN IV 312,3* (= do., Mp) (quoted Nett 60,32
(Nett-a), As 46,8); Dhp 362 (= gocarajjhatta-saṁ-
khātāya kammatthānabhāvanāya rato, Dhp-a) ≠ Th
981 (= do., Th-a).

ajjhatta-rūpa, n., something of one's self, Vin
III 112,31' (= ajjhattaṁ upādinna-rūpa, ib. 113,7',
Sp); Ps I 219,24.

ajjhatta-vavatthāna, n., analysis of internal
factors, Paṭis I 76,13 (~e paññā).

ajjhatta(ṁ)-vimokkha, m., personal emanci-
pation, SN II 54,1 (abl. ~ā; = ajjhatta-saṁkhāre
pariggahetvā patta-arahattena . . ., Spk II 82,3—
83,18).ajjhatta-vimokkha

ajjhatta-vuṭṭhāna, m. (gender attraction), (being)

ajjhatta-saṁyojana, mfn., having fetters within
one's self, AN I 63,22 (~aṁ puggaiaṁ; Mp: ajjhatta-
saṁyojanena payutto puggalo); Pp 22,11 (= ajjhatta-
bandhano, Pp-a); — n., internal fetters,Vibh 361,15 (Ed.
ajjhattaṁ s°; Vibh-a 495,9: ajjhatta-saṁkhāte kāma-
bhave bandhanaṁ); Mp II 45,10 (= ajjhatta-saṁ-
khãte kāmabhave chandarāgo).

ajjhatta-santi, f., inner peace, Sn 837—38
(= nibbāna, Pj; cf. Nidd I 185,1 (Nidd-a)).

[ajjhatta-sambhava, mfn., id., Th 1126 (~ o,
a doubtful reading; metre requires - - ˇ - - ˇ ].

ajjhatta-samuṭṭhāna, mfn., originating from
within, f. ~ā (hirī), Ja I 207,17 (opp. bahiddhā-
samuṭṭhānaṁ ottappaṁ) ≠ Ps II 422,20; Sv ad DN
I 204,10 (do. scil. rogo).

ajjhatta-suñña, n., the personal void (unsub-
stantial), Patis II 181,3 (cakkhuṁ, etc.).

ajjhattârammaṇa, mfn., taking something in-
terior (personal) for its object, Dhs p. 2,19; 1047
(~ā dhammā); Vibh 63,16 (cattāro khandhā ~ā);
327,41 (~ā paññā + bahiddhârammaṇā p°, ajjhatta-
bahiddhârammaṇā p°). — °-ttika, n., Tikap 335,30
(cf. Dhs p. 2,19-20).

ajjhattika, mfn. [from ajjhattaṁ, q. v.; sa. ādhyāt-
mika], 'belonging to one's self (opp. bāhira), Vism
450,26 (cakkhādi-pañcavidhaṁ attabhāvaṁ adhikicca
pavattattā ~aṁ); SN I 73,2 (bāhirā h'esā rakkhā,
n'esā rakkhā ~ā): (a) belonging to the body or indivi-
duality: ~assā upādāya, AN II 212,9 = Vibh 392,20
(= ~aṁ khandha-pañcakaṁ upādāya, Mp, Vibh-a;
quoted Ps I 219,27); tayo khandhā bāhirā, viññāṇa-
kkhandho ~o, Vibh 67,24; rūpaṁ ~aṁ, Vibh 13,12;
Dhs 673; 751; — paṭhavī-dhātu siyā ~ā siyā bāhirā,
MN I 185,14-22 (quoted Vism 348,3l); 421,33 = AN
II 164,28 (+ āpodhātu, etc.; Mp); Vibh 82,5; dvādasa
dhātuyo ~ā, Vibh 96,13; — cha ~āni āyatanāni
(ɔ: cakkhāyatanaṁ . . . manāyatanaṁ, opp. cha
bāhirāni ā° ɔ: rūpâyatanaṁ . . . dhammâyatanaṁ),
MN III 216,9; Khp IV 6 (quoted As 46,12); DN III
243,14 (Sv); AN V 52,31; MN III 32,3; châyatanā
~ā, châyatanā bāhirā, Vibh 79,27; their assāda: SN
IV 7,2 foll. (Spk); they are dukkhaṁ ariyasaccaṁ,
SN V 426,8 (cf. Vibh 119,25); they are styled piyarūpa-
sātarūpaṁ, It 114,12 (It-a), αndvaṇo, MN II 260,15,
eko anto, AN III 400,25;— pañcannaṁ viññāṇānaṁ
vatthū ~ã, Vibh 319,25; — ~aṁ cakkhuṁ apari-
bhinnaṁ hoti . . ., MN I 190,20 foll.; cha indriyã
~ā, Vibh 131,41; — ~ā dhammã, Dhs p. 5,24;
1530; ~o lobhacoro, Dhp-a l 312,10 (Ed. ajjhan-
tiko); — n. — cittaṁ, Nidd I 346,24. — (b) inte-
grant, indispensable, in ~aṁ aṅgaṁ (conditio sine qua
non): It 9,13; SN V 101,17; AN I 16,23 (Mp: niya-
kajjhattavasena). — (c) belonging to one's own house
or relationship, ~aṁ janaṁ, Ja III 402,21'; ~o
ekapitaro, Ja VI 446,2'; (cf. ajjhatta-bhātika, aj-
jhattika-saṅgaha). — — °-kammaṭṭhāna, n., one's
own (special) spiritual exercise, Dhp-a I 375,14 (~aṁ
sammasanto); II 226,18 (do.). —- °-karaṇa, n., a
personal instrument (e. g. the eye), Clough, Pali
Gr. p. 133,21, cf. Sadd III 552; Rūp 287b. — °-dāna,
n., a gift of something of one's self (one's own body),
Ja IV 402,11. — °-duka, n., a chapter of Dukap,
Tikap 337,9. — °-bāhira, mfn., — ajjhatta-bāhira,
MN I 61,12 (Ps); III 32,28; 63,1s; Dhp-a I 158,24;
Mil 69,2; Nett 191,17 (Nett-a); Vism 368,25. —
°-vatthu, n., an object forming part of one's self

307,16; 319,24 (scil. viññāṇa). — °-vera, n., enmity

ajjhatta-vera, ib. &). — °-saṁgaha, m., kindliness

— °-santati, f., personal subsistence, Ps I 209,8. —
[°-sutta, n., = SN III 180—1.]

e. g. vyākaraṇaṁ adhīte). Cf. ajjhāyati & 1ajjheti,
adhīyati (adhīte).

ajjhavodahi, aor. 3 sg. [ajjha (q. v.) + -v-odahi,
cf. odahati; or perhaps blending of ajjh-odahi and
*ajjh-ava-dahi, cf. anavosita, nirassajanti]; pañjare ~,
he put (them) into the cage, Ja V 365,29* (= odahi
ṭhapesi).

ajjh-°, prp. = adhi (this often takes the place
of sa. abhi) before vowels, Kacc 45; Sadd III 58.

1ajjhā (or acchā), f. = ajana (q. v.), Kacc-v 640
(from √aj); Sadd III 1259.

2ajjhā, in yāvat-ajjhā-vinīta, (v. r. to yāvatā ca
vi°) AN I 285,33, prob, represents ajjhāya, as aññā
for aññāya in sammad-aññā-vimutta and pariyā for
pariyāya in pariyāgata, sajjhā for sajjhāya in sajjhā-
magga (Ai Gr I § 241, b).

ajjh-āgāre, ind. [loc. of adhi + ăgāra; as to
'governing prepositions' see (besides cases reported
under agga-, anto-, bahi-, pāra-, cf. Schubring ad
Kalpasūtra I 11 p. 37) (a) loc.: ajjhācāre ajjhājīve
ajjhārāme ajjhokāse, adhi-citte (adhi-cetasi, JAs
1912,243) adhi-sīle adhi-paññãya adhi-pātimokkhe,
abhi-dhamme abhi-vinaye; (b) acc. m.: adhi-Brah-
mãnaṁ, pl. adhi-deve; (c) acc. n. (as in sa.): ajjh-
! attaṁ ajjh-āsayaṁ adhi-cittaṁ adhi-jegucchaṁ adhi-
paññaṁ adhi-vimutti adhi-sīlaṁ, abhi-dassanaṁ
(Ja VI 193,22*), abbh-atthaṁ, — hence comp, nouns
as ajjhokāsa-gata ajjhiṇa-mutta adhisīla-sikkhā abhi-
dhamma-kathā (paron, in MN I 214,24, etc.) adhi-
deva-ñāṇa-dassana, and secondary nouns as abhi-
dhamma (abbhokāsa); Ct.s (see also Nidd on adhi-
deve, Sn 1148, and cf. abhivinayo . . . adhipātimok-
khaṁ, Vin V 1,17-18) mostly: "adhisīlaṁ = uttama-
sīlaṁ", and the like, Sv ad DN I 174,15], at home,
AN I 132,2 (= sake ghare, Mp) = II 70,14 = II
109,21 (It-a = do.).

ajjhācarati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. adhy-ā + √car], 1. to
practise (something bad), commit (acc.), AN IV 270,1i
(yaṁ bhattu amanāpa-saṁkhātaṁ, opp. bhattu
manāpaṁ carati); As 89,24 (dussīlyaṁ); inf. ~ituṁ,
Vin II 301,6; DN III 133,13 (nava ṭhānāni); MN I
523,4 (pañca ṭhānāni) ≠ AN IV 370,2 (= pañca
kāraṇāni atikkamituṁ, Mp); Mil 266,31 (yaṁ kilesaṁ
lokavajjaṁ); pp. ajjhāciṇṇa, grd. ajjhācariya (ajjhā-
caraṇīya) q. v. — 2. to have intercourse with, aor. 3
pl. ~iṁsu, Ja IV 231,18 (aññamaññaṁ; cf. ajjhācāra).

ajjhācariya, grd. of prec; °-vatthu, n., object
of offence, Pj I 31,1i (v. l. ajjhācaraṇīya-v°, ib. Ap-
pendix Pj II 866).

ajjhācāra, m. (cf. ajjhācarati), transgression, fault,
Abh 430 (= vītikkama); kāyika-vācasika-°, Sp I 19,1
(= saññamavelaṁ abhibhavitvā pavatto ācāro ~
vītikkamo, Sp-ṭ); esp. in an erotica! sense, Vin III
121,8' (= 'kāya-saṁsagga', Sp ad Vin III 120,34**,
Sp-ṭ); 128,35' (explaining 'obhāseyya'; Sp); Mil 127,20;
Sp I 216,8 (°-malinatta, n., q.v.);Ja I 396,4; V 429,22
[in Ja V 318,18* w. r. for ajjhãvara, q. v.; in Sv III
129,15 read with pt: tasmiṁ anajjhācāro acalo].
[Nett-a reads ajjhācāro for sampādanaṁ, Nett 44,18
and explains adhiṭṭhahitvā ācaraṇaṁ, thus making
it a counterpart to an-ajjhācāro, Nett 44,15.] — Ifc.
v. an-°, punappuna°, vatthu°, sulabha°.

ajjhācāre, ind. [loc. see under ajjhāgāre], in
matter of conduct; adhisīle sīlavipanno ~ ācāravipanno,
atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno, Vin I 63,33 (Sp); 67,9;
114,25,36 (Vjb Sp-ṭ ad Vin II 3,8; in atidiṭṭhiyā
ati- for adhi- may be due to the later analysis referred
to s. v. ajjhāgāre, cf. ajjhāsayaṁ ādibrahmacariyaṁ;
according to Sp adhisīle here means 'as to Pārājikā
and Saṁghādisesā', while ajjhācāre is 'as to the other
five āpattikkhandhā').

ajjhāciṇṇa, mfn. (pp. of ajjhācarati), practised,
accustomed, committed; bahuṁ assāmaṇakaṁ ~aṁ,
Vin II 80,34; MN II 248,15; 250,3 foll'.; idaṁ me
upajjhāyena ~aṁ, Vin II 301,5; vasalavādo dīgharat-
taṁ ~o, Ud 29,1 (v. r. for samudāciṇṇo, Ud-a 194,13).

ajjhājīve, ind. (adhi + ājīva, loc; see under
ajjhāgāre), with regard to the rigours of the regimen;
~vā adhipātimokkhe vā, MN II 245,17 (= ājīva-
hetu, ājīvakāraṇā, Ps).

ajjhāpajjati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ā + k'pad), 'to go
too far', incur, commit (an offence), As 219,6; part.
~anto, Vin III 164,16' foll, (pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ);
f. ~antī, Vin IV 237,13' (saṁghādisesaṁ); inf. ~ituṁ,
As 219,7; pp. ajjhāpanna, q. v.

1ajjhāpana, n. (from caus. of adhi + √i), teaching,
instruction, Mil 225,31. Cf. ajjheti (ajjhāyati),
adhīyati.

2a-jjhāpana, n. (cf. jhāpeti), not burning, not
scorching, Ja VI 311,7' (allahatthassa, q. v.).

ajjhāpanna, mfn. (pp. of ajjhāpajjati, very often
confounded with ajjhopanna, q. v.), 1. (in an active
sense, with acc) who has committed (some offence);
garudhammaṁ ~, Vin II 255,17 = AN IV 277,6; Vin
III 164,17'; Mil 255,1 (pārājikaṁ); — 2. (in a passive
sense), which has been committed, Vin I 103,37' (āpatti),
[the v. l. ajjhāpanno Ud 35,24 is unknown to Ud-a
and Mp-ṭ ad AN IV 356,1s]. — Ifc. v. an-°, ñatta°.

ajjhāpannaka, mfn. = ajjhāpanna (1); antima-
vatthuṁ ~o, Vin I 121,2 = 135,29 = II 173,18
(sikkhaṁ paccakkhātako ~ ummattako).

(ajjhāpekkhati) pr. 3 sg. [ajjha + apekkhati,
q. v.], to abandon, neglect (?); aor. 3 pl. ~ irhsu (yena
kiccena sampattã), Ap 181,13 (or w. r. for ajjhupek-
khiṁsu?).

ajjhābhava, m. (from next), intercourse, contact
with (gen.), Ja II 357,6*,15'.

ajjhābhavati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ā + √bhū), to have
to do with (acc), Ja II 357,16' (where Ct. takes it =
abhibhavati, but see Kern p. 67).

ajjhāya, m. [sa. adhyāya], a chapter or section
of a book, Abh 911 (= 'sagga'). — Ifc. (a reader,
student) v. manta° & cf. 2ajjhā.

ajjhāyaka, m. (from ajjhāyati, cf. sa. ādhyāyika,
adhyāyin), one who studies (the Vedas), skilled in the
Vedas, a brahmanical teacher, DN I 88,4 (mãṇavo ante-
vāsī . . . ~o + mantadharo tinnaṁ vedãnaṁ pāragū,
etc.; Sv); 121,1 (+ do.); 130,'u (do.); AN I 163,10
(do.; Mp); 166,18 (do.); III 223,17 (do.); Th 1171
(tiṇṇaṁ vedāna pāragū); Bv II 6 (+ mantadharo,
etc; quoted Ja I 3,17*); Ap 24,12; Ja VI 199,27* (~o
yācayogo āhutaggi ca brāhmaṇo); 201,27* (~ānaṁ);
204,31* (~aṁ mantaguṇūpapannaṁ); 498,22* (dāna-
patiṁ yācayogaṁ amacchariṁ); MN II 154,4 (+ upa-
nīto); DN III 94,24 (taken as a + jjhāyaka); Sn 140
(v. r.). — Ifc. v. an-°, manta°.

ajjhāyaka-kula, n., a family of Veda teachers,
Sn 140 (~e jātā brāhmanā; v. r. ajjhāyakā kule jātā,
Pj II 192,2).

ajjhāyati, pr. 3 sg. (prob, denom, from ajjhāya
[sa. adhyāya], cf. sajjhāyati), to study, learn by heart;
Sv I 247,16; Sadd II 13, 242. — Cf. ajjheti, adhīyati
ḷ (adhīte).

ajjhāyana, n. = ajjhayana; Rūp Ce p. 86,15
Dhātum 759 (v. l.); Sadd II 1343. — Ifc. v. eka°,
veda°.

ajjhārāme, ind. (adhi + ārāme, loc; see ajjhā-
gāre), within the ārāma (q. v.), Vin I 187,31; III
239,7'; IV 182,16**.

ajjhārūha, m(fri), which grows in and up over
(sometimes spelt ajjhāruha); (a) parasite (on, with
gen.): mahārukkhā . . . rukkhānaṁ ~ā, SN V 96,8
(scil. assāttho, nigrodho, etc. ≠ Ja III 398,27* foll.;
= abhiruhanaka, Spk); Ja III 399,14; — (b) metaph.:
āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso ~ā, SN V 96,21—97,1 (scil.
kāmacchando vyāpādo, etc.) = AN III 63,12 ( =
cetaso ajjhārūḷhā, Mp), quoted As 382,22 (Ed. ajjho-
rohā i. e. ajjhārohā; cittaṁ abhibhavantā ārohantī
ti cetaso ajjhārohā, mṭ). Cf. Amg. ajjhāroha.

ajjhārūhati [adhi-ā + √ruh] 1. to grow in and
up over (as a parasite plant splitting and choking
a tree, see Ja III 208,18 foll, 398,4 foll), found in
the pp. ajjhārūḷha q. v.; — 2. to tyrannize, to bully,
SN I 221,34* (v. l. ajjhoruhati; = ajjhottharati, Spk)
= 223,19*, quoted Nett 173,3*.

ajjhārūḷha [pp. of ajjhārūhati q. v.], (a) in a
passive sense: yehi (scil. ajjhārūhehi) ~ā rukkhā
obhaggobhaggā vipatitā senti, SN V 96,7; — (b) in
an active sense: ~âbhivaḍḍhanti brahantam pi vanas-
patiṁ, Ja III 399,3* (scil. ajjhārūhā rukkhā, ib. 14'),
cf. Mp ad AN III 63,12. — Ifc. v. an°.

Ajjhāroha, m. Npr. of a mythical fish, Abh 673;
Ja V 462,17 (so Ja-pot; Ee Ajjhohāro, Ck Ajjhāro,
Cs Ajjhoro).

ajjhāvara, m., companion, company, retinue,
train, Ja V 318,18* (Ee here ajjhācāra); 322,23*;
324,7*; 326,3*; 327,29* (Ct. always = parisā; [perhaps
it ought to be corrected into ajjhācara, representing
*abhi-ā-cara]).

ajjhāvasati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. adhi-ā + √vas], to
inhabit (as a ruler), to dwell in (as an owner) (acc);
to hold (a position); to lead or enjoy a certain mode
of life (very often with the object agāraṁ, acc, a house-
hold life): Sn 1002 (Pj) ≠ DN II 16,13; AN V 288,2;
Vin IV 224,31'; Sn p. 106,10-18 (imaṁ paṭhaviṁ);
It 75,23 (saṁgāmasīsaṁ abhivijiya ~); AN I 106,30
(saṁgãmasīsaṁ ~; = abhibhàvitvā [ā]vasati, Mp);
— 2 sg. ~asi: MN II 71,21 (phītaṁ Kuruṁ); — 1 sg.
~ãmi, MN II 71,23 (do.); DN I 134,27 (paṭhavi-maṇḍa-
laṁ abhivijiya); Mil 88,15 (agāraṁ); — part. m. ~anto,
MN I 515,28 (putta[dāra]sambãdha-sayanaṁ); Mil
243,4; 348,13 (do.); AN III 302,18 (mahantaṁ bho-
gakkhandhaṁ); instr, sg. ~atā, DN I 63,4 = MN II
55,28 = Pp 57,13 (Ed. °~ato); instr, pl. ~antehi, Dhp-a
I 6,25 (gehaṁ); gen. pl. ~ataṁ, AN I 49,15; part. med.
m. ~amāno, Ja I 56,10; — pot. 1 pl. ~eyyāma, MN II
72,1 (taṁ abhivijiya); —- aor. 3 sg. ~vasi, Ja I 145,27;
V 177,13 (taṁ, scil. nagaraṁ); 3 pl. ~vasiṁsu, ib.
31.2,9' (phītaṁ dharaṇiṁ; = 'āvasuṁ'); fut. 3 sg.
~vasissati, Ap 94,6; — abs. ~itvā, DN III 76,24
(= tattha vasitvā, Sv); — pp. ajjhāvuttha (q. v.).

ajjhāvasathe, ind. (adhi + āvasathe, loc cf.
ajjhāgãre), in a house, Vin III 239,7' (opp. ajjhārāme).

ajjhāvuttha, mfn. (pp. of prec), inhabited,
occupied, Vin II 21.0,32; SN II 106,1; Ja II 333,20
(pāsādo; cf. °-pāsādo, ib. 4); Pv-a 24,21 (sāmibhāvena
°-gharaṁ); Ja VI 95,19 (°-pubbo, scil. bhūmippadeso,
inhabited before). — Ifc v. an-°.

ajjhāsate, pr. 3 sg. med. [sa. adhi + √ās], to sit
upon, Mogg-v II 2 (with acc rukkhaṁ).

2ajjhāsaya, m. (from adhi-ā + √çi, cf. āsaya
[as to adhi- cf. adhimutti, adhippāya]), orig, meaning
'place, seat, domicile, receptacle' (cf. sa. pakvāçaya,
āmāçaya), hence esp. (a) said of the mind as a
store of dispositions, i. e. the mental disposition (of
the hearer): Dhp-a I 6,6 (°-vasena, scil. Buddha
dhammaṁ desenti), cf. III 216,2; Ja I 88,17 (tesaṁ
~aṁ oloketvā); Dhp-a III 217,9 = IV 202,1l (tassa
~aṁ viditvā); Dhp-a I 249,2 (tassa ~aṁ ajānanto);
II 139,21 (nâhaṁ puttassa ~aṁ bhindissāmi); III
95,15 (do.); Ps I 15,26; II 343,16; III 484,11; Spk
II 167,10; Mp II 318,9 (ad AN I 285,33); — (b)
inclination, intention, aspiration, wish: Abh 766; Ja
IV 266,29 (Satthu ~aṁ gaṇhituṁ) ≠ Dhp-a III
228,13, cf. Ps II 346,1s; Ja V 382,19 (Bodhisattass'
ev' assa ~o); VI 222,29 ' (eso mam' ~o); As 314,19
(~aṁ karoti, to entertain a wish for); 334,24 (abl.
~ato); Pv-a 88,7; 168,4; cha ~ā, Vism 116,22 (alo-
bha° + )..—- Ifc. v. atta°, adāna°, adosa°, aneka°,
amoha°, alobha°, ahita°, ākāsa°, upādinnaka°,
uḷāra°, eka°, evam-°, kalyāṇa°, gāma°, jhāna°,
dāna°, nāna°, nissaraṇa°, nekkhamma°, paṇīta°,
para°, paviveka°, puggala°, purisa°, maha°,
yathā°, (yuddhā°?), visama°, veneyya°, hita°,
hīna°.

1ajjhāsaya, mfn. (cf. next), inhabiting, resorting
to; ifc. v. arañña°, bila°.

ajjhāsayaṁ, ind. (cf. prec & ajjhāgāre), as to
the state of mind; DN II 224,9 foll. (~ ādibrahma-
cariyaṁ, q. v., i. e. ajjh-(āsayaṁ + ādibrahma-
cariyaṁ) if ādibrahm° does not stand for adhi-brahm°,
see note on atidiṭṭhiyā s. v. ajjhācāre; Sv = uttama-
nissaya-bhūtaṁ); III 39,14—40,5 (do.).

ajjhāsaya-gahaṇa, n., Ja II 352,17 (sabbesam
°~gahaṇatthaṁ, in order to have the assent of the
assembly).

ajjhāsaya-dhātu, f., the element 'mental dis-
position', Spk II 1.74,18 (ad SN II 153,24: 'dhātuṁ
paṭicca uppajjati saññā' = ajjhāsayaṁ paṭicca saññā
uppajjati; cf. SN II 154,20-21 (Spk)).

ajjhāsaya-pūraṇa, mfn., fulfilling one's desire,
Ja VI 15,34'; 528,17' (both in connection with puṇṇa-
patta).

ajjhāsaya-phala, n., reaping of one's desire,
Ja VI 16,18'.

ajjhāsaya-sampanna, mfn., with the right
(friendly, liberal) intentions, Dhp-a III 97,9 (Rt
sædāT-æti); Pv-a 116,10.

ajjhāsayânurūpa, mfn., 1. according to one's
mental dispositions, Pv-a 61,4 (°-kammaṭṭhāna);
106,11; 128,4. —- 2. according to one's wish, Ja III
437,19; VI 301,31' (tava ~aṁ karoma = 'yathā-
matiṁ').

ajjhāsayânusandhi, m., that form of sequence
between the dhammakkhandhā in a sutta which
is commanded by the hearer's mental disposition:
pucchânusandhi + ~ + yathânusandḥi, Sv I 122,22
—123,10 (giving as an instance MN III 19,10-23 );
Ps 12,25; this anusandhi does not occur in Ud,
Ud-a 4,30.

ajjhāsita, mfn. (pp. of adhi-ā + √çi, cf. ajjhā-
saya), intent upon; ifc. v. jhāna°, brāhmaṇattha°.
— ajjhāsitatta, mfn., whose mind (attā) is set upon;
ifc. v. vimutti-°.

ajjhiṭṭha, mfn. (pp. of ajjhesati, cf. ajjhesita),
asked, requested (to preach the dhamma, or to give a
sentence (as a judged)); Sn p. 218,13 (= yācito, Pj);
DN II 289,2 (°-pañhā, w, r. ~ā pañhā; = ajjhesita-
pañhā puṭṭha-pañhā, Sv); Sp I 103,3; Ud-a 310,36
≠ Dhp-a IV 101,22 (v. l. abhijjhittha, cf. samijjhit-
ṭha, Ja VI 12.25*); — Ja VI 292,28* (= āṇatta). —
Ifc. v. an-°. See also sam-ajjhiṭṭha.

ajjh-iṇa-mutta, mfn. (i. e. adhi-iṇa-mutta), free
with regard to debt, Kacc-v 46; Sadd III 59.

[ajjhupagacchati], pr. 3 sg. (adhi-upa + √gam,
cf. sa. abhyupagam°), 'to enter, arrive to', to assent,
agree to (an opinion, view, and submit to the con-
sequences); pot. 3 sg. "gacche, Thī474 (= sampa-
ṭiccheyya, Thī-a); aor. 3 sg. ajjhupāgami, Ja II 403,3*
(saṁyamaṁ); VI 129,8* (do.); 3 pl. °āgamuṁ, Ja V
323,10* (with gen. isīnaṁ [or read isinaṁ, acc. sg.?]
= isīnaṁ santikaṁ upagatā, Ct.); pp. v. next.

ajjhupagata, mfn. (pp. of prec. also ajjhūpagata,
Vv 151, cf. majjhūpagata; another rythmic variant is
ajjhupagata (q. v.) justified by taking ajjhupāgami
as from adhi-upa-ã + √gam, cf. (secondary) sa.
abhyupāgata and see ajjhupeti), who has attained
to, entered upon, agreed to; resorting to, dependent of;
Th 587 (in āryā: - ˇ ˇ ˇ ≃ ; sāmaññaṁ); vevaṇ-
ṇiy[am] amhi ~o, AN V 87,31; 210,9 (cf. parapiṇ-
ḍaṁ ~o, Mil 243,9); tad eva . . . allīno, tad eva . . .
~o, AN V 187,7; ~o kapiniddaṁ, Mil 300,31; seṭṭhiṭ-
ṭhānaṁ ~o, ib. 291,10.

ajjhupagata, mfn., = ajjhupagata. Th 1109
(in jagatī); Ap 47,1; 322,14 (in çloka).

ajjhupagamana, n. (cf. sa. abhyupagamana),
acceptance, assenting to, Vin II 97,34; 104,5 (upaga-
manaṁ + ~aṁ adhivāsanā apaṭikkosanā).

[ajjhupaharati], pr. 3 sg. [adhi-upa + √hṛ],
to eat; only aor. ~āhari, Ja II 293,13* (bhojanaṁ;
= ajjhohari, Ct.).

ajjhupāvekkhi, aor. [of adhi-upa + √viç, to
sit down], Ja V 377,5* (thus Tr. for ajja pāvekkhi,
Mss. & Ed.).

ajjhupekkhaka, mfn. (cf. next & upekkhaka),
disinterested, impartial; As 133,22 (ājānīyānaṁ °-sā-
rathi, a charioteer, treating (his horses with imparti-
ality). — abstr. f. ~tā & n. ~tta, As 196,17 (Ed.
ajjhūpekkhākata°) = Vism 321,25.

ajjhupekkhaṇă, f. or n., indifference, disregard,
impartiality; Dhp-a IV 3,18 (adhivāsanaṁ ~aṁ);
Ps I 84,8 (~ato upekkhā); Paṭis I 16,10 (°-aṭṭha);
II 119,22 (do.); Vibh 230,12 foll. (f. ~ā); As 133,21;
— °-tā, f., Ps I 298,30 (impartiality).

ajjhupekkhati, pr. 3 sg. [adhi-upa + √īkṣ], to
look on without interfering, to tolerate, to be indifferent;
~ati, AN I 257,14 (= pakkâpakkabhãvaṁ upadhā-
reti, Mp!); Patis 161,24 (saṁkhāre); 168,6 (visuddhaṁ
cittaṁ); II 24,14; Ja I 147,21; Nidd I 508,12*
(Nidd-a); 2 sg. ~asi, Vin II 78,34 = III 162,14; 3 pl.
~anti, Ss 53,8; 2 pl. ~atha, Ja V 229,5 (tolerate);
part. gen. ~ato, MN II 223,1β; 224,30 (with gen.);
pot. 3 sg. ~eyya, Nidd I 508,22* (Nidd-a); 1 pl.
~eyyāma, MN I 155,25 (= avyāvaṭā bhaveyyāma,
Ps); Dhp-a IV 125,3; aor. 3 sg. ~i, Mil 275,9 (did not
interfere); 3 pl. ~iṁsu, MN I 155,25 (let in peace); fut.
2 pl. ~issatha, AN III 194,22; abs. ~itvā, Bv I 52
(cf. Ap 320,23); grd. ~itabba, AN I 126,8 ≠ Pp 36,23
(~o na sevitabbo); — nomen agentis ~ita(r), m.,
SN V 69,11 ≠ Vibh 227,23 (Vibh-a 313,32); SN V
324,29 = 331,1 = MN III 85,1 (Spk III 383,11 reads
~ito for ~itā); Ps I 82,1; — nomen actionis ~aṇă,
f. or n. (q. v.).

ajjhupeta, mfn. (pp. of next), who has attained
to, Dāṭh IV 5 (saṁyamam; cf. Jail 403,3*).

(ajjhupeti), pr. 3 sg. [adhi-upa + √i, cf. sa.
abhyupa-i° and abhyupâ-i°], to go. to meet; to go to
lie on a place (in one's abode); pot. 1 sg. ~eyyaṁ,
DN III 23,25 (tam eva āsayaṁ; = upagaccheyyaṁ,
Sv); aor. 3 sg. ~esi, ib. 23,34; fut. 1 sg. ~essaṁ, Ja
IV 440,10* foll. (= upăgamissāmi, Ct).

1ajjheti, pr. 3 sg. = ajjhāyati (q. v.); Pj II 447,23
(vyākaraṇaṁ ~ vedeti ca); grd. ~etabba, Pj II 456,21
(abl. ~to, because it must be recited); ~eyya, ajjhā-
yanīya, ajjhayitabba, Kacc-v 637. Cf. adhīyati
(adhīte).

2ajjheti, pr. 3 sg. [sa. adhy-eti, adhi + √i; cf. Pāṇ
113,52 &sa-Dhātup 24,38], to long for, regret; to mourn;
Sn 948 (na so socati nâjjheti; = abhijjhati, Pj; cf.
Nidd I 433,11: na upanijjhāyati na nijjhāyati na
pajjhāyati).

2ajjhena, m(fn), who reads, recites, prob, so
assumed Ja VI 209,27' in the sense of mantajjhāyaka
(read: ajjhena-m-aggin ti ajjhena aggiṁ) but cf.
ajjhena-m-aggiṁ below.

1ajjhena, n. = ajjhayana (q. v.), Dhātup 354
(= √i, cf. Dhātum 580; Sadd II 13); 545 (= √cacc);
MN II 199,17 (~aṁ brāhmaṇā catutthaṁ dhammaṁ
paññāpenti; = manta-gahaṇaṁ, Ps); loc. ~e, MN III
1,12 (Ps); Ja II 327,16* (Ed. ajjhesanaṁ, Cks ajjhena
ca, read ajjhenaṁ ca); VI 201,9* = 207,25* (~aṁ
ariyā . . . upāgu); [VI 207,2* (~am aggiṁ tappayitvā,
see below and 2ajja)]; pl. ~āni patiggayha, Ja V 10,15*
(= vede paṭiggahetvă adhīyitvā, Ct.); Ja III 114,28'
(~ena = 'japena'); Nidd I 80,23 (~ena, = ajjhāyana-
vasena, Nidd-a); Vibh 353,18,34; cf. also ajjhayana,
ajjhāna, pariyajjhena). — Ifc. v. chanda°, jhāna°,
manta°.

ajjhena-kujja, n., futile studies or doctrines,
Sn 242 (v. l. °-kutt(h)aṁ; = niratthaka-anattha-
janaka-gantha-pariyāpuṇanaṁ, with v. l. °-kuṭṭaṁ
(ɔ: °-kūṭaṁ), Pj).

ajjhena-m-aggiṁ, Ja VI 207,2* (prob. w. r.
for ajjena-m-aggiṁ idha tappayitvā, i. e. feeding the
sacred fire with clarified butter (see 2ajja). The blunder
may be due to ajjhenam ariyā, ib. 201,9* and 207,25* ;
Ct. ib. 209,27' is corrupt, see 2ajjhena.

ajjhesati, pr. 3 sg. [adhi + √eṣ]; to ask, request
(mostly: to ask one to preach the dhamma, cf. Sp ad
Vin I 113,5; with acc. of the person or the thing asked
for); ~ati, AN IV 153,8 = 155,3 (sāmaṁ vā dham-
mam bhāsati paraṁ vā ~); 3 pl. ~anti, Vin I
116,25; AN IV 299,15; Dhp-a IV 18,11; 1 pl. ~āma,
MN III 10,13; aor. 3 sg. ajjhesi Vin II 200,10; Ud
59,21 (= āṇāpesi, Ud-a) = Vin I 196,34; 3 pl.
~esiṁsu, Vin I 116,13-16; fut. 3 sg. ~esissati, Mp
I 240,25 (taṁ . . . dhammaṁ ~); inf. ~esituṁ, Vin
I 113,9 (paraṁ); abs. ~esitvā, Ps II 182,9 (dham-
madesanaṁ); pp. v. ajjhiṭṭha & ajjhesita.

ajjhesanā, f. [sa. adhyeṣaṇā], request, sollicitation
(esp. to preach the dhamma); Abh 427 (sakkāra-
pubbaṅgama-niyojanam; cf. Sp-ṭ ad SpI 2,13*:
garuṭṭhānīyaṁ payirupāsetvā garutaraṁ payojanaṁ
uddissa abhipatthanā); Vin I 6,23 (Brahmuno ~aṁ
viditvā) = DN II 38,19 (= yācanaṁ, Sv; cf. Bv I
1-2; II 211) = SN I 138,1 (= do., Spk) = MN I
169,5 ≠ AN II 21,27; Dhp-a I 86,1β (Brahmuno
~aṁ adhivāsetvā); do. (to write a commentary work):
Sp 12,13* (Vjb); Vism 712,2*.

ajjhesita, mfn. (pp. of ajjhesati, cf. ajjhittha),
asked, Nidd II 78,29 (= 'ajjhiṭṭha', Sn p. 218,18);
Pj I 131,27 (ekaṁ ~o pi, appaṁ yācito bahudāyako
uḷãrapuriso viya. . .); do. (to write a ṭīkā, cf. ajjhe-
sanā), Sp-ṭ conclusion v. 3; see also As-mṭ conclusion
v. 2. Cf. also yācita, āyācita, abhiyācita. — Ifc. v.
an-°.

ajjhokāsa-gata, mfn. (see next), abiding in the
open air, SN II 230,20.

ajjhokāse, loc. (adhi + okāsa, [see under
ajjhāgare], — abbhokāse, q. v.), in the open air,
Vin I 15,24; 152,21; SN I 104,2; 112,14; 212,6; III
100,6; Dhp-a III 15,20; IV 101,20 (cf. Ud 59,17); Ja
V 195,5' (opp. udakaṭṭhãne).

ajjhokirati, pr. 3 sg. [adhi-ava + √kf, cf. sa.
abhyava + √kṛ], to strew, sprinkle, throw on, cover,
3 pl. ~anti, DN II 137,21 foll, (okiranti ~ abhippa-
kiranti, scil. Tathãgatassa sarīraṁ; ajjhottharantā
viya kiranti, Sv); fut. 3 sg. ~issati, Anāg 102 (pup-
phāni).

ajjhogāhati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava + √gāh, cf. sa.
abhyava-√gāh), to dive or plunge into, to enter or go
far into; ~ati, DN I 101,5-13 (vanaṁ); Nidd I 152,24
(pagāhati ogāhati ~ati pavisati); Ps III 625,19 =
Pj I 176,14; 2 sg. ~asi, DN I 102,19; 3 pl. ~anti,
DN I 222,25 (samuddaṁ); AN III 368,24; V 133,20;
aor. 1 sg. ajjhogahiṁ, Ap 20,2 [as ārūhati: ãruhi,
āyūhati: āyuhe; cf. sa. gūhati: aguhat]; inf. ~ituṁ,
Ps I 112,14; abs. ajjhogãhitvā (Mss. generally and
Edd. sometimes ajjhogahetvā or °gāhetvā, where -e-
prob. is due to confusion with °ganhati (√grah)): Ap
20,7 [ - - ˇ - ≃ ; Vin I 23,4; III 18,30; DN II 134,21;
173,15; III 62,24; SN III 91,11; AN III 75,20; IV
356,10; MN I 79,1 (cf. note p. 536); 108,18; 147,10;
152,5; 156,21; 229,22; 359,15; 447,21; 501,29; II 8,29;
9,4; Mil 87,10 (cf. note p. 422; quoted As 142,23);
300,27; Ja I 7,4; Dhp-a I 375,1; Pj I 185,29 (ariya-
saccāni paññāya); Ps I 192,19 (nadiṁ vā taḷākaṁ
vā); pp: ajjhogāḷha (q. v.).

ajjhogāḷha, mfn. (pp. of next), who has entered
or dived into, AN IV 100,11 (mahāsamudde) ≠ Sp I
119,12* (mahaṇṇave) = Pj II 442,29*; Mil 348,1*
(dhute guṇe, keeping the dhutaṅgas); Ps III 124,21
(mahāsaraṁ, scil. mahānāvā). — °-ppatta, mfn.
[blending of ajjhapatta and ajjhogāḷha], who has
taken up (his abode) within, SN I 201,17 (aññata-
rasmiṁ kule ativelaṁ ~o; = ogāhapatto, Spk).

ajjhotthaṭa, mfn. (pp. of next, also spelt °tthata),
covered, flooded; overcome, overwhelmed; Pv-a 55,15
(gehena); As 15,4 (Buddha-rasmīhi); Pj II 437,11
(udakena); Dāṭh V,5 (sokena); Ja I 363,17' ('āsīno'
= abhiniviṭṭho ~o); 410,13'; V 91,25' (= 'adhi-
panna'); 379,19' (= do.); Pj I 153,19 (= 'phuṭṭha').
— °-hadaya, mfn., with the heart overwhelmed (by
love, pemena, mahoghenêva), Dhp-a I 278,18.

ajjhottharati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava + √stṛ, some-
times spelt °ottarati as from adhi-ava (or ut-) + √tṛ),
generally meaning 'to cover, to spread over' in various
combinations; thus: (a) to fall and remain lying,
covering something: Ja I 61,20 (turiyāni ~itvā nipaj-
jiṁsu); AN III 92,2 = Pp 67,26 foll, (abhinisīdati
abhinipajjati ~ati; — avattharati, Pp-a); part. pass.
~iyamāna, AN III 92,3 = Pp 67,28; — (b) to flow
over, overspread: Mil 296,14-17 (sadevakaṁ lokaṁ;
dvādasa yojanāni); Sv II 232,9 (expl. 'ajjhokirati');
Ps II 330,9 (Vajjiraṭṭhaṁ); Ja III 289,14 (~itvā);
— (c) to fill (with): Dhp-a I 426,4 (aor. ~ari, nagaraṁ
gandhena; Ed. avatthari); III 30,17 (seṭṭhidhītaraṁ
pubbasineho ~ari); Ja I 330,20 (Ee °ottari); do.
with pass, sense (= was flooded), Vv-a 48,1 (gāma-
padeso); — (d) to cover (with), to spread out: Ps II
563,16 (khip[p]aṁ gahetvā macche ~ante); II 260,11
(pāsa-rāsim ~itvā); III 291,3 (dānaṁ mahantaṁ
~itvā); — (e) to transgress (boundaries): Vin I 111,15
(sīmāya sīmaṁ ~anti, 'to encompass', Trsl; Sp); ib.
20 (pot. ~eyya; grd. ~aritabba); Ps II 215,17 (vatiṁ
ajjhottharantā pavisanti, 'passing over'); — (f) to
overcome, overwhelm: Ja I 410,11' (atibhavati +
~ati — 'ativattati'); Dhp-a I 75,12 (abhibhavati
+ ~ati — 'pasahati'); Mil 338,22 (abhibhavati +
~ati); Spk I 402,12 (= 'ajjhārūhati'); Ja I 163,19'
(= 'atibhoti'; vañcetī ti attho); As 400,18 ('anvā-
ssaveyyuṁ' = anuppabandheyyum + ~eyyuṁ);
Ja I 333,3 (inf. ~ituṁ asakkontā); Ja I 72,5 (part,
med. ~aramānā); 73,4 (udakena naṁ ~itvā, 'to
deluge'); Mil 336,27 (atikkamitvā atisayitvā + ~itvā,
'to surpass').

ajjhottharita(r), m. (nomen agentis from prec):
Kkh (Ce) 5,28 (sīmãya sīmaṁ ~tā; cf. Vin I 111,15).ajjhottharita

ajjhottharita(r), m. (nomen agentis from prec):
Kkh (Ce) 5,28 (sīmãya sīmaṁ ~tā; cf. Vin I 111,15).ajjhottharita

ajjhopanna, mfn. (pp. of adhi-ava + √pad; Amg.
ajjhovavaṇṇa, cf. Vyu 110,6-7 and see adhipanna;
often confounded with ajjhāpanna (q. v.)), addicted to
(loc), mostly in the formula: gathita mucchita +,
DN I 245,25 (kāmaguṇe; Sv, pt; cf. Sv III 28,7 ad
DN III 46,28: ajjhāpanno ti āmise atilaggo) = MN I
173,27 (= taṇhāya ajjhogālhā, Ps); MN I 162,9 (cf.
note p. 543); II 203,16; AN I 74,5 (Mp); 274,20 ( =
taṇhāya gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā pavatto, Mp, Mp-t);
III 68,14 (itthiphoṭṭhabbe rattā +); V 178,6 (ga-
thita +); SN II 270,1 (do.); IV 332,28 (bhoge gathito
mucchito+); Ud 75,10-26 (kāmesu sattā rattā +;
Ud-a); Sv I 59,24 (kāmaguṇesu rattā gathitā muc-
chita +); cf. Nidd I 159,24; II 156 (nissita). — Ifc.
v. an-°.

(ajjhobhavati), pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava + √bhū),
I to overcome; aor. 3 sg. ~bhavi, Ja II 80,16* (taṁ
maṁ paṁko ~ [ - ˇ ˇ ≃ ; thus Bi ajjhabhavi may
be a good conjecture] = adhibhavi, Ct.).

ajjhomaddati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava + √mṛd),
to tread down (upon); AN IV 191,11 = 193,15 (rathī-
saṁ ~, scil. assakhaluṅko; = dvīhi purimapādehi
īsaṁ maddanto tiṭṭhati, Mp).

ajjhomucchita, mfn. (pp. of adhi-ava-√mūrch,
but prob, a blending of adhimucchita and the formula
mucchito ajjhopanno), clinging to (loc.) in longing
or regret; AN III 57,27 (= adhimucchito gilitvā
pariniṭṭhapetvā gahaṇasabhāvāya atirekamucchāya
taṇhāya samannāgato, Mp; see under ajjhosāya).

[ajjhorūlha, mfn., w. r. for ajjhārūḷha (q. v.),
SN V 96,8. — ajjhorūhati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava +
√ruh), w. r. for ajjhārūhati (q. v.), SN I 221,34*. —
ajjhoroha, mfn. = ajjhārůha, As 382,22-25 (v. l.
ajjhārūḷha)].

ajjholambati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava + √lamb),
to hang down on (loc. or acc.); 3 pl. ~anti, MN III
164,28-30 (paṭhaviyā olambanti ~ abhi(ppa)lambanti;
quoted Nett 179,4); Saddh 284, 296 (mānasaṁ); pot.
3 pl. ~eyyuṁ, SN III 137,19 foll. (Spk).

ajjhosāya (and ajjhosa), ind. (abs. of ajjhosati ;
sa. adhyavasāya and adhyavasya), having grasped,
mostly in the phrase ~āya (or ~a) tiṭṭhati, to continue
grasping, SN IV 159,8 (cf. Nett 155,25, Nett-a) ≠
MN I 266,30 = II 265,2 (abhinandati +; = taṇ-
hâjjhosānena gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā gaṇhāti, Ps;
as for gilitvā here and below see SN IV 159,8, cf.
ajjhomucchita); MN I 270,15 (do. with negation:
nâjjhosāya); SN III 14,7 (do., = gilitvā pariniṭṭha-
petvā gaṇhāti, Spk); IV 36,5; 60,15; 79,20 (do.) 71,11*
(nâjjhosāya [ɔ: *ajjhavasāya - ˇ ˇ - ˇ] bhuñjati);
Mil 69,3 (abhinandanti +); Mp II 64,4 (ajjhopannā
ti ~ gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā ṭhitā); an-ajjhosāya
titthato, MN I 270,17; tañ ca ajjhosa tiṭṭhati, SN IV
73,20* = Th 98 (Th-a); 794; nâjjhosa tiṭṭhati, SN
IV 74,23* (= taṁ ārammanaṁ gilitvā, Spk) =
Th 806.ajjhosāya

[*ajjhosati or *ajjhoseti], pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava +
√so; *ajjhosiyati would correspond to sa. adhyavasyati,
and Sadd gives siyati as pr. 3 sg. of √sā antakammani),
to determine (a place), catch, take hold of; to conceive,
ascertain (during meditation); fut. 2 sg. ~issasi, MN
I 328,16 (paṭhaviṁ, etc.; = paṭhaviṁ ajjhosāya
gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā taṇhā-māna-diṭṭhīhi gaṇhis-
sasi, Ps); 1 sg. ~ issāmi, ib. 21; inf. ~ituṁ, MN II
263,8 (abhinandituṁ abhivadituṁ +); abs. (a ) ~itvā,
Ps II 99,7 (v. l. ~etvā); (b) ajjhosāya and ajjhosa
(q. v.); grd. ~itabba, MN I 109,36 (v. l. ~etabba;
abhinanditabba + ; quoted As 5,4); pp. ajjhosita, q. v.[*ajjhosati

ajjhosanna, mfn. (pp. of adhi-ava + √sad, cf.
osanna, avasanna), Sv I (Se) 460,4 (w. r. for ajjho-
panna, DN I 245,25, = ogālha); Mp II 64,4 (do.,
AN I 74,5).

ajjhosāna, n. [sa. adhyavasāna], catching at,
grasping, coveting, DN II 58,34 = III 289,4 = AN
IV 400,26 (chandarāgaṁ paṭicca ~aṁ, ~aṁ paṭicca
pariggaho; '— ahaṁ maman ti balava-sanniṭṭhānaṁ,
Sv Mp); MN I 191,4 (chando ālayo anunayo +;
= ajjhogāhitvā gilitvā gahaṇavasena ~aṁ, Ps);
411,21 = 498,16 (sārāga +); pl. ~ā, SN III 187,4;
V 89,3 (saṁyojana-vinibandhā +-; Spk); AN I 66,10
foll. (kāmarāga [or ditthirāga]-vinivesa- + ; Mp); Dhs
1059 (As 363,9), 1136 (cf. Trsl. p. 277); Dhp-a IV 63,2
(ālaya +); — °-lakkhaṇa, n., character of a°, Nett
23,29; mfn. ib. 27,11 (~ā taṇhā). — Ifc. v. an-°,
ekanta°, kāma°, diṭṭhi-°, bhava°.

ajjhosāya (and ajjhosa), ind. (abs. of ajjhosati ;
sa. adhyavasāya and adhyavasya), having grasped,
mostly in the phrase ~āya (or ~a) tiṭṭhati, to continue
grasping, SN IV 159,8 (cf. Nett 155,25, Nett-a) ≠
MN I 266,30 = II 265,2 (abhinandati +; = taṇ-
hâjjhosānena gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā gaṇhāti, Ps;
as for gilitvā here and below see SN IV 159,8, cf.
ajjhomucchita); MN I 270,15 (do. with negation:
nâjjhosāya); SN III 14,7 (do., = gilitvā pariniṭṭha-
petvā gaṇhāti, Spk); IV 36,5; 60,15; 79,20 (do.) 71,11*
(nâjjhosāya [ɔ: *ajjhavasāya - ˇ ˇ - ˇ] bhuñjati);
Mil 69,3 (abhinandanti +); Mp II 64,4 (ajjhopannā
ti ~ gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā ṭhitā); an-ajjhosāya
titthato, MN I 270,17; tañ ca ajjhosa tiṭṭhati, SN IV
73,20* = Th 98 (Th-a); 794; nâjjhosa tiṭṭhati, SN
IV 74,23* (= taṁ ārammanaṁ gilitvā, Spk) =
Th 806.ajjhosāya

ajjhosita, mfn. (pp. of ajjhosati , sa. adhyava-
sita), (a) in an active sense: adhering to, catching hold of,
grasping, MN I 65,18 (allīna, upagata +; with acc.
bhavadiṭṭhiṁ); 233,10 (do., = taṇhādiṭṭhivasen' eva
veditabbo); Nidd I 75,7; Thī 470 (with loc.; =
taṇhāvasena abhiniviṭṭhā, Thī-a); Pv 761 (toe; =
do'. Pv-a); AN II 25,28*; Mil 76,24; — (b) in a pas-
sive sense: what is adhered to, grasped, occupied;
taken for granted, Nidd I 411,13 (Nidd-a); SN II
94,15 (~aṁ mamāyitaṁ parāmaṭṭhaṁ; = taṇhāya
gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā gahitaṁ, Spk) = 96,7; AN
II 25,24*; 26,1* (diṭṭhaṁ sutaṁ mutaṁ + ; = gilitvā
pariniṭṭhapetvā gahitaṁ, Mp). —- Ifc. v. an-°.

[*ajjhosati or *ajjhoseti], pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava +
√so; *ajjhosiyati would correspond to sa. adhyavasyati,
and Sadd gives siyati as pr. 3 sg. of √sā antakammani),
to determine (a place), catch, take hold of; to conceive,
ascertain (during meditation); fut. 2 sg. ~issasi, MN
I 328,16 (paṭhaviṁ, etc.; = paṭhaviṁ ajjhosāya
gilitvā pariniṭṭhapetvā taṇhā-māna-diṭṭhīhi gaṇhis-
sasi, Ps); 1 sg. ~ issāmi, ib. 21; inf. ~ituṁ, MN II
263,8 (abhinandituṁ abhivadituṁ +); abs. (a ) ~itvā,
Ps II 99,7 (v. l. ~etvā); (b) ajjhosāya and ajjhosa
(q. v.); grd. ~itabba, MN I 109,36 (v. l. ~etabba;
abhinanditabba + ; quoted As 5,4); pp. ajjhosita, q. v.[*ajjhosati

ajjhohaṭa, mfn. (pp. of adhi-ava-√hṛ; cf. sa.
abhyavahṛta), eaten, swallowed, Abh 757; As 330,16
(taṁ hi . . . ~aṁ kucchiṁ vitthambheti); Ss 148,4;
Saddh 610 (with active sense: ~o va balisaṁ maccho
ɔ: the canonical vaṁkaghasta; cf. bhattaṁ bhutto,
Kacc-v 628).

ajjhoharaṇa, n. (from ajjhoharati), (a) putting
into, applying (of a goad-stick), AN V 324,18 (pato-
dassa ~aṁ; = attano abhimukhassa patodassa
~saṁkhātaṁ patanaṁ, Mp); — (b) eating, Ps I 256,24
(dva-tikkhattuṁ °-matten'eva, by eating only twice
or thrice). — Ifc. v. brāhmaṇa-°.

ajjhoharaṇīya, mfn. (grd. of ajjhoharati), what
is to be, or can be eaten, Ja II 8,6'; VI 258,23' (°âhāro);
Dhp-a I 284,4 (°-mattaṁ, only so much). — Ifc. v.
gala°; cf. ajjhoharitabba.

ajjhoharati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-ava + √hṛ, cf. sa.
abhyava + √hṛ), (a) to put into, to pour into, ~ati,
MN I 423,8 (= anto paveseti, Ps; but more likely to
c below); pot. 3 sg. ~eyyuṁ, MN I 245,14; fut. 1 pl.
~issāma, ib. 11; — (b) to drag down, Ja VI 198,4*; —
(c) to swallow, to eat, pr. 3 sg. ~ati, As 401,26 (pari-
bhuñjati ~, = 'āhāreti'); Mil 366,28 (ajjhohāraṁ);
1 sg. ~āmi, AN IV 318,10 (saṁkhāditvā ~); 3 pl.,
~anti, SN II 269,11 (do.); aor. 3 sg. ~ari, SN II
270,27; Ja II 293,21' (= 'ajjhupāhari'); VI 205,2*
= 213,6* (taṁ sā gar'~); Pv-a 283,11; abs. ~itvā, Ja
I 460,24 (maṁsaṁ khāditvā [ɔ: saṁkhāditvā] ~);
pass. 3 sg. ~īyati, As 330,4 (kabaḷiṁkatvā ~); grd.
~itabba, As 330,13 (galena ~aṁ = 'galajjhohara-
ṇīyaṁ'); Mil 366,30 (yoginā . . . ajjhohāraṁ ~aṁ);
pp. ajjhohaṭa (q. v.); cf. ajjhoharaṇa and next.

1ajjhohāra, m. [cf. sa. abhyavahāra], (a) the
act of swallowing, eating, taking food, Dhātup 379
(= √bhuj1); Vin IV 233,22' (~e ~e āpatti saṁghā-
disesassa); — (b) food, Mil 176,5; 366,28-30 (~aṁ
ajjhoharati . . . ~aṁ ajjhoharitabbaṁ).

ajjhohita, mfn. (pp. of adhi-ava-√dhā; cf. sa.
abhyava + √dhā), laid upon (or into); uṇhaṁ ~aṁ
mukhe, Ja II 7,27* (= uṇhaṁ ajjhoharaṇīyaṁ mukhe
~aṁ ṭhapitaṁ, Ct.).

ajā, f. [ts.], a she-goat, Abh 502; Ja III 125,6*
(~ kānā, cf. kāna-elako, ib. 10'); Ja III 401,14,19,27*;
IV 251,23* (cf. Mhbh II 2193 [66,8]); Dhp-a I 176,24.
Cf. ajī, ajikã.

a-jāta, mfn. [ts.], unborn, not yet developed,
Ja IV 26,6*; Dhs §1036 (~ā abhūtā asañjātā, etc., scil.
dhammā anuppannā); ~aṁ abhūtaṁ akataṁ asaṁ-
khataṁ, said of Nibbāna, Ud 80,23 (Ud-a 449,14) ≠
It 37,5 (It-a 211,2). — °-pakkha, mfn. [sa. ajāta-
pakṣa], whose wings are not yet developed, Ja IV
280,14*. — °-buddhi, mfn., who has not yet come to
years of discretion, Vism 437,10-23 (dārako).

Ajātasattu, m. [sa. Ajātaçatru], Npr. of the king
of Magadha, son of Bimbisāra, and contemporary of
Buddha, generally styled rājā Māgadho ~Vedehiputto,
DN I 47,4, etc.; instr. ~unā, MN II 116,29; Ja IV
343,1; gen. ~uno, Mp II 141,2; ~ussa, DN I 49,9; Ja
IV 343,2; MN I 231,5 ; legend about his name and short
biography, Sv I 133,28 — 139,6; 153,9-27; his mother
Vedehi-kumārī (Kosala-devī, or Kosalarāja-dhītā) was
a sister of king Pasenadi, JalI 403,1β; III 121,17
(her death: Ja II 237,20); he reigned 32 years, Dīp
III 60; Mhv II 31; his capital Rājagaha, DN I 47,1;
49,31. — As a little child (Ajātasattu-kumāra) he
accompanies his father to see Jotika's palace, Dhp-a
IV 211,10; admirer and friend of Devadatta, Vin II
185,1 foll.; Ja I 185,28; 508,10; SN II 242,2; Deva-
datta incites him to kill his father and to attempt
Buddha's life, Vin II 190,15 foll., Dhp-a I 140,5 foll.;
II 164,7; Ps III 480,3; Pv-a 105,23 ; he kills his father
Bimbisāra and attacks Jotika's palace, Dhp-a IV
221,25 (cf. ib. 211,10); ~ussa pitughāta-kammaṁ,
Ja V 261,33 (cf. Mp II 141,2: ~uno kammaṁ kusala-
cchedakaṁ ahosi); his remorse, Sv I 140,13; attempts
the life of his brother Sīlava-kumāra, Th-a ad
Th 608—9; prepares an attack on the Vajjī, DN II
72,4; AN IV 17,15; he fights Pasenadi, SN I 83—85;
Ja IV 343,1 (cf. II 237,17; 403,16 foll; III 406,1);
Dhp-a III 259,7; he marries Vajira-kumāri(kā), the
daughter of Pasenadi, Ja II 404,20; his son Udāyi-
bhadda (or Udaya-bhaddaka), DN I 50,25; his fear
of king Pajjota, MN III 7,14; his enmity with the
Licchavī, SN II 268,2; he takes the refuges, DN I
85,6 foll.; his anger against Upaka, the pupil of
Devadatta, AN II 182,24; he punishes the murderers
of Moggallāna, Dhp-a III 66,20; in the 8th year
of his reign Buddha dies, DīpIII 60; Mhv II 32
(Mhv-ṭ); Mhbv 85,1i; he asks the Mallas for a portion
of the relics of Buddha, DN II 164,29 , and erects a
thūpa for that purpose, ib. 166,31; Sv II 274,3—276,3;
279,18—284,9 (cf. Bv XXVIII,2; Vv-a l 70,1; 200,2;
Pv-a 212,4); protector of the first Buddhist council (of
Mahãkassapa) at Bājagaha [a post-canonical tradi-
tion], Mhv III 16; Pj I 94,24 foll.; Sp 110,6 foll. (Sp-ṭ);
Kv-a 2,8; Sās 5,11; murdered by his son, (a tradition of
this dynasty), Sv I 153,23; Mhv IV 1—5 (Mhv-ṭ); goes
to hell in spite of his conversion and will be re-born
as a pacceka-buddha under the name of Vijitāvī (so
Bm and Sv-nṭ), Sv I 237—38.

a-jāti, mfn., where there is no birth, n. sg. (subst.)
~iṁ, Bv II 13 (= nibbānaṁ, Bv-a), quoted Ud-a
493,21 (where Ce confirms the reading ajātim (a)pi).

a-jānana, n., ignorance, Mil 266,1i (anādariyena
vā ~ena vā, scil. āpattiṁ āpajjanti); — used as a
participle in the following combinations: °-kāla, m.,
Ja VI 177,19 (tadā supaṇṇānaṁ nāge gahetuṁ ~o,
i. e. it was not known to them at that time how to catch
the snakes); — °-tā, f. abstr., Ja III 92,10' (~āya
acetanaṁ); — °-bhāva, m. id., Ja V 199,8 (methuna-
dhammassa).

a-jānika, mfn., not to be known (or perhaps better
~ikā, f. secrecy (mystification), HS; Tr. suggests ajā-
niya), Ja VI 368,22 (~aṁ katvā, stealthily, without
his knowledge).
