[scil. cittaṁ] assa atthîti atthikavā, Sv).

atthika-vāda, m. (2atthika + vāda), the doc-
trine of positive morality; DN I 55,29 (tesaṁ tucchaṁ
musā vilāpo ye keci ~aṁ vadanti; paron.) = MN I
515,17 (Ps). — mfn., adhering to that doctrine; MN I
404,14 (sīlavā purisapuggalo sammādiṭṭhi ~o). Cf.
natthika-vāda, m. & mfn.

atthi-kkhaṇa, m. (1atthi + khaṇa), the very
moment of (its) existence; loc. ~e, Abhidh-av 19,11
(opp. bhaṅga-kkhaṇe and bhaṅgato uddhaṁ [cf. sa.
kṣaṇikatva]).

atthikinī, f (adj.) (from 1atthika), desirous of,
seeking; only ifc. v. viveka°; as to the formation ~ikinī,
cf. anantarāyikinī, ārāmikinī, etc., Mogg III 33 foll.

atthi-khīra, (m)f(n), [sa. asti-ksīra], having milk;
Sadd 299,4; 450,11; 673,21; Mogg-v III 21 (~ā brāh-
maṇī). Cf. Pāṇ II 2,24 vārt íl.

atthitā, f. (abstr. of 1atthi; sa. astitā), being,
(permanent) existence, reality; SN II 17,9 (dvaya(ṁ)-
nissito ayaṁ loko: atthitañ c'eva natthitañ ca; —
sassataṁ, Spk) = III 135,1; Ja V 110,5 (kassaci ~aṁ
atthitānatthitaṁ vā jāneyyāsi); As 394,33 (vuṭṭhānaka-
paññāya ~ā); Vism 118,27 (visabhāgānaṁ puggalā-
naṁ ~ā); 121,5'; Ps 1296,31 (guṇānaṁ attani ~aṁ
paccavekkhantassa); Pj I 123,24 (sobhanānaṁ ...

(-instr.) ~āya, Ps 1273,13; Pj I 132,2; Ud-a 153,2-3;
384,22; Pv-a 94,14 (giving the sense of the suff. -va(t));
143,24 (do.). — Cf. natthitā. — Ifc. v. idam-°,
suv-°.

atthi-dhamma, mfn., having real existence; Mil
270,23 (yathā yathā ~aṁ opammehi ādīpamyaṁ);
316,6 (~assa nibbānassa); Ps II 345,14 (Ee) ("yaṁ kiñci
neyyaṁ nāma ~an" ti, cf. Nidd I 178,15). — Cf.
natthi-dhamma.

atthi(n), mfn. [sa. arthin], desirous, wanting;
with some serious intention; Abh 740 (m., a beggar,
mendicant); nom. m. atthī, Sn 957 = 1043 = 1105
= 1112 = 1118 (~i pañhena āgamiṁ; = atthiko
atthin°aṭṭhi(n)), q. v.; āmisa°, cittasamādha°, bhojana°,
vāda°, sukha°.

atthi-paccaya, m., positive causality (something
existing being the cause of something other); Tikap 6,22;
Tikap-a 20,24 (= Vism 540,14); 55,28 foll.; 66,3 foll.;
Abhidh-s 39,8 (≠ avigatapaccaya, Vism 541,13). —
°-dhamma, m., things liable to be that, Vism 541,12.
— Cf. natthipaccaya.

atthi-bhāva, m., existence; the being present;
As 31,11; 83,37; Ud-a 38,29; Ps II 140,12 (Ee) (attani
~aṁ na jānāpetukāmo); thus frequently with jānāti
or similar verbs: Ja I 222,6 (sarassa ~aṁ . . . na
saddahatha); 290,21 (~aṁ ñatvā); III 287,10 (sūkarā-
nam ~am ñatvā); V 356,1 (°haṁsānaṁ ~aṁ ārocetvā);
VI 160,9 (°assa vasanaṭṭhānaṁ vā ~aṁ vā natthibhā-
vaṁ vā); Dhp-a I 247,14 (bhikkhūnaṁ vihāre~aṁ vā
natthibhăvaṁ vā jānāhi); Dhp-a I 162,12 (tāya sañ-
atthi-bhāva217,2 (°assa ~aṁ vā natthibhāvaṁ vā ñatvā); do.
with negation = to take no notice of, not to care for
(gen.): Dhp-a II 5,1 (bhikkhūnaṁ ~am pi ajānitvā);

20,19 (tassā ~aṁ na jānāti); 68,4 (do.); V 95,17
(~aṁ pi 'ssā va na aññāsi). — Nibbānassa atthi-

bhāva.

atthiya, mfn. [sa. arthya; cf. atthika], 1. useful,
profitable; only ifc. v. atta°, kim-°, maha°, yad-°.
— 2. desirous of, ifc. v. sukha°. Cf. next.

atthiyā, ind. (cf. atthāya), on account of, for the

cf. Ja IV 380,25* = Ps III 76,17* (reading metrically

atthi-saṁkhalūpama, mfn., like to a skeleton

atthi-sukha, n. (1atthi + sukha), delight of

foll. (+ bhoga-sukha, anaṇa-sukha, anavajja-sukha;

atth'-uccāraṇa-visesa, m. (2attha, etc.), differ-

atth'-uddhara, m. (2attha + uddhāra), (a) a

nation of the Aṭṭhakathā-kaṇḍa, q. v.; Dīp V 37 (quoted

26,14—27,20 (evaṁ); 28,8-13 (me); 28,14-25 (sutaṁ);
31,24—32,12 (samaya); Pj II 237,28 (°-paduddhāra-
padavaṇṇanā); Ud-a 46,17; abl. ~ato, Vibh-a 86,2-10
= Vism 496,31—497,6; — °-ṇa, n. id. (b); Ps I 244,6
(tesaṁ dhammānaṁ °-nayen' etaṁ [ɔ: pañca pi . . .

an abstract of the contents, As 6,37 (~aṁ, scil. Aṭṭhaka-

atth'-uppatti-kala, m., the time of an aṭṭhup-

atthûpaparikkhi(n), mfn. from prec. (q. v.);
AN II 97,16 (Mp); IV 221,10; 223,10; 296,6; 328,11.

atthûpasaṁhita, mfn. (2attha + upasaṁhita,

atthûpeta, mfn. (2attha + upeta), expert in the

yaṁ āsabhī vācā bhāsitā, Ck; Ed. ulārā kho ty-

[atra-bhavam, Ja V 169,26* = 197,1*; so Fsb.

kurvī o: āstīrya kūrcīm or āstīrṇa-kūrco?).

1atriccha, mfn., wishing too much, exceedingly
covetous, greedy; Ja III 206,10; IV 5,17'; Vibh-a 472,6.
Etymology (as well of atricchatā, and of atricchā)
uncertain; all these words seem to originate with phrases
like atricchaṁ cakkam āsado, Ja I 414,6* (= atra
1atriccha= III 207,15* = IV 4,23* (Ed. here following B-mss.
atriccho; Ct.: atricchatāya samannāgatattā atriccho
[Cks atricchā, see Ja II 231,1*] . . . atr' icchan ti pi
pāṭho, atra atra icchamāno ti attho; atricchā ti pi
pāṭho, atricchāyā ti attho), quoted Vibh-a 472,4*;
we prefer to take atricchaṁ as part. m. sg. of *atric-
chati or aticchati (q. v., cf. aticchatā, f.), /. e. ati +
icchati, cf. Amg (sam)aïcchaï; but icchati may repre-
sent sa. icchati and īpsati, and ṛcchati as well; cf.
yadicchā (sa. yadṛcchā) and atricchatā.
Rem. As to the duplicate aticchatā, atricchatā
cf. mṭ ad Vibh-a 470,12 foll.: aticca icchatī ti
aticc'-iccho, tassa bhāvo aticc'-icchata ti vattabbe
cci-kāra-lopaṁ katvā aticchatā ti vuttaṁ; . . .
atricchatā ti ca sā eva vuccatī ti, tatrâ pi
neruttika-vidhānena padasiddhi veditabbā. Thus
atricch° could be approximative sa. aty-ṛcch° or
even a-tṛps° (√tṛp, see PED s. v. atricchā), if at
any rate *atṛpsu, *atṛpsā could be proved to signify
'insatiable, insatiability'.

atricchatā, f. (abstr. of 1atriccha) = atricchā
(q.v.); Ja III 222,6; 223,23'; IV 331,8*-14* (quoted

chatâdīnaṁ pāpadhammānaṁ); 241,2 (~aṁ paja-
hanto); Vibh-a 470,15 (= 'aticchatā', Vibh 470,6—
472,17); Ps I 96,22 (+ pāpicchatā, mahicchatā); II
185,14 (do., = Mp I 75,6); Vism 70,25 (~āya pahā-
nam); 78,17 (~āya dvāra-pidahanaṁ); Ud-a 228,8
(°-âdayo dose ārakā parivajjetvā). — °-hata, mfn.,
atricchatā

[atricchati, pr. 3 sg.; part. m. ~aṁ, v. r. Ja IV
4,23* (= atra atra icchamāno, ib. 5,20'); see next.]
atricchā, f. (cf. 1atriccha & atricchatā), in-

pi pāṭho, atricchāyā ti attho, ib. 5,ai% see next); —

bhena, see atricchati). — °-niggaha, m., subduing

(atricchā + abhibhūta), overcome by greediness, Ja
[atricchati327,26 (°-vasena).

ati, ind. [ts.], prefix to nouns (subst., adj., adv.)
or prp. to verbs, before vowels generally taking the form
acc-, e. g. acc-uṇha, acc-odāta, sometimes with lengthe-
ning of the foll. vowel, e. g. accāhita = ati-ahita, but
also ati (or at'), e. g. ati-ambila, ati-iṭṭha, ati-ucca &
at'-ucca. —- 1. (a) prefixed to a subst, implying 'abun-
dance, excess, superiority, transgression, above'; — (b)
to an adj. or adv. = too (much), very much, quite. —
2. to verbs and their derivates = too much, very much;
over, through; by, away (far away); beyond, too far;
also 'into' (e. g. ati-neti, ati-harati). — 3. as govern-
ing prp. v. ati-diṭṭhiyā (cf. adhi-° & abhi-°). -—
4. sometimes inserted (like adhi) in an iterative comp.,
implying 'cumulation', v. cakkâticakka, chattâtic-
chatta, balâtibala, mañcâtimañca, mānâtimāna
cf. Sakkānaṁ ati-Sakko, devānaṁ atidevo etc. (but
differently devâtideva, q. v.). —- Cf. ativiya (atīva),
by which it is generally rendered in Ctt. — Sometimes
alternating with or corresponding to adhi- (see ati-
deva), or abhi- (see atikkanta, cf. atijāta). — Com-
bined with an other prp., see upâti-°, pâti-°, vîti-°. —
The sense of ati ts given Abh 1138 (= atisaye); 1182
(antobhāva-bhusatthâtisaya-pūjāsu atikkame || bhū-
tabhāve pasaṁsāyaṁ daḷhatthâdo siyā 'ati'); Būp
87,8 ('ati'ti atikkamana, atikkanta, atisaya, bhusattha,
etc., see these words); Ud-a 224,29 (atī ti accantatthe
nipāto); cf. Sadd III Ce 774,17.

ati-aggi, m. [cf. sa. atyagni], too hot a fire, Mil
277,29 (~inā odanaṁ uttarati).

ati-añjati, pr. 3 sg. [ati + √añj), to charge too

atikkanta-vara, mfn., who is above (granting)

atikkanta-vela, mfn., being out of all bounds,

atikkanta-satthuka, mfn., of which there is no
more teacher, ~aṁ pāvacanaṁ, Sv I 34,14 = Pj I
110,3 = Ps I 10,18. Cf. atīta-satthuka.

atikkantikā, f., a woman transgressing the bounds
of good behaviour, Mil 122,20 (bhinna-sīmāya ~āya).
Ifc. v. sīmâ°.

atikkama, m. [sa. atikrama], transgressing,
transgression, surpassing, overcoming, Abh 776; 1182
(the sense of prp. ati-, cf. Rūp 87,8); sabba-[ṭ]ṭhitīnam
~am addā, SN I 193,21* (= atikkama-bhūtaṁ nibbā-
naṁ, Spk); dukkhassa ~aṁ, Dhp I 91 = Anāg 69;
caturaṅgo ~o, Saddh 64 (parassa dāresu). — Ifc. v.
aṅgâ°, (aṭṭha)lokadhammâ°, an-°, apagamâ°,
ākāsâ°, ārammaṇâ°, upacārâ°, kālâ°, dur-°,
majjhaṇhâ°, rūpanimittâ°, vassānâ°, viññāṇâ°,
himapātâ°.

atikkamati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. atikrāmati, atikramate],
1. intrans. (a) to pass away, elapse (pañca vassasahas-
sāni); (b) to pass (near) by (avidūre); —2. trans, (c) to
pass, cross, transgress (maggaṁ, sīmaṁ; āṇaṁ, vacanaṁ,
sikkhāpadaṁ); (d) to transgress against, or to be unfaithful
to (bhariyaṁ); (e) to transgress, or to commit adultery
with (parassa dārāni; cf. aticarati); (f) to surpass
(devānaṁ devânubhāvaṁ); (g) to overcome, to escape
from (saññojanāni, bhavaṁ): — pr. 3 sg. ~ati, Pv-a
67,18 (dvārasamīpena maggena, b); Ja III 243,26'(<f);
3 pl. ~anti, Sn p. 48,2 (avidūre, b); Ja IV 53,21*
(amhe, d); VI 115,6* (parassa dārāni, e); AN IV
201.12 (sikkhāpadaṁ, c); 1 pl. ~āma, Ja IV 53,20*
(d); — pot. 3 sg. ~eyya, Sn 396 (e); Dhp 221 (sañño-
janaṁ sabbaṁ, g); [Mil 265,4 see atikkameti, caus.];
— aor. 3 pl. ~iṁsu, DN II 130,14 (nissāya nissāya ~,
b; for story cf. Mahābhāṣya II 120,20); ~amuṁ, Ap
68,18 (tiṁsa vassasahassāni, a; quoted Th-a (Ce) 21,18*
ad Th 1); — part. ~manta, DN II 130,19 (b); Ja IV
141.13 (c); Mil 227,15 (āṇaṁ, c); an-atikkamantā,
Ud-a 346,31 (g); — inf. ~ituṁ, Ja I 437,13 (tassā
vacanaṁ, c); — abs. (α) atikkamma, Sn 361 ( ˇ ˇ - ˇ ;
bhavaṁ, g); It 51,11* (metre corrupt, read ati[k]kamma
< so > māradheyyaṁ(?), g); MN III 120,12 ≠ DN
II 12,10 (devānaṁ devânubhāvaṁ, f); Ja I 147,30
(maggaṁ, c); VI 592,25 (do.); = after, besides, Rūp
87,8 (giving the sense of ati-); Ja I 262,19; MN I
200,17; III 195,1 ≠ AN V 226,20; — Ja III 472,12*
( ˇ ˇ - ˇ ;g); Kv-a 35,5* (paññattiṁ an-atikkamma
(b); — (β)~itvā, Ja I 137,3' (f); 263,22 (sīmaṁ, c); IV
139,25 (c); Pp 17,2 (c); Mil 336,27 (f; + atisayitvā
ajjhottharitvā); Dhp-a I 96,7 (pabbajita-divasato
addhamāsaṁ ~, a fortnight after his pabbajjā); Pv-a
15,14 (+ laṁghitvā, d); 168,19 (c); an-atikkamitvā,
Ja I 348,11 (kālaṁ, without coming too late, at time);
IV 246,3 (Bhadda-nakkhattaṁ ~; better v. l. °kka-
metvā, caus.); — grd. (a ) ~amitabba, SN I 29,2 (d;
viheṭhetabbaṁ ghaṭṭetabbaṁ, Spk); (β) ~amanīya
(q. v.); — pp. atikkanta; caus. atikkameti & atik(k)a-
māpeti (q. v.).

atikkamana, n. [sa. atikramaṇa], overstepping,
transgressing, overcoming; Abhidh-av 983 (tassâtikka-
manatthāya); Rūp 87,8 (= prp. ati-, e.g. atirocati
amhehi [Pv 316], atīto). — Ifc. v. an-°, sīmâ°.

atikkamāpeti, pr. 3 sg. (caus. of prec), to cause
to let pass; abs. ~etvā, Ja VI 5,3 (pakativelaṁ, after
the proper time).

atikkameti (or atikkameti, q. v.), pr. 3 sg. (caus.
of atikkamati), to cause to pass, to let pass; imper.
~ehi, Ja I 151,5 (mayhaṁ vāraṁ); —- pot. ~eyya,
Mil 265,4 (divasaṁ); Spk I 138,2 (= 'atipāteyya');
— fut. ~essāmi, Ja I 151,10; — inf. ~etuṁ, Mil
265,1 (na so divaso sakkā ~); — abs. ~etvā, Ja IV
247,6 (ajja; if you miss this day); an-°, Ja I 162,29
(vutta-velaṁ, without missing); Ja IV 246,3 (v. l.)
Cf. next.

atikkameti, pr. 3 sg. = atikkameti (q. v.);
paṭhamaṁ pādaṁ suṅka-ghātaṁ ~eti, Vin III 52,10';
part. gen. ~ayato, Vin III 251,17**; aor. ~esi, Ja I
114,22 (divase); pot. ~eyya, Vin III 149,17** (pamā-
ṇaṁ); abs. ~etvā, Vin III 151,32'.

ati-kkhaya, m., (gradual) loss or destruction,
Cp III 10,4 (cf. Ja I 329,30; 331,16).

ati-(k)khippam, ind., too soon; ~aṁ Sugato
parinibbāyissati, DN II 140,1 = 148,7 ; ~aṁ Bhagavā
parinibbuto, DN II 157,22 = 158,17, 22 = 159,11 =
162,21 = Vin II 284,16.ati-khippam

ati-kāya, mfn. [ts.], of extraordinary body, Ja V
267,5* (~o, scil. Ajjuno; = bala-sampanna-mahā-
kāyo, Ct.); 269,5* (kimayo ~ā; Ct. ib. 274,22')-

ati-kāra, m., doing to much, Ja I 431,1* (paron.:
~am akarâcariya [ ˇ ˇ - ˇ ˇ ˇ - - ˇ] = atireka-
karaṇaṁ, Ct.; Ck, Ee, Se atikaram).

ati-kāla, m., very early time, too early a time;
adv. (acc.) instr, gen. (as ciraṁ cirena cirassa): instr,
in the phrase: ~ena gāmaṁ pavisati, atidivā paṭi-
kkamati, Vin I 70,4; MN I 469,26-28 (with diva for
atidivā; = atipāto, Ps); SN I 200,28 (= pāto va,
Spk); AN III 117,3 (= atipāto va, Mp); — gen.
~ass'eva, too early Ja III 119,12; — in Sv I 113,6
~aṁ explains 'ati-velaṁ', (beyond the time) too long.

ati-kāḷa, mfn., too dark; f. ~ī, DN II 175,24
(atidīghā+, opp. accodātā); MN I 88,9 (do.); gen.
~iyā, Ja VI 3,6 (atidīghāya +).

ati-kilamati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. ati + √klam], to be
over-exerted); 1 sg. ~āmi, Ja IV 284,19' (= 'nitam-
māmi').

ati-kilinna, mfn. (ati + pp. of √klid), too much
boiled, said of odana, bhatta, and opp. to uttandula
(q. v.): Ja I 340,3; III 383,2-4; IV 44,9; Ps III 361,16;
Ud-a 405,10.

ati-kisa, mfn. [sa. ati-kṛça], too lean, too thin;
f. ~ā, DN II 175,24 (atidīghā'+, opp. atithūlā); MN
I 88,9 (do.); gen. ~āya, Ja VI 3,4 (atidīghāya+).

ati-kusala, mfn., very clever or skilful, given as
ex. of the sense 'atisaya' of prp. ati, Rūp 87,9; Sadd
III 774,20 (Ce).

ati-kodha, m., excessive anger, given as ex. of the
sense 'bhusaṁ' of prp. ati, Rūp 87,9; Sadd III 774,20
(Ce).

ati-khaṇati, pr. 3 sg. [ati + √khan], to dig too
deep; pot. ~aṇe, Ja II 296,15* (nâ°); pp. atikhāta,
q. v.

ati-khaṇana, n. (from prec), digging too deep,
Ja II 296,20' (read atikhaṇanena for atikhaṇena; =
'atikhātena').

ati-khara, mfn. [ts.], too sharp; Ud-a401,25 (scil.
ābādho, cf. ib. 401,6) = Sv ad DN II 128,10*; Ja II
249,6 (~aṁ katvā vādemi, said of too sharp tuning
of a lute).

ati-khāta, n. (pp. of atikhaṇati), digging too
deep; ~aṁ hi pāpakaṁ . . . ~ena nāsitaṁ (scil.
dhanaṁ), Ja II 296,15*-l6* (= atikhaṇana, Ct.). (Cf,
ati-dhanta).

ati-(k)khippam, ind., too soon; ~aṁ Sugato
parinibbāyissati, DN II 140,1 = 148,7 ; ~aṁ Bhagavā
parinibbuto, DN II 157,22 = 158,17, 22 = 159,11 =
162,21 = Vin II 284,16.ati-khippam

ati-khīṇa, mfn. [ati + √kṣi(?), cf. khepeti], the
sense is not quite clear, perhaps 'destroyed, consumed,
i. e. quite worn out or slackened'; only Dhp I 56
(cāpâtikhīṇā; Dhp-a III 132,24: cāpāto ~ā, cāpā
vinimmuttā sarā, 'arrows shot from the bow'(!) cf. Sadd
II 1236).

ati-khuddaka, mfn., too short or very small,
Vin IV 171,6 (~aṁ nisīdanaṁ). Cf. ati-khuṭaka =
'atimaṭāhaka', Sp ad Vin II 138,10 (see Vin II 319,34;
Sp Ce omits this passage).

ati-ga, mfn. [ts.], who has passed beyond, over-
come, escaped from; only ifc. v. 4asitâ°, oghâ°, catu-
yogâ°, pañca-saṅgâ°, yoga°, saṅgâ°, sabba-
saṁyojanâ°, sīmâ°.

[ati-gacchati] pr. 3 sg. [ati + √gaṁ or √gā], (a)
to overcome, to conquer; no forms of the present tense
are found, see acceti; aor. 3 sg. accagamā, Sn 8 (imaṁ

in the phrase accayo maṁ [no] ~, Vin I 315,10; II
192,13; DN I 85,16 (Sv = maṁ atikkamma atibha-

— accagā, Sn 1040 √sibbaniṁ; Nidd II 10,15); Sn
638 = Dhp 414 (mohaṁ); 3 pl. accaguṁ, It 93,14*

niṁ; Ed. ajjhagū; — atikkamiṁsu, Ct.); — (b) to
pass away, to die, aor. 3 sg., Mhv XL I 3 (navame

ati-gata, mfn. (pp. of atigacchati), who has
passed beyond or away, who has overcome; [Ja III
484.2 9* (nasakkh'atigato poso punar-eva nivattituṁ;

ati-gatatta, n. abstr. of prec, Dhp-a IV 159,15.

ati-gandha, mfn. [ts.], strong smelling; m. lemon

ati-gambhīra, mfn., very deep or profound;
AN I 219,31 (~aṁ pañhaṁ); Ud-a 424,14 (°-vittha-

ati-gami(n), mfn., who passes beyond or con-
quers; ifc. v. yogâ°.ati-gami

ati-gami(n), mfn., who passes beyond or con-

ati-garu, mfn., highly reverend, venerable; gen. m.

ati-gālayati (also written °gāḷayati), pr. 3 sg.

ati-gāḷha, mfn. [sa. ati + gāḍha, pp. of √gāh],

Pp-a 215,24 (~ena, = 'āgālhena', Pp 32,34 = AN I
283.3 2).

ati-guṇa-kāraka, mf. (~ikā), a great benefactor,
whose benefits (kāra, [√kṛ], cf. bahu-kāra) are not

dukkara-kārikā, ib. 329,26-3 0).

ati-guṇatā, f. (abstr. of ati + guṇa), extra-
ordinary virtue, Mil 278,9.

ati-ghamsati, pr. 3 sg. (ati + √ghṛṣ), to rub out;
abs. ~itvā, Paṭis II 196,8 (Buddhañāṇaṁ deva-
mannssānaṁ paññaṁ pharitvā ~ tiṭṭhati, v. l. atikka-

ati-caṇda, mfn. [ts.] very violent, ~o, Dhp-a IV
14,2; ~aṁ, ind., Ja VI 34,17 (gantvā).

ati-caraṇa, n. [ts.], transgression (esp. adultery);
Ps III 427,8-12; — °-bhāva, m. id. (abstr.), Dhp-a III
349,10 (itthiyā ~o).

ati-carati, pr. 3 sg. [ati + √car], Utt. to go beyond
the bounds (to graze too much): ~antaṁ goṇaṁ tuṇḍe
paharati (proverbially), Ja IV 300,17 (Ja-pot: sæpa-sē

of the person cuckolded); 3 sg. °rañño mahesiyā

~itvā, Dhp-a I 327,4 (parassa dare); Ja I 463,5; pp.
aticiṇṇa (q. v.).

ati-cari(n), mfn. [ts.], transgressing, committing
adultery, m. ~ī (mātugāmo), SN IV 242,6 (assad-
dho+); — most frequently f. °-cārinī: Abh 238;
Vin IV 225,20; SN II 259,25 = Vin III 107,10; AN
III 261,9 (mātugāmo ~inī); Ja IV 428,19'; V 435,12*;
430,35 (gen. pl. ~inīnaṁ); Pv 352 (bhariyā dussīlā
~inī; Pv-a); Dhp-a III 348,15; 350,1 (~iniṁ itthiṁ);
Pv-a 151,21 (do., v.L); 152,2; Vv-a 110,4. — Ifc. v.
an-°, dhammâ°.ati-cari

ati-carita(r), mf. (nomen agentis or fut. II of
prec), one who transgresses, or who commits adultery
(after a verb of the sense 'to remember'); AN II 61,25

v. l. aticaritvā); AN IV 66,11 (do., Ed. aticarittā, v. l.
aticārittaṁ, aticarituṁ, aticaritvā).ati-carita

ati-carita(r), mf. (nomen agentis or fut. II of
prec), one who transgresses, or who commits adultery
(after a verb of the sense 'to remember'); AN II 61,25
(after nâbhijānāmi [see abhijānāti] with acc. pers.;

aticārittaṁ, aticarituṁ, aticaritvā).ati-carita

ati-cari(n), mfn. [ts.], transgressing, committing
adultery, m. ~ī (mātugāmo), SN IV 242,6 (assad-
dho+); — most frequently f. °-cārinī: Abh 238;
Vin IV 225,20; SN II 259,25 = Vin III 107,10; AN
III 261,9 (mātugāmo ~inī); Ja IV 428,19'; V 435,12*;

an-°, dhammâ°.ati-cari

aticca, ind. (abs. of acceti), 1. having passed
beyond or through, having overcome, surmounting (acc),
Sn 519 (saṁsāraṁ; Pj); 527 (saṅgaṁ jālaṁ; = atikka-
mitvā, Pj); 529 (sabbaṁ vedaṁ; Pj); 531 (niraya-
du[k]khaṁ); 373 (kappātīto, aticca suddhipañño;
cf. the paronomastical schema . . . upasaṁkami,
upasamkamitvā . . . nisīdi, nisinno . . ., Vin III
1,23; 2,1 [Oldenberg, Gesch. d. Altind. Prosa, p.
49—52 = Gött. Abh. XVI. 1916—17]); Ud 71,11* (taṁ
saṅgaṁ); Ja V 396,22* (sabbāni bhūtāni). —2.beyond,

3. (used in the sense of aticarati, q. v.) having cuck-
olded (acc), Ja V 424,22* (ete patī pañca-m-aticca);
Vv-a 72,28 (~ cāro = 'ati-cāro).

ati-cchatta, n., a pre-eminent umbrella, As 2,19
(= atireka-ppamāṇaṁ visesa-vaṇṇa-saṇṭhānaṁ ca
chattaṁ). — Ifc. v. chattâ°. — m. [sa. Lexicogr.
aticchattra ɔ: ahicchattra], a mushroom; f. ~ā, the
anise plant; MTD.

aticchatā, f. (absír. of ati + icchā), desiring too
much, greediness, Vibh 350,36 (= attano lābhaṁ
aticca icchanabhāvo ~ā, . . . atricchatā ti pi etissā
eva nāmaṁ, Vibh-a 470,13).

(aticchati), pr. 3 sg. [Amg. aīcchaī (with full
flexion), from sa. ati + √i, after the analogy of
ati-gacchati (atîta = ati-gata); Tr. (cf. Sp-ṭ below)
refers to ati-√iṣ (eṣati) confounded with ati-√iṣ
(icchati); PED ati + ṛcchati] to pass on, only used
in imper. 2 pl. aticchatha (bhante)! a phrase by
which a mendicant is refused alms in a civil way (the
inverse phrase is tiṭṭhatha bhante, Ja V 212,15):
Ja III 462,12; VI 70,26; Dhp-a I 401,6; 402,6; IV
98,25-26 (Ed. aticcha); Ps III 71,13; Mp I 412,20;
II 137,3; Vv-a 101,1; Mil 9,13 ≠ Sp I 37,12-26 (cf.
Mhv V 132: gacchā ti); Ss 105,21; Vism 343,27; Sp-ṭ
ad Sp I 37,12: aticchathā ti atikkamitvā icchatha,
idha bhikkhā na labbhati, ito aññattha gantvā
bhikkhaṁ pariyesathā ti adhippāyo. Cf. Tr. notes
p. 65 & Oldenberg in Kuhn's Zeitschr. XXV (1881).

aticchāpeti, pr. 3 sg. (caus. of aticchati), to ask
to pass on; imp. 2 sg. ~ehi, Ja III 462,11.

ati-cāra, m. [ts.] — prec; Vv 132 (= aticca
cāro, Ct); Dhp-a III 348,16 (tassā ~ena lajjito); 350,1'
(= 'duccaritaṁ').

ati-ciṇṇa, mfn. (pp. of ati-carati), transgressed,

dhammo; = mayā sucarita-dhammo atikkanto, Ct.).

ati-citra, mfn., very splendid or brilliant, Mil
28,10-2 6 (~āni pañha-paṭibhānāni).

aticira(ṁ)-nivāsa, m., dwelling (inhabiting,

(aticiraṁ-nivāsena piyo bhavati appiyo); cf. ati-

aticira(ṁ)-nivāsa, m., dwelling (inhabiting,

(aticiraṁ-nivāsena piyo bhavati appiyo); cf. ati-
