cf. Kacc-v 316); cf. ajjh-āgāre above, and adhi-citte,
adhi-jegucche, adhi-deve, adhi-paññāya, adhi-sīle. —
Cf. also ajjhattaṁ, adhi-kumāri, adhitthi, adhi-
paññatti, adhi-(vi)mutti.

adhika, mfn. [ts.], exceeding, surpassing (in
number, etc.), differring in quantity: superior or in-
ferior; Abh 1176 (giving the sense of prp. abhi, e. g.
abhivassati, Abh-sūci); 1177 (do. of adhi, e.g. adhi-
sīlaṁ, Abh-sūci); Kacc-v 316 (the sense of upa ác

~o samāno; Ed. avikkosamāno); Ps III 415,5 (manus-

gharatanato uttaro . . . ~o vā visiṭṭho); — often in

kappa-sahassâ°, Dhp-a I 83,10, etc. — Ifc. v. an-°,

Adhikakka, n. Npr. of a sacred bathing place

(°-âpara-vacana, see 1añña (1.) cf. Sadd 266,27; 271,23,

adhikaraṇa-samatha

pl. catunnaṁ ~īnaṁ upari, As 263,9.adhikaraṇī

adhi-karotiadhi], Kacc-v 321 (cittaṁ ~ dhammā vattantîti

deity, or a haunting demon, cf. adhi-tiṭṭhati, adhi-
adhi-vatthahoti, Vin III 58,13 (cf. Sp (II) 374,20, w. r. adhi-
vatto); (loc) ~ā devatā, Vin I 28,36; MN I 306,5;
SN I 197,1; III 250,1; IV 302,23; Ja I 223,23;
II385,28; IV 194,1; Dhp-a III 182,2; Pv-a 17,28;
voc. f. ~e (Makhādevasmiṁ), Ja III 327,26* (tasmiṁ
~e ti devataṁ ālapati, Ct.); acc ~aṁ devataṁ,
Ud-a 323,1; adhivuttha-devatā, Ja VI 370,14-25; ba-
hi-nagare tale adhivattho Dīghatālo (or Dīghataphalo)
nāma yakkho, Ps III 422,1 = Ss 103,10; Ap 530,6
= Thī-a 144,18* (upassayâ°, v. l. °vutthā). — (b) in-
habited by (ifc ) Ja V 416,22** (°kaṇerusaṁghâ°);
V 420,9** (°tāpasa-gaṇâ°, cf. ib. 422,32'). — 2. (from
adhivāseti [cf. paññatta to paññapeti, etc.], generally
adhivuttha), (a) who has received an invitation and
accepted it (with object bhattaṁ); Vin I 232,25 (adhi-
vuttho'mhi . . . Ambapāliyā gaṇikāya bhattaṁ, cf.
DN II 97,14 below); — (b) do. in a passive sense;
~o me vassāvāso, MN II 50,27 (/ consent to spend
the rainy season (there)); ~aṁ ca pana samaṇena
Gotamena (scil. bhattaṁ), MN II 92,5; ~aṁ kho me
. . . Ambapāliyā gaṇīkāya bhattaṁ, DN II 97,14 (cf.
Vin I 232,25); DN I 226,1 (adhi-vatthaṁ); ~aṁ mayā
. . . bhattaṁ, Dhp-a III 469,5. Cf. adhi-vāsita.

adhi-vasati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. adhi + √vas, cf. ajjhā-
vasati], to dwell, inhabit (acc); vihāram ~ati, Rūp
287; Sadd 717,11; gāmaṁ ~ati, Pay fol. gai v. 7;
pp. adhivattha (adhivuttha), q. v.; caus. adhivāseti,
q. v.adhi-vasati

1adhi-vāsa, m. (cf. adhivāseti), acquiescence,
holding out; Abh 958 (sampaṭicchane); — ifc. v.
khudâ°, dur-°. Cf. adhivāsaka, adhivāsana.

adhi-vāsaka, mfn. (from adhivāseti), enduring,
patient; Ja IV 77,1' (parehi vuttānaṁ duṭṭha-vaca-
nānaṁ ~o; — 'khantā duruttānaṁ'). — °-jātika,
mfn. (in Mss. often spelt adhi-vāsika°), enduring or
patient by nature; uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanā-
adhi-vāsaka= III 97,27 = 137,2 = AN II 118,3 = III 163,34
= 389,12 = V 132,12. — Ifc. v. an-°.

adhi-vāsana, n. = adhi-vāsanā, Ja IV 77,6'
(gender influenced by sotthānaṁ ib.). — °-khanti,
f., patient endurance; Ja II 237,5'; III 263,20' (~iyā
samannāgato, = 'akkodhano'); V 174,32' (o: khanti-
pāramī); Ps II 99,22 (~iyaṁ ṭhito); Ud-a 263,11;
°-bala-vibhāvanaṁ udānaṁ, Ud-a 262,31 (ad Ud
45,30*). — °-tā, f. abstr., Dhs 1341 (khanti khama-
natā + ; As 396,1). — °-viriya, n., energetic endur-
ance; Ja V 174,31' (ɔ: viriya-pāramī)— Ifc. v. an-°,
īsam-°.adhi-vāsana

adhi-vāsanā, f. (from adhivāseti; cf. 1adhivasa
& Buddh, sa. adhivāsanā); (a), consent, assent, accept-
ance; Vin II 104,5 (kammassa kiriyā karaṇaṁ upaga-
manaṁ ajjhupagamanaṁ+); Ap 39,15 '~aṁ aññāya);
305,25 (do.); MN I 236,15 (~aṁ viditvā); II 63,9 (do.);
Dhp-a I 33,10; Mhv XXX,2; AN III 31,15 (°-kālo);
— (b), endurance; acc. ~ aṁ sotthānaṁ (split comp.),
Ja IV 76,1* ≠ Mvu I 285,1*; instr., abl. ~ā, MN I
7,13; 10,24-33 (dassanā+ . . . pahātabbā, scil. āsavā)
= AN III 387,23 ≠ 389,6; ~āya, AN III 387,23
(~āya pahīnā) ≠ 389,6.

adhi-vāsayati, pr. 3 sg., see adhi-vāseti.
adhi-vāsāpeti, pr. 3 sg. (caus. of adhi-vāseti (a)),
to cause (or ask) someone to stay or wait; 2 sg. ~esi.
Ja I 254,22 (amhe aññaṁ saṁvaccharaṁ); /nf.~etuṁ,
Ja V 200,18 (yāva pitu āgamanā).

adhi-vāsita, mfn. (pp. of adhivāseti (b)) = adhi-
vattha (adhi-vuttha) 2 b: accepted (said of an in-
vitation); Dhp-a III 470,12 (satthārā Cūḷasubhaddāya
nimantanaṁ ~aṁ).

adhi-vāseti, pr. 3 sg. (caus. of adhi-vasati, cf.
adhivāsana; for Ct.-analysis see As 395,31), (a) to
wait; (b)[prob, originating with the polite imper. ~ehi,
"suffer"] to consent (esp. to accept an invitation [to,
acc.]), to agree or grant; (c) to have patience (often
with a neg. part, as avihaññamāno), to bear, endure
(acc); to pardon; to give in; — pr. 3 sg. ~eti
adhi-vāsetiUd-a (c)); do. DN II 99,5 (sato sampajāno ~ avi-
haññamāno, ≠ 128,1, aor. ~esi) = SN I 28,3 (c);
~eti na-ppajahati na vinodeti, MN I 453,9 = SN IV
76,27 = It 115,14 (c); nâdhivāseti pajahati vino-
deti, MN I 11,12 (c); sarikhāy' ekam ~eti, DN III
224,21 = MN I 464,14 (c); — 2 sg. ~esi (ç), Ja II
386,10' (= 'titikkhasi'); — 3 pl. ~enti (c), DN II
158,3; — part. m. ~ento, Ud 21,7 (vedanaṁ, —
upari vāsento (cf. As 395,31) sahanto khamanto, Ud-a
(c)); °-vāsayanto (khudaṁ pipāsaṁ), Ja IV 330,5* (c);
an-adhivāsento, Ja IV 235,19* (b or c); gen. ~en-
tassa (mahādukkhaṁ), Ja I 46,20 (c); ~ayato (an°),
MN I 10,31 (c); pl. ~ayantā (an°, or n'adhiv°), Vv
961 (pipāsaṁ; = ~etuṁ asakkontā, Vv-a (c)); part.
med. øen.~ayamānassa, Ps II 227,11 (kakacôk(k)anta-
naṁ, c); — imper. 3 sg. ~etu me (bhante Bhagavā, etc)
svātanāya bhattaṁ (b, generally followed by aor. ~esi
kho Bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena), DN I 109,23 (= sam-
paṭicchatu, Sv, ɔ: sādiyatu, pt); 226,2; II 97,12; MN
I 236,12; II 50,1; Vin I 17,28; Sn p. 103,24; ~etu no
bhante Bh. āvasathâgāraṁ, DN II 84,19 (b); ~etu me
bhante Bh. Bārāṇasiyaṁ vassâvāsaṁ, MN II 50,24 (b);
— 2 sg. ~ehi tāva (a), Dhp-a II 191,17; Ja III 277,6;
~ehi svātanāya bhattaṁ (b), MN II 63,5; Dhp-a I
33,8; — 3 pi. ~entu (bhattaṁ), SN IV 289,5 (b); —
2 pl. ~etha (a), Ja I 254,20; thokaṁ ~, Ja VI 588,6;
Dhp-a I 197,1; (b) Pv-a 17,8; — pot. 3 sg. °-vāsaye
(c), Ud 45,30* (~ aduṭṭhacitto; = adhivāsana-khan-
tiyaṁ ṭhatvā khameyya, Ud-a); °-vāsaye (phuṭṭho
ḍaṁsehi. . tatra), Th 31 = 244 (c) (= saheyya, Ct.);
°-vāsayeyya (sītaṁ accuṇhaṁ), Sn 966; Ja III 205,11*
(asocamāno ~) (c); °-vāseyya, DN II 115,33 (b or c);
— 2 pl. °-vāseyyātha (nâdhi°), MN I 129,27 = II
251,23 (c); — aor. 3 sg ~esi (b) Ap 39,14; Vin I
17,30 (tuṇhībhāvena); DN I 109,24; MN I 236,13;
II 63,1; Pv-a 17,8, etc. (cf. above imper. 3 sg.
~etu); — 3 pl. ~esuṁ (b), SN IV 289,1 (bhattaṁ);
— fut. 1 sg. °vāsessāmi, Ja IV 279,4 (a); — inf.
~etuṁ, Vv-a 337,1 (c); — abs. ~etvā, Ja II 352,18
(dve sāvanā, a); III 281,3 (dve tayo pahāre, c); IV
407,17 (vedanaṁ, c); V 51,25 (do.); —grd.n.~etabbaṁ,
Ja VI 288,20 (a); Mil 94,12 (chiddaṁ disvā ~, c); —
pp. adhivāsita (q. v.), adhivattha (adhivuttha), cf.
cudita: codita, Buddh, sa. rupta: ropita, etc.

adhi-vāha, mfn. (adhi + √vah; cf. sa. abhi-
vahati), carrying, bringing; only ifc. v. dukkhâ°,
sukhâ°.

adhi-vāhana, mf(-l)n. = prec.; taṁ [scil.
yogakkhemaṁ] adhikatvā vāhiyyati, abhimukhaṁ
vāhiyyatī ti ~aṁ, Pj II 150,1. — Ifc. v. papafica-
saṁghāṭa-du(k)khâ°, yogakkhemâ°.

adhi-vinnā, f., a chief wtfe(?), MTD (cf. sa. id.
with different meaning & adhi-vedana below).

adhi-vimutti, ind. concerning, with regard to
the vimutti (q. v.); DN I 174,34 (Ee adhi-mutti; but
see Sv (II) 360,3). — °-tā, f. abstr., ifc. v. kāmâ°.

adhi-vutti-pada, n. [cf. adhi-vacana, °vutti re-
presenting sa. ukti (√vac); orig, used paronomastically
as a verbal noun to abhi-vadati (see Sn 891)], (point(s)
of) theory, dogma, anekavihitāni ~āni abhivadanti,
adhi-vutti-padavacanapadāni, (b) as *adhi + vṛtti: "abhibhavitvā
. . . vattanato"); 30,5 foll. - MN II 228,13 (Ps = Sv)
= 233,ø; — tesaṁ tesaṁ ~ānaṁ abhiññā sacchi-
kiriyāya, AN V 36,25 (Ee adhi-mutti°; Mp ≠ Sv).

adhi-sakkāra, m., excellent honour; Dhp-a I
111,23 (C*», blending of adhikāra and sakkāra, Ed.
adhikāraṁ; cf. Dhp-a2 (I) 94 n. 1; Gp seems to favour
adhikāra).

adhi-samuppanna-nāma, n. (pp. of adhi-sam-
ut-√pad + nāma(n)), a term whose meaning does not
agree with the literal meaning of it; opp. anvattha-
nāma (q. v.), quoted by Tr. only from the Burmese
Atthasālinī (Westergaard, Cat. p. 106b), ɔ: adhicca-
samuppanna (?).adhi-samuppanna-nāma

adhi-sayana, mfn. [ts., cf. 1adhiseti], lying or
sleeping on; f. ~ā (mañcaṁ viya), Pv-a 80,25 (so
CeEe; ɔ: adhisayānā, part. med.?).

adhi-sayita, mfn. (pp. of 1adhi-seti), (a) active:
lying upon (with acc, e.g. bed, eggs); Mogg-v V 59
(~o khaṭopikaṁ bhavaṁ); Ps II 193,28 (migassa . . .
pāsarāsiṁ °-kālo); — (b) passive: occupied (by a
person lying), brooded (by a hen); Mogg-v V 59 (~ā
adhi-sayitaditāni paribhāvitāni (scil. aṇḍāni), Vin III 3,32 (Sp:
tāya janettiyā kukkuṭiyā pakkhe pasāretvā tesaṁ
upari sayantiyā sammā ~āni) — MN I 104,4 (Ps =
Sp) = SN III 153,15 (Spk do.) = AN IV 125,21
, (Mp do.); ~aṁ dhanaṁ (nāgena), Ps II 128,19-20.

(adhi-sarati), pr. 3 sg. (adhi + √sṛ), to over-
power; pot. 3 sg. mā te ādhisare †mucca (ɔ: muccha?
the gloss patitthayatu meaning prob, patiṭṭhīyatu
(Tr)), Ja V 117,5* (so read with B. for avisare, Cks);
abs. ~itvā, ib. 119,2' (Cks avisaritvā; = atikka-
mitvā pavatte paresaṁ akusala-dhamme[su], taking
adhisara as a noun).

adhi-sallikhati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi-saṁ + √likh),
to lay too much strain upon (abstinence); MN I 449,12
(~t'evâyaṁ samaṇo — atisallekhati, ativāyāmaṁ
karoti, Ps) = AN I 236,30 foll. (= ativiya salle-
khati (Ee sallikh°), ativiya sallikhitaṁ katvā saṇha-
saṇhaṁ kathetîti attho, Mp). Cf. Sadd 330,19.

adhi-sīla, n., 'higher conduct' (origin as adhi-
citta); Sp I 244,2; Sadd 752,28. — adhisīlaṁ, ind.,
as to the moral conduct; DN I 174,18 (yad-idaṁ ~aṁ
+ adhijegucchaṁ. . . adhipaññaṁ . . . adhi(vi)mutti);
AN I 230,27 (~aṁ sikkhissasi); 236,8* (~aṁ adhi-
cittaṁ ca adhipaññaṁ ca viriyavā). — adhisīle,
ind. id. (cf. ajjhāgāre); ~ sīlavipanno (paron.) Vin
I 63,33 = 67,8 = 114,24; ~e adhicitte adhipañ-
ñāya, Vin I 70,16; AN III 106,1 (na sakkhissanti
adhi-sīlasee Mp II 378,1); mama sāvakā ~e sambhāventi,
MN II 9,15; ~e sampavattā hoti, AN III 133,1; ~e
samādapeti, AN III 263,28 (v. l. ~esu; Mp: adhisīlesu
= pañcasu sīlesu); ~e [+ adhicitte, adhipaññāya]
samādapetuṁ, A NV 73,15. — °-pūraṇa, mfn., ful-
filling the moral precepts; Ps II 403,1 (so Ck; Ce Ee Se
asithila-pūrako). — °-sikkhā, f. (& °-sikkhā-samā-
dāna, n.), (undertaking of) moral training, see pas-
sages quoted s. v. adhi-citta-sikkhā above.

Adhisīla, m. Npr. of the chief pupil of Anoma-
dassi-thera at Sudhammapura; Sās 60,16.

2adhi-seti (or adhi-sayati), pr. 3 sg. (adhi +
√çī), to lie in or on (acc. or loc); pot. 3 sg. °-sayeyya
(pāsa-rāsiṁ), MN I 173,81; 174,1; fut. 3 sg. °-sessati
(paṭhaviṁ), Dhp 41 (= paṭhaviyā upari sayissati,
Dhp-a) quoted Sadd 717,13; Pay fol. gr 7 (paṭhavi-
2adhi-setiadhi, cf. Sadd 882,29); pp. °-sayita, mfn. (q.v.).

2adhi-seti, pr. 3 sg. (adhi + √çri), to take refuge
or recourse to (acc); yañ-ñaṁ disataṁ ~, Sn 671 (Pj
= gacchati, giving as v. r. abhiseti = allīyati, apas-
sayati).
adhi-harati, pr. 3 sg., v. l. for abhi-harati (q. v.).

adhīta, mfn. [ts. pp. of adhīyati], (a) learnt,
studied; ~o uggahīto, Sp-ṭ ad Sp I 7,15 (= 'pariyatto').
— (b) learned (in veda); Ap 411,13 (~ā vedagū sabbe).

adhīna, mfn. [ts.], subject to, belonging to, depen-
dent on (loc); Abh 728; Sv I 212,26 = Ps II 318,1
(na attani ~o, = 'anattâdhīno'); Sv I 212,28 (paresu
~o, = 'parâdhīno'); yaṁ khalu dhammam ādhīnaṁ
adhīnanaṁ vase vattati), Ja V 350,16*. — Ifc v. attâ°,
anaññâ°, anattâ°, aparâ°, dhammasaṁghâ°,
parâ°, Buddha°, Sâ°, Sīhaḷâ°.

[Adhīnasattu, suggested by Tr. for Adīnasattu,
Ja V 26,1'.]

adhīyati, pr. 3 sg. (adhi + √i, sa. adhyeti &
ved. adhīyati; in Mss. also spelt adhiyati or adhiyyati),
lit. 'enter into, take possession of (cf. adhi-gacchati):
to read, study, understand, esp. to learn by heart
(acc); ~īyati, Ja III 28,22* (dhammaṁ; opp. sajjhā-
adhīyatiopp. vāceti); Mil 164,2 (vijjaṁ); 2 sg. nâdhīyasi bhik-
khuhi saṁvasanto, SN I 202,29* (= na sajjhāyasi,
nâdiyasī [ - - ˇ - ] ti vā pāṭho, Spk); 1 sg. ~īyāmi,
Ap 343,1 (mante); 3 pl. ~īyanti, Ja VI 458,24* (metr.:
adhĭyanti ve mahārāja = sa. adhi + yanti,
cf. ajjheti) quoted Sadd 322,30; 3 sg. med. ~īte
(vyākaraṇaṁ), Sadd 883,2; Pay fol. gr 7 (given as
ex. of the sense 'ajjhayane' of prp. adhi); Sadd
m,23 ≠ Mogg III 2 (sâggi ~); 2 sg. med. ~īyase,
Ja VI 458,19* (dibbaṁ~ māyaṁ); — part. gen. ~īyan-
tassa, Vin I 270,9 (satta me vassāni ~); part. med.
~īyamāno (mante), AN III 224,21. (quoted Pj II
316,14; = vede sajjhāyanto gaṇhanto, Mp); —
imper. 2 sg. med., ~īyassu, Dhp-a III 446,1 (tassa
santikaṁ gantvā~); — pot. 3 sg. med. ~īyetha, Ja III
218,26* (sabbaṁ sutaṁ); — inf. ~īyituṁ, Ps III
478,10 ad MN III 1,12 (tayo pi vedā na sakkā
ekadivasena ~); adhīyitu-kāma, mfn., wishing to
learn (mante), DN I 114,13 ≠ 130,23 (codd. adhiy°);
— abs. (a ) adhicca (q.v.); (b ) ~īyitvā, DN I 96,6
(mante); AN III 224,23 (do.); Ja IV 75,13' (suta-
pariyattiṁ); V 10,19' (paṭiggahetvā ~); (c) adhīyâ-
naṁ, Ja V 450,14*; 451,9' (= sajjhāyitvā); — pp.
adhīta, mfn. (q.v.); — grd. ~īyitabba, mfn., Ja III
219,8' (sabbaṁ ~aṁ). — Cf. ajjhāyati & 1ajjheti.

adhîrita, mfn. (pp. of adhi + √īr), uttered, pro-
nounced; Kacc-v 46 (given as ex. of adhi before the
vowels i, ī); Sadd 619,10. Cf. abbhīrita.

a-dhuttī, f. (sa. a + dhūrta, f.), not depraved;
~ī + athenī asoṇḍī avināsikā, AN IV 266,6 = 268,24
= 270,16; pl. ~í + do., AN III 38,8 (Mp: purisa-
dhutta-surādhuttatā-vasena ~iyo).

adhunā, ind. [ts.; Kacc 235], (just) now, lately,
recently, newly; Ud-a 379,18 (= 'idāni'); 402,29 (do.);
Ja III 181,8'; Dāṭh II 94. In comp.s with pp.:
°-kārita, mfn., newly built; Ps ad MN I 353,20
(= 'nava'); — °-kālakata, mfn., just deceased; DN
III 117,5 (~o, scil. Nigaṇṭho Nāthaputto; = sampati
adhunāputto) — Vin II 185,23 (°-kālaṁkato); AN IV 75,25
(Tisso bhikkhu); — °-âgata, mfn., newly arrived
(to, acc.); nava, acirapabbajita + (followed by acc.
imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ): MN I 457,32; SN III 91,16;
AN III 138,12; Vin I 40,20 ≠ Dhp-a I 92,11; Th-a
ad Th 552 (= 'ajjatana'); °-vadhukā-samena cetasā
viharissāmi, with the same mind as a newly arrived
daughter-in-law, AN II 78,34 (the simile styled adhunâ-
gata-vadhukôpammaṁ, Mp); — °-âbhisitta, mfn.,
just anointed (king, rajjena), DN II 210,24 (= sam-
pati abhisitto, Sv); 227,2; — adhun'-utthita, mfn.,
just arisen; Mil 155,10 (~ena Mārena); — adhunū-
papanna, mfn., recently reborn (in, acc); pl. ~â,
DN II 208,1 ≠ 221,9 (so read with v. l. 221, n. 3
for adhunuppannā).

a-dhurā, f., 'not a place of honour i. e. a mean or
unprofitable work; loc. ~āyaṁ niyuñjati, Ja IV 241,3*
(= saddhādhura-sīladhura-paññādhuresu a-yojetvā
a-yoge niyuñjati, Ct.), quoted Pj I 127,27*.

a-dhūpana, mfn., without (seasoning by means
of) fumigation; Ja III 144,1 (aloṇena ~ena udakena
sinna-pannena, cf. ib. 21 and a-lona-dhūpana, Ja IV
236,27). 'a-dhūpana

adho, ind. [sa. adhas], (a) below, down, down-
wards (opp. uddhaṁ); Abh 1156; with gen. or in
comp.s according to Mogg III 8 (= Pay: adho-
Gaṅgaṁ or adho Gaṅgāya; cf. adho-Gaṅgaṁ below);
uddhaṁ kātuṁ na pana adho (scil. telaṁ), Ud 14,10
(= heṭṭhā, Ud-a); ~ gaccha bho sappi-tela, SN
adhouddham adho ācamayamāno, Mil 152,17 (cf. adho-
virecana); gantā so nirayaṁ ~, Ja V 267,19*; 270,12*
(cf. 273,12'); patanti nirayaṁ ~, Ja VI 224,24*;
~ kesamatthakā (abl. downwards from) Thī 33 ≠ DN
II 293,11. (= kesaggato hetthā, Vism 240,30) =
MN I 57,14 = III 90,13 = Vibh 193,18 (Vibh-a
= Vism); akkhakato paṭṭhāya ~, Sp (III) 549,9 ad
Vin III 129,36'(= 'adli'-akkhakaṁ'); akkhakānaṁ ~,
Sp ad Vin IV 214,18' (do.); — (b) (a) denoting one
of the ten dimensions (disā), viz. nadir (uddhaṁ de-
noting zenith), or (β) opp. to uddhaṁ and tiriyaṁ:
Sn 1122 (disā catasso, vidisā catasso, uddhaṁ adho,
dasa disatā imāyo); SN I 122,17* (uddham adho ca
tiriyaṁ (ca)); 122,1 = III 124,4 (gacchati purimaṁ
disaṁ, etc.); Ud-a 178,20 (puratthimā disā +); in
connection with the appamañña exercises: uddhaṁ
adho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi . . . mettā-sahagatena cetasā
. . . pharitvā, DN II 186,30 = MN II 76,9 = SN V
115,29 (quoted Vism 308,1, - heṭṭhā, ib. 23) ≠ DN
I 153,20; paṭhavīkasiṇaṁ eko sañjānāti uddhaṁ
adho tiriyaṁ advayaṁ appamāṇaṁ, DN III 268,21
(= heṭṭhā bhūmitalâbhimukhaṁ, Sv = Vism 176,31)
= AN V 60,17; uddhaṁ ~ ca tiriyañ câpi majjhe,
Sn 537 = 1055 = 1068 = 1103; yathā ~ tathā

avayava, with (haplol.) loss of one -va, = "in whom

taṇhâvassuti-abhāvena ~o, Ct.); MN III 221,11 (~o
ca viharati sato sampajāno; = patigha-avassavena

262,6 (kāyakammaṁ ~ aṁ; quoted As 68,32); IV
228,12* (sadā sato viharetha ~o); Ud-a 306,28 (kiie-
sehi ~o parisuddha-sīlo samāhito). — °-citta, mfn.,
whose mind is free from defilement; gen. ~assa,

tassa, Dhp-a). — °-pariyāya, m., a discourse

an-avasitta, mfn., not overflown, not bespattered,

an-avasīdana, n., 'not sinking down', non-ex-
haustion, activity, energy; kăyassa ~aṁ, Pj II 122,14.

an-avaseka, mfn., not overflowing; samatitthikaṁ
~aṁ telapattaṁ yathā parihareyya, Ja I 400,1* (so

sesakaṁ; — an-avasiñcanakaṁ a-parissavanakaṁ),
quoted Nidd I 471,18* (w. r. an-avasesaṁ; = an-
avasiñcanakam a-parisiñcanakaṁ, Ct.) and Ja III
an-avaseka

plete, altogether, or of which nothing is left, all done

an-assaya, mfn. [sa. an-āçraya], without sup-

an-assavi(n), mfn., [(a) without discharge, not
inflamed (said of wounds); m. ~ī (vaṇo), MN II

Sn 853 (sātiyesu ~ī; = sāta-vatthusu kāmaguṇesu

an-assāsaka, mfn., who cannot recover his

a-nahāta, mfn. [sa. a-snāta], not bathed; m. ~o,

— [(b) the nibbāna; a mistake in SN IV 368,24 (Ee

anta-guṇamhṭ] bandhanaṁ); 358,17 (antantare ekavīsati bhoge

space: Abh 771; Ja V 197,17* (ūrunaṁ ~asmim);
320,9 (caturaṅgula-mattena ~am asamphusantaṁ;

— (b) of time: It 121,22 (etasmiṁ ~e); Pv-a 5,2 (do.);

352,12* (ñātisaṁghassa-m-antaraṁ; = chiddaṁ, Ct.

— ifc. v. addhakosa°, an-°, antar-°, abbh-°, ara°,
ekadivasa°, kaṭṭha°, kaṇṇacchidda°, kamma°,

jana°, nir-°, pakkha°, pada°, pabbata°, pāda°,
pāsāṇa°, puppha°, purisa°, phalaka°, Buddha°,
musala-m-°, mūla°, meṇda°, rāja°, rukkha°,

raṁ) ko jāneyya aññatra Tathāgatena, AN III

maya°; — or even (a) 'species', 'kind', see:
khaga°, turiya°, duma°, bhājana°, bhāsa°,
maṇimutta°,' miga°, moha° (Sn 478), rukkha°,

āyatana°, indriya°, khandha°, citta°, dhamma°,

ṭivattuṁ na sakkomi, Ja V 351,8* (= antare

antaraṁPp-a 231,24 (do.) = Sv (II) 355,5 = Mp II 384,20

Abhidh-k-vy, Trsl. Ill 181, n. í], one of the (64) subdivi-

antara-khajjakapetvā). — °-velā, f., Mhv-ṭ ad Mhv XXIX 27.

ghāṭakaṁ gharaṁ; cf. Vin-vn 1830—34); 186,8**
foll. (~e gamissāmi; quoted Spk II 34,30); 189,27**
(na pallatthikāya ~e nisīdissāmi (b), quoted Spk
I 134,29, cf. MN III 126,16); 199,15** (~e chiuMes-
sāmi, scil. patta-dhovanaṁ); bhattagge + ~e, Vin
I 341,1(6) ≠ II 179,25 foll.; Vin I 40,5 (~aṁ pa-
viṭṭho piṇḍāya carati (a)) = Dhp-a I 91,21; Vin II
213,1 (saṁghāṭiṁ ottharitvā ~e nisīdanti (b)); Ud
7,21 (~aṁ paviṭṭho . . . piṇḍāya (a); Ud-a: antara-
vīthiyaṁ); Nidd I 366,8 (~aṁ paviṭṭho vīthiṁ paṭi-
panno; = ummārabbhantaraṁ, Nidd-a (!)); MN II
7,31 (~aṁ paviṭṭhā; = indakhīlato paṭṭhāya, Ps
(a)); 137,25 (~aṁ pavisanto; = gharummārato
paṭṭhāya, Ps (b)); III 126,16 (~e nisīditā (b); =
nibbodaka-patana-ṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya, Ps Ck [Se & Ce
v. l. nimbodaka-]); SN II 19,12 (~aṁ pavitth'amha;
= indakhīlato paṭṭhāya antogāme, Spk) ≠ Mil
11,24; SN III 121,13 (kathaṁ . . . mādiso ~e kālaṁ
kattabbaṁ maññeyya (b)); AN V 201,17 (susaṁ-
vuto ~e pi nisajjāya; cf. Vin IV 186,19**).

antaraghara-ppavesana, n., entering into the
houses; Pj I 242,11 (saṁgha-gaṇa-° + °~esu).

antaraghara-saṁyutta, mfn., related to a°;
Utt-vn 611 (~ā sekkhapaññattiyo [metr. antarā-gh°?];
cf. Vin IV 186,8** foll).

antaraṅga, n. [sa. antar-aṅga], an essential part
(ɔ : part of a word-stem); — °-tta, n. abstr. [sa. an-
taraṅgatva]; Mogg-v II 117. — °-dhura, (n), 'office
of the Interior', a certain department of state; Mhv
LXIX 32—35 (Trsl.; cf. EZ III 145,3).

antara-cakka, n. [sa. antara-cakra], name of a
certain science, a branch of astrology or augury; Mil
178,22 (sā-cakkaṁ miga-cakkaṁ +). Cf. Bṛhat-Sam-
hitā ch. 87 ('tt[ī/i]e Compass divided into different parts',
Trsl).

antara-cara, m(fn.), moving inwardly; SN IV
173,18—174,30 (~o vadhako ['a domestic foe'] uk-
khittâsiko); = abbhantara-caro, Spk, cf. ib. dahara-
kālato paṭṭhāya . . . sambaddhaṁ ~aṁ). Cf. antarā-
vadhaka.

antaraṭṭālaka, m. (2antara + aṭṭālaka), an inter-
mediate (small) watch-tower; acc. pl. ~e, Ja VI 390,2.

antaraṭṭhaka, mfn. (from 3antar(a) + aṭṭhakā,
q. v.), occurring between the 'eights' (i. e. the aṭṭhakā
days); ~o himapāta-samayo, the time of snowfall
between the aṭṭhakā, AN I 136,31 (Mp II 225,6 takes
a° as a subst, m. = māgha-phagguṇānaṁ antare aṭṭha-
antaraṭṭhaka6,14 (Ud-a) ≠ Vin I 31,35 sitāsu ḥemantikāsu rattisu
~āsu himapātasamaye, supported by Sp-ṭ against
Tr. MN I 536,21); rattiyo sītā hemantikā "~ā, MN
I 79,25 (p. L; quoted Mil 396,4, reading °ṭṭhake) ≠
Vin I 288,6 (cf. also Ps II 48,10 on MN I 79,25); Ja
I 390,21 (himavāta-samaye ~e; read himapāta-s°).

antarato, ind. (abl. of antara), from within, in-
wardly; yass' ~ na santi kopā, Sn 6 (= yassa citte
na santi kopā, Pj) ≠ Vin II 184,27* = Ud 20,4*
(= abbhantare attano citte, Ud-a, cf. 2antara B 2),
quoted Ud-a 109,29; bhayam ~ jātaṁ, AN IV 96,21*
(= abbhantare uppannaṁ, Mp; quoted Pj II 20,15*)
≠ It 83,23*; 84,11*, 23*.

antara-dvāre, ind. (3antara + dvāra, loc.),
within the gate, between the gates; Ps II 15,24; Ja I
308,27 (= vāsal-aturehi, Ja-pot) = Dhp-a III 317,15
(— vāsal-bada-dī, Rt); Ja V 231,23 (w. r. anan-
tara-°; = mahādvārassa ca cūḷadvārassa ca majjḥe,
pt); ib. 28 (v. l. dvārantare, B* & Se).

antara-dīpa, m., an island amidst a river; Pj II
27,4 (Mahāmahī bhijjitvā . . . ~aṁ akāsi); 581,6
(yattha Godhāvarī dvidhā bhijjitvā . . . ~aṁ akāsi);
°-vāsi(n), mfn., living there; Ja IV 472,21'.

antara-dīpaka, m. (a ) = prec, dimin.; Mp II
253,31 (nadīnaṁ duggamaṭṭhānaṁ ~aṁ, in a river);
Dhp-a III 137,1 (~aṁ pavisiṁsu, v. l. anantara°);
(b) loc. ~e, on a little island, Ja I 240,11 (in the sea);
III 133,11 (in a river).

antara-dhāna, n. [sa. antar-dhāna; cf. antarā-
dhāna below], verbal noun of antara-dhāyati: °-nidassa-
naṁ, Ud-a 171,20, (a) (sudden) disappearance, vanishing,
passing away (from one existence into another); cf. Abh
51; Vin III 8,10 (Buddhānaṁ ~ena; = khandhantara-
antara-dhāna~ena); DN III 122,2 (atha nesaṁ satthuno ~aṁ hoti);
MN I 49,24 (cuti cavanatā bhedo ~aṁ maccu mara-
ṇaṁ kālakiriyā) ≠ III 249,24 ≠ Nidd I 124,1 (Nidd-a);
Nidd-a (Ee) I 67,19 (~āya; = 'antarāyāya'); Dhs
645 (rūpassa khayo vayo bhedo paribhedo aniccatā
~aṁ; As: antaradhāyati etthāti~aṁ) — 738 = 872;
Mil 126,1 (cakkhūnaṁ ~aṁ); — (b) (successive) decline
or decadence; saddhammassa ~aṁ, SN II 224,10; Mil
131,27; saddhammassa sammosāya ~āya saṁvattati,
SN II 224,30 ≠ AN I 17,34 ≠ 59,4 ≠ II 147,19
foll. ≠ III 176,18 foll.; the disappearance of Buddhism
is prophesied to traverse five stages of decline: pañca
~āni, Mp I 87,3 = the prose Anāg, quoted JPTS
1886 p. 34,19 (scil. adhigama-°, paṭipatti-°, pariyatti-°,
liṅga°, dhātu-antaradhānaṁ) ≠ Ss 22,30 (here: pari-
yatti-°, paṭipatti-°, paṭivedha-°, liṅga°, dhātu-°); the
holy doctrine expires in three stages, tīṇi ~āni (i. e.
tīṇi sāsanantaradhānāni), Mil (133,29-)134,5 (scil.
adhigama°, paṭipatti°, liṅga°); do. Vibh-a 431,27
(scil. pariyatti-°, paṭivedha-°, paṭipatti-°); Spk II
202,13 foll. — Ifc. v. adhigama°, an-°, khandha°,
candâbha°, dhātu-°, paṭipatti-°, paṭivedha°, pa-
riyatti-°, liṅga°, saddhamma°, sāsana°.

antaradhāna-manta, m., a charm by which
something is made to disappear; Dhp-a IV 191,8
(ābhāya ~).

antara-dhāpanā, f. (verbal noun from next);
As 163,30 (= 2'vibhāvanā'); Sadd 81,12 (do.).

antara-dhāpeti, pr. 3 sg. (caus. of antara-
dhāyati), to cause to disappear, to destroy; + vūpa-
sameti, Vin III 70,24 (megho . . . rajojallaṁ; = adas-
sanaṁ neti, Sp) = SN V 50,8 foll; do. (bhikkhu . . .
akusale dhamme), Vin III 70,27 = SN V 51,4 ≠
antara-dhāpeti~āpeti, SN II 224,22 foll.; 3 pl. ~āpenti, AN I 18,25;
19,14; 20,19(opp. ṭhapenti; Mp I 87,2); MhvXXIII 10;
imper. 2 pl. ~āpetha, Ja I 147,28; pot. 3 sg. ~āpeyya,
AN III 394,16 (rajam); 395,8; 1 pl. ~āpeyyāma, Ja
II 415,20; aor. 3 pl. ~āpesuṁ, Vin III 8,13-20 (brahma-
cariyaṁ, i. e. suffered it to disappear; = vināsesuṁ
adassanaṁ nayiṁsu, Sp); abs. ~āpetvā, Ud-a 101,24
(= 'paṭisaṁharitvā'); Pv-a 123,15.

antara-dhāyati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. antar + √dhā,
antar-dhatte ác antar-dhīyate], to disappear, vanish
away (opp. pātu-bhavati); Vin IV 54,24 (with tmesis:
antarâpi dhāyati; — ~āyati pi, adassanam pi gac-
chatī ti attho, Sp) quoted Sadd 481,24; MN III
157,26; Ud-a 80,31; Pv-a 152,22; 245,5; Ps II 3,27*;
Vibh-a 432,13 foll; Mil 134,3; Vv-a 48,3 (v. l. ~āyi);
Abhidh-av 107,8*; with gen. (dat.) pers, (like pātu-
bhavati): MN I 330,2-6 [se also apagacchati], but
according to Grr. with abl. pers., Kacc-v 276 (upajjhā-
yā ~āyati sisso; cf. Sadd 704,24; PāṇI 4,28); other-
wise mostly with loc: Jetavane ~āyati Bhagavā, ib.;
see s. v. antarahita; 1 sg. ~āyāmi, SN I 132,11* =
Thī 232 = Ap 556,21; DN II 109,19 = AN IV 307,27 ;
MN I 330,2; 3 pl. ~āyanti, Nidd I 5,3 (Nidd-a); —
part. med. ~āyamāna, mfn., MN I 445,5 = SN
antara-dhāyatiābhaṁ); neg. part. m. an-antaradhāyamāno, Nidd
II 86,25; — imper. 2 sg. ~āyassu, MN I 330,3;
~āya(?), Ps II 414,5; — pot. 3 sg. ~āyeyya, Mil 98,13;
— aor. 3 sg. ~āyi, Vin I 7,10 = SN I 138,28; DN
III 60,10; MN I 143,20; SN I 1,25; 103,24 (Māro);
211,9 (āloko); 238,16 (Sakko); Ja IV 4,3; Dhp-a I
33,3; 109,26; IV 191,6; Mil 217,29; Mhv XIV,5; 3 sg.
med. (ce ) ~āyatha, Sn 449 (Māro) = SN I 122,24* =
Dhp-a I 433,13* ≠ MN I 338,31*; Vv 924; Pv-a
217,5; (β) ~āyittha, Ud-a 433,6 (= 'na paññāyittha');
3 pl. ~āyisuṁ, Mhv XVIII 34; — fut. 3 sg. ~āyissati,
Vin I 43,21; Ud 45,25; DN II 140,3 = 148,9; 1 sg.
~āyissāmi, MN I 330,5; 3 pl. ~āyissanti, Ja I 119,1
= Dhp-a I 248,11; — inf. ~āyituṁ, MN I 330,6;
~ātuṁ, Nidd-a II 266,1 ad Nidd II 34,33 (~ samatthe
tucchôkāse — 'antalikkhe'; so Ce; Se °dhātusa-
matthe); — abs. ~āya, Ja VI 32,19; — pp. antara-
hita (q. v.); — caus, antara-dhāpeti (q. v.).

antara-dhāyana, n. (from prec), disappearance;
ifc. v. candâbha-° (Dhp-a IV 191,3).

antarantara, ind. [antara + antara], at intervals,
now and then, from time to time, occasionally; Ja I
161,19; II 101,25; III 527,12; V 456,6; VI 5,19 foll.
(alternating with antarantare); Dhp-a II 86,6; III
215,15; 361,2 (opp. paṭipāṭiyā); IV 191,18; Pj II
antarantaraPs I 216,22; — alternately, now. . . now; Ja IV 106,21';
431,23 (~niddāyati e'evapabujjhati ca); Ps II 324,13
(~ ṭhitāsu pi nisinnāsu pi nipajjamānāsu pi). —
antarantarā(-)kathā, f., interrupting speech [always
with opāteti] ts to be written as two words, antaran-
tarā being an adv. to the verb; cf. antarā-kathā, Vin
I 46,21 (na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassa ~ā kathā
opātetabbā; Sp: antarantarā aniṭṭhite tassa vacane);
MN II 10,9 (api nu me sāvakā . . . ~ā kathaṁ opā-
teyyuṁ; Ps: antarantare); 122,4 (mā me bhonto
. . . ~ā kathaṁ opātetha) ≠ Sn p. 107,7 (= MN
ch. 92); MN II 168,23 (brāhmaṇānaṁ ... mantaya-
mānānaṁ ~ā kathaṁ opāteti).

[antarantara, abstracted from the foll. āmreḍita-
cpd.s; see antarantarena].

antarantare, ind. [antare + antare], (a) adv.,
from time to time; Ja I 259,29; VI 6,30 foll. (alter-
nating with antarantarā); Ps (Ee) III 242,6 (= 'an-
tarantarā'); — (b) prp. with gen., inside, in the
middle of; Dhp-a I 59,12 (vanasarhiassa ~ vicarati,
to and fro in . . .; Ck antarantarena); Mp II 268,13
(aññissā kathāya ~ katarā kathā uppajji); [Pj I 57,12
w. r. for ant'-antare ; cf. Vism 358,17 = Vibh-a 62,17].

antarantarena, ind. (instr, formation to prec),
straight through, through the middle of (with gen., cf.
antarantare, b); Dhp-a I 63,6 (bhikkhūnaṁ ~ gantvā);
358,7 (purisānaṁ ~ gacchanti).

antara-parikhā, f., an intermediate ditch (?);
ifc. v. ukkiṇṇa° (mfn., Ja IV 106,16*).

antara-pura, n. [3antara-; cf. sa. antaḥ-pura &
antepura, antopura below], the king's palace; loc.
~asmiṁ, Ja VI 143,25* (āryā-metce; = rāja-nivesa-
nassa antare, Ct.).

antara-bāhira, mfn. (*antara + b°), what is
inside and outside; n. assā ~aṁ (scil. Bārāṇasiyā),
Ja I 125,26; n. pl. ~āni (Bārāṇasī-°), ib. 2 8 (and in
a would-be verse given in Se, missing in Ee; see
antara-bāhirato Ja I 126,5). — Ifc. v. sa° (Ja I 125,21*: Bārāṇasi
santara-bāhiraṁ [ - - | ˇ ˇ - | ˇ ˇ - | ˇ - ]).

antara-bhatta, n., (1) cf. antara-khajjaka; ~aṁ
pacitvā, Pj II 107,5; 117,27; — (2) loc. ɔ: prp. an-
tar(a) + bhatta = antarā-bhatte (q. v.), during the
meal (even before finishing the meal): ekasmiṁ yeva
antara-bhattatarābhatte); III 183,7; Ps I 256,28 = Sv I 188,5
(Ee antarābhatte); ~asmiṁ, Dhp-a IV 12,18. —
°-samaye, loc, during the meal; Ja IV 282,22; Ps II
289,27 (Ee antarā-bh°).

antara-bhogika, m(fn.), a border chief; m. pl.
~ā, Vin III 47,1 (padesa-rājā + ; = dvinnaṁ rājū-
naṁ antarā katipaya-gāma-sāmikā, Sp); Ps( Se) III
681,21; gen. pl. ~ānaṁ javana-dūte pesetvā, ib. 15.

Antara-megiri, m. Npr. of a monastery in
Ceylon; Mhv XXXVIII 48 (Sinh, me = megha? cf.
EZ I p. 161,6 n. 2).

antara-vatthu, n., a court-yard; acc. ~uṁ olo-
kento, Mp I 451,10 (= gehaṅgaṇaṁ, Mp-ṭ); loc.
~umhi, Ja I 232,15-20 (= midul-madhyayehi, Ja-
pot).

antara-vassa, n., the rainy season (= anto-
vassa, q. v.); instr, ten'eva ~ena, during that r. s.,
Vin II 183,20 ≠ Ud 25,25 (= tasmiṁ yeva antara-
vasse, Ud-a); MN III 269,25 = SN IV 63,6; Dhp-a
I 138,10; loc. tatiye ~amhi, Th 128; gen. pl. dvinnaṁ
~ānaṁ ekāvācā me bhāsitā, ib. (= during two r. s.;
antara-vassa§ 222 G a).

antara-vāra, m., a subdivision (of the sacred
texts), opp. mahā-vāra; Ps I 56,3 (catuvīsatiyā ~ehi
paṭimaṇḍetvā).

antara-vāsaka, m. [cf. sa. antar-vāsas, n.\, an
inner garment, esp. the innermost of the three robes of
a Buddhist bhikkhu (or bhikkhunī); Abh 292; Vin I
94,8 (saṁghāṭi, uttarāsaṅgo, ~o) = II 272,11 ≠ V
175,2; 1287,29 (chinnakaṁ~aṁ); 289,35—-290,14 (~o
chiddo hoti); 298,27 (pañca paccayā . . . ~assa nik-
antara-vāsaka(~o temiyati); V 217,27* (nivattho ~ena); Vin-vn
558—9; 2708; Utt-vn 738 (saṁghāṭi pārutā kāye
nivattho ~o); Khuddas III 9; 16; Ap 303,23 (~aṁ);
Vin III 205,35 ≠ Mil 124,23 (~aṁ dhovissāmi);
Sīmāv 27,17. — Ifc. v. dukūla° (Ja IV 219,16).

Antara-vitthi, m. Npr. of a village in Ceylon;
Mhv LX 68 (gāmaṁ ~iṁ); LXX 322 (~imhi).

antara-virahita, mfn., 'without interval', adja-
cent (or next in rank); f. ~ā, Sv (III) 864,3 (= 'anan-
tarā', see an-antara, mfn. above).

antara-vīthi, f., [secondary noun from ~iyaṁ,
~iṁ ɔ: vīthi governed by 3antar(a)- and constructed with
gacchati, paṭipajjati 'in the street, along the street'], the
street; Ja I 340,29 (+ catukka, rājadvāra); acc ~im
olokento, Ja IV 63,28; Dhp-a I 328,2 (olokayamānā);
339,14 (olokayamāno); pāsādā otaritvā ~iṁ paṭi-
antara-vīthigamanaṁ, Ja I 466,23; loc ~iyaṁ (pāsādadvāre),
Ja V 64,24; ~iyaṁ ṭhatvā, Dhp-a III 178,8; Ps II
4,1; Ud-a 88,5 (gacchantaṁ); 89,25 (ṭhitabhāvaṁ);
Pv-a 96,9 (thitako); āmakasusāne ~ saṁkāraṭṭhāne
. . ., Ja I 373,6; + saṁkārakūṭesu, Ps (Se) III 704,8;
loc. pl. ~īsu, ib. i (udakatittha-susāna-saṁkāra-°);
— °-patipanna, mfn., by chance present in the
street, Ja IV 68,5 (cf. V 187,25 above). — Cf. Coo-
maraswamy, Eastern Art, 1931 p. 183.

antara-saṁyojana, n., an inner bond or fetter;
MN III 275,20.

antara-satthi, (ɔ: satthi governed by prp. an-
tar(a), in acc loc), between the thighs; loc. ~imhi
pakkhipitvā (scil. naṅguṭṭhaṁ), Ja V 243,23' (v. l.
°-sakkhimhi); Ps II 316,30 (cf. sīhaseyyā, AN II
245,1-10, and Mp (Se) II 512,8 ≠ quoted Ss 14,14);
vāladhiṁ ~imhi pakkhipitvā, Dhp-a III 185,16; loc.
f. ~iyaṁ khipanto (udakaṁ), Ps II 272,14; loc. pl.
~īsu, Ja I 218,28 (nigrodha-gacchaṁ ~īsu katvā
gacchāmi). Cf. antarā, 2 (a).

Antara-samudda, m.Npr. of a locality; Sp (II)
306,28 (acc ~aṁ); 307,2 (abl. ~ato).

antara-sāṭaka, m., an outer(\) garment; (un-
traced quotation in) Vv-a 166,26 (cf. 2antarā, an-
tarīya).

antara-hita, mfn. (pp. of antara-dhāyati; scanned
like sa. antarhita in two post-canonical passages), va-
nished, disappeared, not present; ifc. covered, hidden;
Ud 45,25 (~o so saddo); Mil 98,15 (do.); DN II 109,20
antara-hitagāthaṁ abhāsiṁ); 487,4 (yā pi me esā bhoto . . . ahu
pasādamattā, sa pi me etarahi ~ā); SN II 274,26
(satthā ~o mahiddhiko mahânubhāvo); AN III 407,8
(kusalā dhammā ~ā); Nidd I 267,11 (attā me ~o);
Dhp-a III 116,13 (idaṁ ~aṁ); Abhidh-av 107,9*
(tasmiṁ ~e, - - ˇ - ); Vibli-a 432,15 (do.); Mil
134.1 (adhigame ~e); Mhv XXVIII 10 (~āya
[ - - ˇ - ˇ ] godhāya); the place from which one
disappears is usually put into loc. (sometimes alter-
nating with abl, cf. abl. pers, with antaradhāyati δc
Kacc-v 276): DN I 222,16 (Brahmaloke ~o) ≠ Ud-a
82,30 (Brahmalokā, v. l. ~e); MN II 79,14 (Tāvatiṁ-
sesu ~o); Ja VI 84,9* (sa devatā ~ā [ɔ: sa devat'
ant°: - - ˇ - ˇ ˇ ˇ - ] pabbate Gandhamādane);
Vin I 230,19 (orimatīre ~o) = DN II 89,19 = Ud
90,8 (orimatīrā, abl.); Mil 18,27 (Asokârāme ~o);
Kacc-v 276 (Jetavane ~o Bhagavā, quoted from
Ud 22,23, cf. ih. 23,10); [~āya bhūmiyā, As 214,27
ts w. r. for anantarahitāya bh°]. — Ifc. v. an-°.

1antarā, ind. [ts.], 1. adv. (a) inside; Vin III
149,13** (= abbhantarimena mānena, Sp); — (b) mid-
way, on the way (ɔ: before reaching the goal); Abh
1150; Vin I 106,24 (~âpi parivasanti); Dhp 237
(vāso pi ca te n'atthi ~; Dhp-a); antarā (y)eva,
Pj & Nidd ad Sn 1120 (= 'antarāya', q. v.); Ja
IV 429,4* (~ yeva sīdati); Ja I 114,31 (~ va nip-
phannaṁ) = Dhp-a I 241,3; Ja IV 213,14 (~ va vi-
nassissatha); Ps (Se) III 470,16 (~ na tiṭṭhati); Pj
I 164,6 (~ yojane yojane vāsetvā); Sv (III) 861,14
(~ a-ṭṭhapitāya, nirantaraṁ pavattāya; = 'a-pari-
punnāya'); — (c) of time: in the meantime; Sn 291;
Vin II 43,18; SN V 50,23 foll. (antarā yeva); Ja IV
441,20*; Ud-a 92,28 (~ ti vacanam pana vikappan-
tara-dīpanaṁ); Ps II 94,12; Sv I 164,17 = Ps (Ee) III
232,17 (soCeEe; Se antarāmagge); Spk II 278,1; Mp
(Se) III 17,16; — (d) do. beforehand, untimely; Sn 694
(ath' ~ me bhavissati kālakiriyā; = antarā yeva,
Pj); SN I 62,13 (~ va kālaṁkato; Spk); Ja I 55,2
(~ yeva kālaṁ katvā); Ja III 256,5' (~ va naṭṭhā);
IV 54,11 (~ akālamaraṇaṁ nāma no n'atthi); VI
57,31.' (~ pabuddho); 452,16' (~ va vināsaṁ pā-
puṇissasi); Mil 251,21 (~ yeva paripaṭanti); 305,3
(~ yeva . . . abbhatthaṁ gaccheyya); in the same
sense repeated: ~ va taṁ puññaṁ khīyati, ~ va
kālaṁ karoti, Dhp-a I 173,21; in the phrase ~ vo-
1antarāantarā-vosana(-gamana) and cf. antarā-kathā, antarā-
maraṇa below. — Cf. an-antarā, antarantarā &
cpd.s below. — 2. prp. between (cf. antarena 2),
(ci) (with gen. pl); ~ satthīnaṁ, Vin II 161,28 ; AN II
245.2 (cf. antara-satthi above); ubhinnam ~, Abhidh-
av 125,7*; °-dvārānaṁ ~, Dhp-a I 272,20; dvinnaṁ
rājūnaṁ ~, Sp (II) 309,8; Ja VI 295,8* (na tesaṁ
~ gacche, not to interfere with their affairs; = tesaṁ
lābhassa antarā na gacche, antarāyaṁ na kareyya,
Ct.); Dhp-a IV 190,8 (v. l.; Ee antare, q.v.); — (b) with
acc. sg. of both terms (like lot. inter te atque inter
quadrupedem); see antarena 2 (c)): Bālāv 278,2 (cf.
Kacc 308; p. 154,24); Sadd 716,21 foll; ~ ca Bājaga-
haṁ ~ ca Nāḷandaṁ, DN I 1,1-5 (Sv), quoted Sp I
16,1 (Sp-t) & Pay fol. go v. 5 (majjhe ti attho);
similarly MN I 149,22; 170,33 (Ps) — Vin I 8,11; Ud
11,27 (Ud-a), quoted Ud-a 164,10; ~ ca velaṁ ~ ca
agyāgāraṁ, AN V 234,13; — (c) of time: within a
certain period, during (with acc); ~ vassaṁ or,
better, as a cpd., before the end of v°, Vin I 138,2;
153,1; cf. anto-vassa.

2antarā, f., an outer(\) garment (cf. antara, n. &
antarīya, n.); ~ā + uttarīyaṁ uttarāsaṅgo upasaṁ-
vyānan ti pariyāyasaddā ete, Vv-a 166,28 (cf. Abh
292); — ifc. v. instr, pl. pīt'-antarāhi, Vv 403 (=
pīta-vaṇṇehi uttariyehi(l), Vv-a).

antarā-amitta, m., an inward enemy; It 83,12
(antarā-mala +), quoted Nidd I 15,12 foll.

antarā-ahosi, aor. 3 sg. of antarā-bhavati, was
interrupted; Vin II 140,1 (dhammakathā ~; = an-
tarikā (ɔ: °it[ā/a]?) ahosi paṭicchannā, Sp Ce).

antarā-kathā, f. [better two words: 1antara
(1, c-d) as an adv. to udapādi or vippakatā] talk,
conversation (between); ~ā udapādi, Vin II 296,29;
Sn p. 115,11 (Pj) = MN ch 98 (Ps (Ee) III 431,18);
DN II 8,2; MN II 2,23; 79,2; III 88,20; SN I 79,28;
IV 281,15 (Spk); AN I 170,8 (Mp); III 167,23; 168,18;
antarā-kathā179,25 (Sv); MN I 161,26 (Ps); 503,1; 514,21 (Ps);
112,18; 30,26; 1119,5; 88,24; AN II 196,32 (v. l.);
Ud 11,14 (Ud-a). — Cf. Ja I 58,20 & antarantarā-
kathā.

antarā-kamma, n., what happened in the mean-
time; tato paṭṭhāya imesaṁ ubhinnam pi ~aṁ na
kathitaṁ (í. e. their fortunes from that moment to the
time of our Buddha), Mp I 155,18.

antarā-kāja, m. (antarā + kāja — kāca, q. v.),
a load suspended (on a carrying stick) between two
persons; Vin II 137,24 (ekato-kājaṁ ~aṁ sīsabhā-
raṁ, etc.; = majjhe laggetvā dvīhi vahitabbaṁ
bhāraṁ, Sp). — Cf. antara-kājaka, antarika-kāja.

antarā-kilesa, m., inner impurity; MN III
275,20 (acc. ~aṁ + antarā-saṁyojanaṁ antarā-
bandhanaṁ).

Antarā-gaṅga, m(?) Npr. of a monastery in Cey-
lon; Mhv XL IV 100 (~a°-savhassa). Cf. Antara-gaṅgā.

antarā-cilima, n., an inner cover or pellicle(l);
MN III 274,34 (~aṁ + antarā-nahārū antarā-ban-
dhanaṁ, 'the inward tendons and sinews and fasten-
ings', Trsl.; Ee °-cilīmaṁ, Se °-vilimaṁsaṁ(l); Ps Ce:
cilimaṁ nahāru bandhanan ti sabbaṁ camme laggaṁ
antarā-cilimabandhanan ti sabba-camma-laggaṁ vilimaṁsam eva);
ib. 275,16.

[antarâtīta, mfn., Ja II 243,17, w. r. for an-
antarâtīta, q. v.]

antarā-dhāna, n. = antara-dhāna [perhaps ab-
stracted from antarā-pi-dhāyati]; Abh 51 (tiro-dhāna
+ ); Abh-sūci reads antara-dhānaṁ [metre faulty]
and explains: antaraṁ dharatī ti antara-dhānaṁ
(q. v.).antarā-dhāna

antarā-nahāru, m. (but used as n., gender
attraction?), the sinews within (the body); MN III
274,35 (antarā-cilimaṁ + ~ū [sic Ee & Se] antarā-
bandhanaṁ); ib. 275,17.

antarā-paccatthika, m., an inward adversary;
It 83,12 foll. (antarā-mala +), quoted Nidd I 15,12 foll.

antar-āpaṇa, m. [ts.], ('between the shops') the
bazar street, hence: bazar; acc. ~aṁ paṭipajjeyyuṁ,
MN I 30,27 (= āpaṇānam antare mahājana-saṁ- ḷ
kiṇṇa-racchāmukhaṁ, Ps); agamaṁ ~, Ap 374,28;
dāsiṁ ~ pesesi, Mp I 454,13; Dhp-a I 181,1 (do.);
antar-āpaṇaJa I 55,20; 350,10-12; III 406,29; loc. ~e, Ap 287,27
(gacchantaṁ ~); paṭimagg(e) ~, ib. 124,6.

antarâpatti, f. (antarā + āpatti), prob. — an-
tarāyikā (q. v.) āpatti; Sp I 29,17 (= 'paṭilābhaṁ
ukkhipati āpatti dukkaṭassā' (untraced) ti evam-
ādinā sikkhāpadantaresu paññattā āpatti, Sp-t). Cf.
Vin II 43,18.

antarā-parinibbāyi(n), m., a person who passes
into nibbāna before the term, i. e. before having passed
the first half of life, Pp 16,24-30 (Pp-a; mṭ), see however
antarā-bhava below; SN V 69,24—70,24 (pañcannaṁ
antarā-parinibbāyinupahacca parinibbāyī, asaṁkhāra-p°, saṣaṁkhāra-p°,
uddhaṁsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī; Spk: yo āyu-vemajjhaṁ
anatikkamitvā parinibbāyati, so tividho hoti, etc.)
≠ SN V 237,13 = 285,18 = 314,21 ≠ 378,21 ≠ AN I
233,21-35 (the same five in opposite order; cf. II
134,23-28) ≠ AN IV 70,18—74,8 (the same more in
detail; Mp: āyuno vemajjhaṁ anatikkamitvā etth'
antare kilesa-parinibbānena parinibbuto hoti, cf.
Abhidh-k-vy Trsl. Ill 39 n. l); DN III 237,21 (pañca
anāgāmino: ~ī, etc.; Sv: āyuno majjhaṁ anatikka-
mitvā antarā va kilesa-parinibbānaṁ arahattaṁ
patto); ≠ AN V 120,5 = Paṭis I 161,12 (cf. Nett
190,1, = yo Avihâdisu tattha tattha āyuvemajjhaṁ
appatvā parinibbāyati, Nett-a)); SN V 201,15 (mu-
dutarehi [scil. indriyehi] ~ī, etc.; Spk) = 204,27;
Kv 366,13; Pj I 182,24; Ud-a 93,1.

antarā-parinibbāyi(n), m., a person who passes
into nibbāna before the term, i. e. before having passed
the first half of life, Pp 16,24-30 (Pp-a; mṭ), see however
antarā-bhava below; SN V 69,24—70,24 (pañcannaṁ
antarā-parinibbāyinupahacca parinibbāyī, asaṁkhāra-p°, saṣaṁkhāra-p°,
uddhaṁsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī; Spk: yo āyu-vemajjhaṁ
anatikkamitvā parinibbāyati, so tividho hoti, etc.)
≠ SN V 237,13 = 285,18 = 314,21 ≠ 378,21 ≠ AN I
233,21-35 (the same five in opposite order; cf. II
134,23-28) ≠ AN IV 70,18—74,8 (the same more in
detail; Mp: āyuno vemajjhaṁ anatikkamitvā etth'
antare kilesa-parinibbānena parinibbuto hoti, cf.
Abhidh-k-vy Trsl. Ill 39 n. l); DN III 237,21 (pañca
anāgāmino: ~ī, etc.; Sv: āyuno majjhaṁ anatikka-
mitvā antarā va kilesa-parinibbānaṁ arahattaṁ
patto); ≠ AN V 120,5 = Paṭis I 161,12 (cf. Nett
190,1, = yo Avihâdisu tattha tattha āyuvemajjhaṁ
appatvā parinibbāyati, Nett-a)); SN V 201,15 (mu-
dutarehi [scil. indriyehi] ~ī, etc.; Spk) = 204,27;
Kv 366,13; Pj I 182,24; Ud-a 93,1.

antarā-bandhana, n., an inner string or liga-
ment (in the body); MN III 274,35; 275,17-20 (also
in metaph, sense).

antarā-bhatte, ind. (cf. antara-bhatta), during
(ɔ: before finishing) the meal; Ja II 391,1; IV 50,9;
Sv I 188,5 (= Ps I 256,28, reading antara-°).

antarā-bhava, m., an intermediate state of
existence, according to the Pubbaseliya and Sammi-
tiya interpretation of antara-parinibbayi(n) (Kv-a
106,1-7); Kv 361,1 foll; Ud-a 92,26-27; 93,3-19;
Spk II 373,1-5; Abhidh-k-vy Trsl. Ill 32 n. l, V 210.
— °-kathā, f., title of Kv VIII etc. 2 (p. 361—66).antarā-bhava

antarā-maggato, ind. (antarā + magga, abl.),
back from the mid-way; AN V 82,34 (senaṁ ... ~
nivattāpeti).

antarā-magge, ind. (cf. prec), on the way; Vin
I 88,28; 244,1; AN III 96,12; Ja I 253,11; IV 429,21'
(= 'antarā'); Ps II 94,6; Mp III (Se) 16,20; Dhp-a
I 3,9; 13,14; 1121,4; III 337,15'; Ud-a 171,12; Pv-a
151,8; 258,1; 269,21; 273,29; Mil 16,26.antarā-magge

antarā-maraṇa, n., premature death [two words?
cf. antarā-kathā]; Ap 310,7 (Ee °-māraṇaṁ); Ud-a
289,27 (~aṁ pāpuniṁsu; cf. antarā maraṇa-ppatto,
Dhp-a I 409,17); Pv-a 136,30; Ps II 290,2. Cf. antarā
akālamaraṇaṁ, Ja IV 54,11'.

antarā-mala, m., inward stain or dirt; tayo
[scil. lobho doso moho] . . . ~â + antarā-amittā an-
tarā-sapattā antarā-vadhakā antarā-paccatthikā, It
83,11 foll. (quoted Nidd I 15,12 foll.).

antarā-muttaka, mfn., given up (or vacant) in
the meantime; Vin II 167,34-37 (tayo . . . senāsana-
gāhā: purimako, pacchimako, ~o) ≠ Vin-vn 2842
(antara-muttako).

1antarāya, ind. (either abs. of antar + √i [cf.
anvāya], or abstracted from antarā-yeva), on the
way, in the meantime; Sn 1120 (v. l. Bm antarāyam;
= antarā eva, Pj; = antarā yeva, Nidd).

2antarāya, m. [ts.], obstacle, hindrance, (and as
an euphemism for) an (imminent) accident, mis-
fortune, danger, or destruction, ruin, death; Abh 765;
nom. ~o. Vin I 149,30 (es' eva ~o ti pakkamitabbaṁ);
Ja VI 74,11 (kadāci kocid-eva ~o bhaveyya); Pj
I 181,12 (na . . . koci ~o atthi); with gen. pers. & rei:
DN I 3,6 foll. (tumhaṁ yev' assa tena ~o); AN III
2antarāya(evaṁ no viharataṁ ~o na hessati; = jīvitanta-
rāyo na bhavissati, Ct.); VI 3,16 (nâssa koci ~o
paññāyati); I 55,9 (n' atth' etassa ~o, cf. Sn 692);
VI 9,26; VI 31,13 (sace mama ~o hoti); 544,2*
(~o pi me assa); Dhp-a II 236,1 (imass' eko ~o
atthi); Ud-a 67,19 (mā kassaci iminā ~o hotu); —
Ja VI 395,1, (visa-yogassa ~o kato, ɔ: prevented); Ps
(Ee) III 328 14 (rajjassa vā jīvitassa vā ~o); — with
loc. pers.: Sn 691 (no ce kumāre bhavissati ~o; =
bhavissati nu kho imasmiṁ kumāre ~o, Pj), cf.
ib. 692 ; — acc. ~aṁ, Dhp 286 (~aṁ na bujjhati;
= jīvitantarāyaṁ, Dhp-a); ~aṁ karoti, to hinder,
prevent (with gen. rei and personæ): Vin I 15,18 (mā
koci . . . ~aṁ akāsi . . . pabbajjāya); Ja VI 171,29
(uposathakammassa me ~am pi kareyya); 295,13'
(tesaṁ~aṁ na kareyya; = 'na tesaṁ antarā gacche',
cf. DN I 227,24 (Sv)); Pv-a 20,31 (te dānassa ~aṁ
katvā); Sp (IV) 869,10 (sagga-mokkhānaṁ ~aṁ ka-
ronti); Mil 156,10 (Bhagavato bhojanassa ~am akāsi);
in some instances the phrase ~aṁ karoti takes an object
in acc. [see parallels s. v. adinna(ṁ ādiyi)]: Vin IV
283,28** (gaṇassa cīvara-lābhaṁ ~aṁ kareyya); MN
II 39,28 (Sakuludāyiṁ ~am akāsi Bhagavati brahma-
cariye); Mil 156,23 (taṁ [scil. bhojanaṁ] ~aṁ ka-
roti); ib. 2 8 (paribhogaṁ . . . ~aṁ karoti); — ~aṁ
vinā, Vism 712,5* ≠ Abhidh-av 137,28* ≠ Vin-vn
3180 (cf. As 1,16*; Ud-a 1,13*); — instr, kenacideva
~ena nâgacchati, Vin II 277,25; Ja I 128,27 (ekena
~ena bhavitabbaṁ) ≠ Dhp-a III 75,9; — dat. ~āya,
Vin IV 134,1 foll. = 135,20** (nâlaṁ ~, cf. JAs
1914 p. 514,6) = II 25,16 = MN I 130,8 ≠ MN I 72,1;
alañ ca te ~āya, MN II 257,1; Nidd I 14,10 (kusa-
lānaṁ dhammānaṁ parihānāya ~āya saṁvattanti;
= antaradhānāya, Nidd-a) — gen. ~assa kāriyā,
Ja VI 544,3*; — abl. ~ā, Vin II 32,24 (aññatra~); —
loc. ~e (sati), Vin I 112,29; — pl. ~ā, DN II 88,1
(Pāṭaliputtassa . . . tayo ~ā bhavissanti, aggito vā,
etc.); cattāro ~ā, Mil 156,17 (adiṭṭha°, etc.); pañca
vassassa ~ā, AN III 243,2; dasa ~ā, Vin I 112,36
(rājantarāyo +, cf. 169,35 & Divy 544,18) ≠ Vin
II 244,15 (gen. pl. dasannaṁ ~ānaṁ aññatarena:
rajantarāyena +); acc. pl. ~e, As 1,16*. — Ifc. v.
agy-°, adiṭṭha°, an-°, amanussa°, udaka°, ud-
dissakaṭa°, upakkhaṭa°, uposatha°, uppatt'-°,
kabala°, kammaṭṭhāna°, khīra°, gamana°, cora°,
jīvita°, paribhoga°, bādhaka°, brahmacariya°,
bhatta°, bhoga°, maṅgala°, manussa°, rajja°,
rati-°, rāja°, lābha°, vāḷa°, sagga°, sagga-
magga°, savana°, siriṁsapa°, hata°.

antarāya-kara, mfn., causing impediments,
preventing; dangerous; DN I 227,24 foll. (tesaṁ ~o;
= lābhantarāya-karo, Sv); SN I 34,14* (aññesaṁ
dadamānānaṁ ~ā narā; = sagg'-antarayo . . . ti
imesaṁ antarāyānaṁ kārakā, Spk); Pv 671 (aññesaṁ
dadamānānaṁ ~o ahaṁ [ɔ:ahuṁ?]); Ja IV 122,11*
(mā me mātā tarantassa ~ā ahu); AN I 161,17
(tiṇṇaṁ ~o + tiṇṇaṁ pāripanthiko (Ee pari°); =
antarāyaṁ vināsaṁ vilopam karoti, Mp); III 68,11
(rajanīyaṁ, etc. + ~aṁ [scil. itthirūpaṁ] with dat.
cf. antarāyika); Ja IV 13,20* (ābādhā ... ~ā; =
antarāya-kārakā, Ct.); V 259,27* (~o mamaṁ); VI
395,14 (vattassa ~aṁ paccāmittaṁ); Ps I 243,26
(anātāpino anto-saṁkhepo ~o hoti); Sv (III) 758,20;
Spk II 206,10 (~o; = 'antarāyiko'); Ud-a 89,28 (jīvi-
tassa~-dhammānaṁ). — Ifc. v. paṭipatti-°, puñña°,
lābha°. — — °-tta, n. abstr., Thī-a 288,15.

antarāya-bhāva, m., the existence of some danger
threatening; ~aṁ pucchi, Ja VI 3,13 (v. l. antarāyâ-
bhāvaṁ, cf. Ja VI 9,25).

antarāya-vimocana, n., doing away with the
dangers (of life); Mhv XXXV 73 (= āyuss' anta-
rāya-paṭimocanaṁ, Mhv-ṭ).

antarāyika, mfn. (from antarāya, Buddh, sa. id. cf.
sa. āntarāyika), causing obstacles, being a hindrance
to, dat. or gen.; dāruṇo lābha-sakkāra-siloko kaṭuko
pharuso ~o anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya,
SN II 226,3 (= antarāya-karo, Spk), cf. AN III 68,11;
sampajāna-musāvādo ~o dhammo vutto Bhagavatā,
antarāyikasee

antarārati, pr. 3 sg. (v. l. santar[ā/a]rati; denom,
of antara, cf. antarāla), to interrupt, Kacc-v 441 (=
santaraṁ karoti; + upakkamālati = upakkamaṁ
karoti), untraced in texts, not mentioned by Rūp nor
by Sadd 823,30.

antarârāmaṁ, ind. (antar(ă) + ārāma), into the
park; Sp (IV) 857,18 ad Vin IV 101,5 (~an ti anto-
gāme vihāro hoti, taṁ gacchati; but Vin Ee 'an-
tara-gāmaṁ gacchati', v. l. antarā-gāmaṁ).

antarāla (also written antarāḷa), n. [ts.], inter-
mediate space, interval; loc. ~e, Dāṭh I 52. — Ifc. v.
nabha°. — °-pathe, ind. (antarāla- taking the place
antarāla114.

antarā-vadhaka, m., an inward murderer; It
83,12 foll. (antarā-mala +), quoted Nidd I 15,12 foll.

antarā-vosāna, n., giving up half-way, in the
Canon two words, antara being constructed with
āpajjati [cf. antarā-kathā, etc., *antara, 1(b)]; ~aṁ
āpādi, It 85,13 (quoted Pj II 20,13; Ud-a 110,1); ~aṁ
āpajjissanti, DN II 78,22 (Sv); ~aṁ āpanno, AN V
antarā-vosāna

antarā-sapatta, m., an inward rival; It 83,12
foll. (antarā-mala +), quoted Nidd I 15,12 foll.

antarāla (also written antarāḷa), n. [ts.], inter-
mediate space, interval; loc. ~e, Dāṭh I 52. — Ifc. v.
nabha°. — °-pathe, ind. (antarāla- taking the place
antarāla114.

antarika-kājaka, m. = antarā-kāja; Khuddas
XL I 38 (= de-denā usulana aturu-kada, sn).

antarikā, f. (from 2antara), space between, cleft,
chink; interval; Kv 226,11 (sīmā+, Ee ~īkā); Vin
III 108,23 (Tapodā dvinnaṁ mahānirayānaṁ ~āya
āgacchati, = antarena, Sp; quoted Sv I 35,2 and Ud-a
110,2: = vivare). — Ifc. v. aggaḷa°, aňgul'-°,
antarikābhamuka°, bhājana°, loka°, vātapāna°, vijj'-°,
sīma°, sutta°.

antar-ita, mfn. [pp. of sa. antar + √i], in a pas-
sive sense generally with instr, or ifc. = separated
by, or being at a distance of; m. ~o, Mp ad AN III
186,1 (kuḍḍâdīhi); f. ~ā, Ps (Ee) III 334,26 (aṭṭha-
usabhamattena ṭhānena ~; so CeEe, Ce giving v. l. an-
taritvā; Ck antaritvā, Se ajānantī (w. r.)); n. ~aṁ,
Mil 291,6 (anekehi bhava-sahassehi, cf. paṭicchanna,
Ja I 98,7, etc.); ifc. Mp I 138,21-22; gen. ~assa( pā-
kāra-kuḍḍâdi-°), As 84,14. — °-tta, n. abstr.; abl. ~ā
(musāvādena, being interwoven with lies), Sv I 73,13
antar-ita

[antariya, mfn. = antarika, ifc. v. pakkha°,
Dhp-a I 345,13, but the reading pakkhuttariya is
supported by gp)].

[anta-ruddhi, f. possibly for anta-vaṭṭi, q. v.,
Ja VI 8,9 (duggandha-gandhen' assa ~īnam nikkha-
mana-kālo viya ahosi; v. l. Bd °ruṭhīnaṁ, Bh °ruci-
naṁ, Se °rutthīnaṁ)].

antarubbhāra, m. (1antara + ubbhāra), a tempo-
rary suspension; ~o + sahubbhāro, Vin V 179,4-12;
Vin-vn 2715 foll. (cf. Vin I 255,20 & Vin Trsl. II 157).

antarussava, m. (antar([ā/a]) + ussava), a festival
held on a particular occasion; Sp (III) 631,18 ad Vin
III 187,23 ('chaṇesū' ti āvāha-vivāha-maṅgalâdisu
~esu; = mahussavassa antarantarā pavattita-
ussavesu, Sp-ṭ).

antarûpaṭṭhāna, n. (antar([ā/a]) + upaṭṭhāna), an
intermediate attendance; Ja I 226,27 (aññāni pi ~āni
honti yeva; opp. tīṇi mahā-upaṭṭhānāni, in the
morning, at noon, and in the evening).

antare, ind. (loc. of 2antara), 1. adv. (a) in,
within; Ja VI 305,6 (~ katvā, = astride on him; cf.
antaraṁ karoti); (b) = 1antarā 1 (b), mid-way;
~ a-patiṭṭhahitvā, Mp II 247,17 (quoted Ss 50,5);
[pure vā pacchā vā ~e vā, Ps (Ec) III 15,22, so Se,
but Ee antarantare.]. ;— 2. prp. with gen., (a) between;
Ja I 52,15 (dvinnaṁ nagarānaṁ); Dhp-a I 67,2 (Sā-
antareca vihārassa ca ~); Ps(Ee)īīl 339,19 (ubhinnam ~);
Dīp XI 9 (ubho-rājānam ~); — (b) amidst, among
(a greater number, cf. abbhantare); Dhp-a I 91,9 (ara-
hantānaṁ ~); 1446,7' (mahājanassa acakkhukassa
~); Ja II 352,13 (amhākaṁ ~); II 182,20 (ettakā-
naṁ manussānaṁ ~); IV 187,11 (manussānaṁ ~,

antalikkha, n. [sa. antar[ī/i]kṣa], the air, atmo-

rante pi bandhatī ti ~o; quoted Ud-a 367,21*; It-a

369,1; manomayo pīti-bhakkho . . . ~o, DN III 29,3;

V 374,4*; Ap 18,8 (v. l).

anta-lopa, m. [ts.], the dropping of a final

antava(t), mfn. [ts.], having an end or term,
antavat~vā attā hoti, DN I 31,9; ~vā attā ca loko ca, MN
II 233,19; Paṭis 1157,13; ~vā loko, Ud 67,1 (= sa-
pariyanto, parivatumo, paricchinna-pamāṇo, na
sabbagato, Ud-a); ' DN I 187, 2 8 foll; SN III 214,32
(also title of the sutta ib.); IV 286,1; 391,24; AN
II 41,8; V 31,5; 186,22; 193,12,28; 196,23; Dhs 1099
(As 371,3); 1117; 1175; Paṭis I 151,15 foll; Nidd I
64,18 (= sa-anto, Nidd-a); Mil 145,12; acc. ~van-
taṁ lokaṁ, AN IV 428,25; n. pl. ~vantāni bhūtāni,

anta-vaṭṭi, f. (3anta + vaṭṭi), the bowels; Vism
258,5 = Vibh-a 241,14 (ekavīsatiyā ṭhānesu obhag-
gā); cf. Pj I 56,27; Ja I 260,17 (°-maṁsa-lohitâdīhi

anta-vaṭṭi~īhi rukkhaṁ parikkhipitvā, Ja III 160,2; pl.(1),
see [anta-ruddhi].

anta-vaṇṇa, m. [sa. antya-varṇa], a man of the
lowest castes; Abh 503 (sudde 'ntavaṇṇo).

antava(t), mfn. [ts.], having an end or term,
antavat~vā attā hoti, DN I 31,9; ~vā attā ca loko ca, MN
II 233,19; Paṭis 1157,13; ~vā loko, Ud 67,1 (= sa-
pariyanto, parivatumo, paricchinna-pamāṇo, na
sabbagato, Ud-a); ' DN I 187, 2 8 foll; SN III 214,32
(also title of the sutta ib.); IV 286,1; 391,24; AN
II 41,8; V 31,5; 186,22; 193,12,28; 196,23; Dhs 1099
(As 371,3); 1117; 1175; Paṭis I 151,15 foll; Nidd I

anta-virahita, mfn., endless; Ud-a 41,20 (~e
saṁsāre) ≠ Vism 526,2], = Vibh-a 134,21 (quoted

antâtīta, mfn. (*anta + atīta), perpetual (an

(accantan ti ~aṁ [so Cks; EeSe an-atītaṁ] avināsa-

antânanta, mfn. (anta + an-anta), limited or
endless; ~aṁ lokaṁ paññāpenti, DN I 22,16 foll.; —

that; Sv I 115,1 (pl. ~ā = 'antânantikâ').

antânantika, mfn. (from prec.), one who insists
on finiteness or infinity (of the world); DN I 22,13
(pl. ~ā = antânanta-vādā, Sv); sassata-vādā +,
Sv I 102,12 ≠ Ps II 5,9 ≠ Kv-a 6,20 — Sp I 60,19
= Mhbv 110,6 (Dharmapr 305,16) ≠ Ss 121,25; Paṭis
I 155,17.

[antāpariyanta, mfn., pl. ~ā, Ja V 319,8', prob,

= 'alaṁ hessanti'; BdSe read pariyattā, omitting attā].

Ja V 399,3* (tav'antim āgatā; = tava santikaṁ, Ct.)
2antietc.

(majjha°), maraṇa°, māraṇa°, vimokkha°, san-
niṭṭhāna°, savana°.

1antika, mfn. [ts.], near, proximate; compar.
& superl, are formed on the base neda [ts.]: nediya,
nediṭṭha, see Kacc 266 ≠ Sadd 686,11 (cf. Pāṇ V
3,63); — n.~aṁ, vicinity, MTD; —acc. ~am, ind.
& loc. ~e, ind., see below.

antikaṁ, ind. [ts.], near to (with gen. or ifc);
Ja I 28,4* (tav' ~aṁ, quoted from Bv II 187, see

— Ifc. v. upa°, jina°, tad-°, Paṇdula° (Mhv X 19),
sa°, sara°.

antika-bhāva, m., nearness, proximity; Pj I
217,32 (udakassa ~ena odakantikaṁ).

266,1*; sāmikaṁ nissāya tass' ~, Ja VI 566,11'(=

odaka°, pura°, sa°.

rantima-dhari(n), SN I 60,35*); dhāreti ~aṁ dehaṁ,
It 50,4*; 53,16*; SN II 278,21*; Sn 502 (~ā, scil.
jāti, Pj) ≠ ayam ~ā jāti, n'atthi dāni punabbhavo,
DN II 15,12; MN I 167,28; Dhp 351 (~o 'yarn samus-
sayo); Th 339 (do.); Thī 22 (do.) = 160; SN III
83,28*; ayam~ā vedagū Brahma-patti, Ja III 359,20*

antima-brahma-patti (Bd brahmupapatti) pacchima-

antīyati, pr. 3 sg. pass, of antati (q. v.); Sadd

anto ~ ummāre thatvā; = eli-pata-ætulē sita, Ja-
ante

IV 275,15; acc. ~iṁ, ib. IV 212,8; gen. ~iyā, ib.

ante-vāsi-vāsa, m. = antevāsika-vāsa; MN II
39,23 (mā bhavaṁ Udāyi ācariy(ak)o hutvā .. .
~aṁ vasi, paron.); Pj II 413,22 ('māṇavo' ti ~aṁ
anatīta-bhāvena vuccati).

°-navamāse, Ps II 369,23; °-nirodhasmiṁ (& °-niro-

IV 132,10; V 118,8'; Mp I 414,9; °-parikkhepe, Mhv
XV 52; °-pātarāse, Ps (Se) III 629,3; °-pokkhara-
ṇiyaṁ, Dhp-a I 351,2; °-majjhantike, see anto-

306,2* (pabbata-m-antarasmiṁ ḷ ~ pavisitvā (un-

anto-aggi, m., indoor fire; ~ bahi na nīhari-
tabbo, Dhp-a I 397,18 = III 466,13 = Mp I 410,1
= 414,6.

anto-aruṇa, m. = anto-aruṇagga, n., the time
before sunset; Ps II 208,30 (°-aruṇena) ≠ Mp II 327,7
(°-aruṇaggena, scil. paricchinnaṁ).

anto-ārāma, m., the inner (i. e. fenced in) part
of an ārāma (q. v.); Vin IV 163,26' (ajjhārāmo nāma
parikkhittassa ārāmassa ~o).

anto-āvasatha, m., the inner (fenced in) part
of any dwelling-place; Vin IV 163,27' (ajjhāvasatho
nāma parikkhittassa āvasathassa ~o).

anto-uṭṭhita-sasana, n., breath arisen from
within; Sadd 399,31 (= assāso).

anto-udara-gata, mfn., being inside the belly
f. ~ā, Ja V 455,2' (= 'hadayantarassitā', q. v.).

anto-olīyana, n. (by gender attraction m.) =
'anto-saňkhepa', q. v.; pt ad Sv (III) 758,20.

anto-karaṇa, n., keeping within, inclusion;
°attho hi ayam ā-kāro [scil. the prefix ā in ā-sava],
Ps I 61,17 = Mp II 183,2 = As 48,13 (mṭ: ayaṁ
ā-kāro abhividhi-attho (q. v.) idha gahito ti"anto-
karaṇattho"ti vuttaṁ ≠ Ps-pṭ). Cf. anto-karitvā,
anto-karaṇa

anto-kasambu, mfn., rotten inside (cf. anto-
pūti . . . kasambu-jāta, AN IV 171,9); SN I 166,8*
(+ saṁk(i)liṭṭha; Ee & Spk °-kasambhu°); it, 33*
(Ee °-kasambu°).

anto-kārika, m., member of a certain council of
fudges; pl. ~ā, Sv (II) 519,15 (so cod. B and Se;
EeCe sutta-dharā; = nīti-sutta-dharā, pt).

anto-kucchi, f., (from anto-kucchiyaṁ, loc), the
belly, vomb; Abh 862 (= 'koṭṭha'); Ps II 278,19 (~i vi-
parivattamānā mahāravaṁ ravi); loc. hatthino ~iyaṁ
saṭṭhi purisā aparâparaṁ caṁkamanti, Dhp-a I
192,10; Sv (II) 436,31. — °-gata, mfn., being in the
mother's womb; ~aṁ (Bodhisattaṁ), Ja I 51,32; Sv
anto-kucchi

anto-koṭṭhâgārika, mfn., hoarding riches; pl.
~ā ime samaṇā Sakyaputtiyā, Vin III 251,2 (= ab-
bhantare saṁvihita-koṭṭhâgārā, Sp) = Vin I 209,22;
mahicchā ime samaṇā ~ā, Ja III 364,2.

anto-gata, mfn., being within (gen.), inward;
contained in, included (cf. anto-gadha); pattassa
~aṁ, Ps II 396,17; jhānassa vaḍḍhitass' ~aṁ rū-
paṁ,Abhidh-av 107,5*; ~ehi indriyehi (+ abahigatena
mānasena), AN IV 87,3 (= bahi avikkhittehi anto
anupavittheh'eva pañcahi indriyehi, Mp), cf. Mvu I
237,10; — °-aṁ, ind., aside, apart (of speech); ~am
anto-gata— °-tta, n. abstr., As 214,17 (diṭṭhīnaṁ ~ā).

anto-gadha, mfn. [anto + *gadha, cf. sa. √gadh :
gadhita, but esp. ogadha, q. v. [amat'-°, katth'-°,
khay'-°, jagat'-°, nibbān'-°, sam-°], this glossed by
°-patiṭṭha(Mp ad AN III 79,11, Mp-ṭ = °abbhantara;
√gādha: patiṭṭhāyaṁ!) or taken from o-gāh, Dhp-a
IV 186,9], contained in, included, comprised; Abh
742; n. ~aṁ (dukkhe), Ps I 223,15 [abl. ~ato ib. 13];
m. pl. ~ā, Ap 364,22 (tava ~ā va te, scil. gaṇino;
cf. Ap 21,6); etesv-eva ~ā, Ud-a 140,14; tīsu sanni-
pātesu ~ā, Mil 125,29; MN III 94,23 (~ā tassa
kusalā dhammā; = antobhavā . . . abbhantaragatā
anto-gadhapl.

anto-geha-ppavesana, n., entering into a house;
Dhp-a III 36,19.

anto-gehâbhimukha, mfn., with the face towards
the interior of the house; Dhp-a I 27,16.

anto-ghara, n., the interior of a house; Abh 862;
loc. ~e, Dīp XII 82 (saha ['and', sgh. hā] ~jane; or
split cpd.); — °-cāri(n), mfn., belonging to the
household; m. pl. ~ino, Spk I 146,22; — °-jana, m.,
household people, Pj I 121,27 (gen. pl. ~ānaṁ); Dīp
anto-ghara

anto-jaṭa, mfn. (cf. jaṭā), entangled within; f. ~ā
(+ bahijatā, scil. pajā), SN I 13,18* (Spk) = 165,19*
(quoted Vism 1,11*; Sadd 352,14).

anto-jana, m. (cf. anta-jana), the inside house-
hold, family; DN III 61,6 (guttiṁ saṁvidahassu ~as-
miṁ; Sv: anto-jana-saṁkhātaṁ tava putta-dāraṁ
sīla-saṁvare patiṭṭhapehi) ≠ AN I 109,28 (Mp ≠
Sv); AN I 152,23-25 (saddhaṁ kulapatiṁ nissāya ~o
... vaḍḍhati); II 137,32 (bhattu abbhantaro ~o,
anto-jana183,2 (~assa ca attano ca pakkabhattaṁ); V 118,7'(~o
ḷ antovaḷañjanaka-parijano); ib, 9' (suṭṭhu-(saṁ)ga-
hita-°); VI 301,17 (~aṁ ovaditvā); opp. bahi-jana: Ja
I 323,7;IV 132,14; VI 4,21.

anto-jāta (or °-jātaka), m(fn.), [sa. antar-jāta],
a slave born in the house (of his master); one of the 3
or 4 kinds of slaves: Abh 515 (~o, dhanakkīto, (sayaṁ)
dāsavyôpagato, karamarânīto; Jolly Recht u. Sitte
§ 13); Vin IV 224,33' ≠ Nidd I 11,8 (°-ka; = anto

361,10-14 (°-ka) ≠ Sv I 168,16 ≠ Ps (Ee) III 8,20
(°-ka) ≠ Vin-vn 216; Sp ad Vin I 76,26; ~âdayo,

anto-jāla-gata, mfn., being in (ɔ: caught in)
a net; Ap 21,6 (~ā ete tava ñāṇamhi; Ce anto-
jālī-katā) = Th-a(Ce) II 100,12* (°-jālī-katā); Ap 21,18
= Th-a (Ce) II 100,24*; Ap 323,19 (~ā pāṇā pīḷitā
honti; Ce °-jālīkatā) = Th-a (Ce) 225,16*.

anto-jāli-kata, mfn., caught in a net; metaph,
comprehended; pl. ~ā, DN I 45,26 foll. (= imassa
mayhaṁ desanā-jālassa anto yeva katā, Sv; anto-
jāle katā ti antojālī-katā, pt). Cf. prec.

anto-ṭhita, mfn., being inside; °-manussā, Dhp-a
I 193,4; n. pl. ~āni, Mhv XI 8 (ratanāni).

anto-ḍāha, m., internal fire; anto-soko + ~o,
Nidd I 128,11 (= abbhantara-ḍāho, Nidd-a); wanting
in Vibh 100,4 etc.

anto-todaka, mfn., pricking or paining inside;
Pj II 100,28 (°aṭṭhena, in the sense of ~, scil. sallaṁ).

anto-dussana, n., inner corruption; Mp (Se) III
351,15 Oṭṭhena; ad AN IV 423,17 (gaṇḍato)) = Ps
(Ee) III 146,5 (reading anto-dosaṭṭhena).

anto-devatā, f., the deity of the house (metaph.
o: the parents in law and the husband); Dhp-a I 398,3
(aggi paricaritabbo, ~âpi namassitabbā) = Mp I
410,12; Dhp-a I 404,14, 17; Mp I 415,10 (pita ~aṁ
namassāpeti).

anto-dosa, m., inner illness or corruption (cf.
anto-dussana above); bhind' etaṁ ~-sallaṁ, Mil 323,18 ;
mfn., Spk I 48,10 (duttikiccha +).

anto-nagara, n., the inner town; ~aṁ sambā-
dhaṁ, amhākaṁ parijano mahanto, Dhp-a I 387,1.

anto-nijjhāna (or °-nijjhāyana), n., suffering
pain inwardly; Pv-a 18,12 (soko ti socanaṁ citta-

lakkhaṇo soko); Ja I 168,19' (~āyana-lakkhaṇena
sokena socati).anto-nijjhāna

anto-nimugga-posi(n), mfn., drawing nourish-
ment while immersed (in the water); n. pl. ~īni
(udake jātāni . . . udakânuggatāni ~, scil. uppalāni,
anto-nimugga-posinyeva hutvā pussanti, vaḍḍhant[ī/i]ti attho) = II 38,29

anto-nimugga-posi(n), mfn., drawing nourish-
ment while immersed (in the water); n. pl. ~īni
(udake jātāni . . . udakânuggatāni ~, scil. uppalāni,
anto-nimugga-posinyeva hutvā pussanti, vaḍḍhant[ī/i]ti attho) = II 38,29
(— yāni anto-nimuggān' eva posiyanti) = MN I 169,13

anto-nirodha, m., (from anto-nirodhe, loc.) the
inner of the nirodha (q. v.); Ps II 365,16 ('samā-
panno' ti padena ~, scil. kathito); ib. 27 (~e niruj-
jhati); II 349,28-32 (~asmiṁ ... ~e).

anto-nisīdana-yogga, mfn., fit to sit in; Dhp-a

anto-parijana, m., one's inner or nearest atten-
dants; Pj I 121,27 (v. l. for anto-ghara-jana).

anto-paridāha, m., internal burning or anguish;
Nidd I 128,11 (anto-ḍāho +).

anto-parisoka, m., inner pain or grief; anto-
soka (q. v.) + .

anto-pavatta, mfn., arisen within (the heart);

anto-paviṭṭha, mfn., come into, having entered;

anto-paviṭṭha

anto-pavisana-vāta, m., the inhaled air; ~o,

anto-pavesana, n., leading in, putting into; Sadd

anto-pubba-lohita, mfn., with (extravasation of)

~aṁ); Dhp-a III 3,2 (~e, so Ck; Ee antepure); Ud-a

anto-pūti, mfn., putrid or rotten inside; SN IV

anto-bhāga, m., the interior; Abh 1166 (one of

anto-vaṁka, mfn., inward curved, concave; Pj

anto-vaṁka-gata, mfn., who has swallowed the

naṁ antomukhaṁ kutilatāya anto-vaṁka-pādatā

anto-sīma(ṅ)-gata, mfn., present within the

anto-sīma(ṅ)-gata, mfn., present within the

anto-suddha, mfn., inwardly pure (opp. bahi-°);

ened; confused, bewildered; ~o, Th 316(= kāmarāgena

~o acakkhuko, MN II 202,1; paribbājakā ~ā acak-

andhaka-makasa(?). — Ifc. v. an-°, andha°, kāma°,

for anu-a° (cf. acc°) in anvādhika and perhaps anv-
ākiri, anvāmaddi, anvāyika: anva° (cf. ajjha°) in
anvagata, anvaga (anvagū).

(anvākirati), pr. 3 sg. (anu + ā + √kṛ) = anu-
kirati; aor. anvākiri, Ja VI 210,25' (if not from anu-
kirati (b), sandhi lengthening, cf. anvādhika).

(anvāgacchati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + ā + √gam],
as to meaning see anvagata; [aor. 3 sg. °-gacchi,
unmetrical v. l. for anvagacchi or anvagañchi, Pv
734 (= anubandhi, Pv-a)]; abs. °-gantvāna (prob. =
having come back again), Ja I 454,16* (Ct.), quoted
Dhp-a III 358,22*; — pp. anvagata (q. v.); — caus.
(anvāgacchati)

anvāgata, mfn. (pp. of prec), (a) pass. =
attained (successively), followed (or protected) by (instr.),
endowed with (instr.); Th 63 (sukhen' ~aṁ sukhaṁ,
enjoyed (successively); tmesis of a cpd. sukhena su-
khaṁ); pl. ~ā, Ja IV 385,12* (~ā isayo sādhurūpā;
= anugatā . . . jānamānā ti attho, Ct., cf. gacchāmi
= jānāmi, Pj I 19,1-2 and 196,2-3); Ja V 4,10* (rūpena
anvāgatitthiyo; = rūpena ~ā itthiyo, Ct.); — (b)
act. (a) come back, returned; f. ~ā (putta-sokena), Ja
anvāgataāgatâsmi, Tr. āhatâsmi)); (β) who has followed, pur-
sued or overcome; m. ~o (Paṇḍarakaṁ nāgaṁ supaṇṇo
~o), Ja V 78,18'; n. ~aṁ (bhayaṁ mahantaṁ ~aṁ;
= 'anvagataṁ', q. v.), Ja V 174,19'.

anvāgameti, pr. 3 sg. (caus. of anvāgacchati),
'to let come back', i. e. to wish something back;
atītaṁ ~eti, MN III 188,1 foll.; pot. 3 sg. ~eyya,
MN III 187,22* foll. (atītaṁ nânvāgameyya, [ ˇ - ≂ |
- - ˇ - ˇ ] nappaṭikaṅkhe anāgataṁ [ ˇ ˇ - - - |
ˇ - ˇ - ]; = taṇhādiṭṭhīhi nânugaccheyya, Ps) =
Ap 506,1.

anvācaya, m. [ts.], connecting of a secondary
action with the main action (usually two independent
clauses, where the kriyā and one kāraka are not the
same); Sadd 768,1; 887,18 (from Rūp; cf. Nyāsa ad
Kāç II 2,29).

anvādiṭṭha, mfn. (pp. of anvādisati), what is
referred to again (see anvādesa); pt ad Sv (III) 863,1 β
('ettha'ti anantara-vutta-dhammā va ~ā ti āha:
"Kaṇha-sukka . . .").

anvādisati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + ā + √diç], to
refer to or confirm again; imper. 2 sg. ~āhi, Pv 120
(datvā ~ me; = yathā-dinnaṁ dakkhiṇaṁ mayhaṁ
uddissa pattidānaṁ (so Ce) dehi, Pv-a); Pv 407 (—
ādisa, Pv-a).

anvādesa, m. [sa. anvādeça], reference to a
(word or) idea already mentioned (cf. ādesa); Pay fol.
glṛ v. í ('atho' ti ~e, = Sadd 892,14); Mogg II 203
(use of the pron, ena-: kathitânukathana-visaye: imaṁ
bhikkhuṁ Vinayam ajjhāpaya, atho enaṁ [in true
Pali naṁ!] Dhammaṁ ajjhāpaya); II 241—242 (use
of me, te, no, vo: gāmo tumhaṁ pariggaho, atho
janapado vo pariggaho) = Pay fol. ga 6.anvādesa

anvādhika, mfn. (anu + adhika with sandhi
lengthening, cf. accāhita, etc.), extra supplying; n.
~am pi āropetuṁ, Vin I 297,30 (= āgantuka-pattaṁ
[ɔ: °paṭṭaṁ] dātuṁ, Sp; cf. Trsl. II 232); Vin-vn
anvādhikacf. agghi [Leumann ad Anāg 108], āveṇi-, pācitti,
nissaggi, ceti, pāni, and mātī [Mhv XXXVII 50],
cf. also Ap 397,17-18: belu-rukkhehi . . . beluvaṁ).

anvādheya, n. [ts.], a wedding present given by
the bridegroom's relatives, MTD.

anvānayati, pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu | ā | √nī], to
lead or bring on oneself, to incur (acc); 3 pl. ~anti
(nindaṁ), Sn 895 (= nindam eva anventi, garaham
eva anventi, Nidd I 306,4; = anu-ānayanti, punappu-
naṁ āharanti, Nidd-a).anvānayati

(anvāmaddati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. *anu + ā + √mṛd],
to squeeze, to wring; aor. 3 sg. ~maddi (metr. galakaṁ
anu-ă-maddi), Ja III 481,23* (= gīvaṁ maddi, Ct.).

anvāya, ind. (abs. of anveti, q. v., after the
analogy of nidheti: nidhāya, uṭṭhehi: uṭṭhāya, ādeti:
ādāya, whence also (samug)-gahāya, see Geiger §212),
used as a postposition with acc, (a) after (in consequence
of); Vin I 269,12 (gabbhassa paripākaṁ ~) ≠ 343,29;
DN I 97,1 (tesaṁ saṁvāsam ~ putto jāyetha) ≠ Ja
anvāyaI 266,16 (vuddhim ~, etc.) ≠ 1144,11; Ja I 56,24
(buddhim [a: vuddhiṁ] ~); 127,24 (piyasaṁvāsam ~,
= priyasaṁvāsayen, Ja-pot); 148,18 (gabbha-pari-
pākam ~); 278,18 (vuddhim ~ = væḍi vayasaṭa
pæmiṇa, Ja-pot); III 126,16 (do.); Dhp-a II 87,10
(do.);' Dīp IX 2 (sīhasaṁvāsam ~) ≠ Mhv VI 9;
— (b) in consequence of, by means of; DN I 13,12
(ātappam ~, etc.; = āgamma, paṭiccā ti attho, Sv)
= II 130,8 = 104,19; II 197,9 (dhammānaṁ bhā-
vanaṁ ~; = anugantvā, paṭipajjitvā ti attho, Sv);
MN I 395,2 (pamādam ~); Ps I 234,11* (muhuttaṁ
pamādam ~, metre faulty) = Sv (III) 748,23*; SN III
256,1 foll. (tesaṁ taṁ cetopaṇidhim ~; = āgamma,
Spk); [a gloss sneham ~ may account for the corrupt
reading of AN II 47,2:1* (quoted Dharmapr 147,28);
read snehănvayam iv' osadhā; cf. Sn 36]; — Ja V
353,3* (uttama-javam ~, so Bd & Se, but see atthāya
above).

anvāyika, mfn. (from anu + (ā +) √i, cf. anveti),
following, a follower; m. ~o, DN III 169,16 (mahā 'ssa
jano ~o hoti); ib. 27* (~o bahujan' assa ahu); Nidd
II 89,2 (~o hoti, scil. Māro, = 'anveti'); n. ~aṁ,
Nidd I 17,2 (~aṁ hoti, scil. dukkhaṁ, = 'anveti');
m. pl. ~ā, Ja V 148,11* (sīlaṁ sirī câpi satañ ca
dhammā ~ikā paññavato bhavanti; = paññāvantam
eva anugacchanti, Ct.), quoted Ja III 348,2:1* & Pj II
146,9*; cf. Mvu III 372,16* v. l.

(anvārohati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + ā + √ruh],
to ascend or enter (together with somebody); aor. 3 sg.
anvāruhi [ - - ˇ - ], Ja IV 465,2* (taṁ, scil. nivesa-
naṁ, . . . ~ Kāsirājā pasanno; cf. Ct. ib. 9')-

anvāvajjanā, f. (anu + āvajjanā, cf. sa. ā +
√vṛj), repeated advertence; Mp I 32,25 (cittassa āvaj-
janā + ) for anvāvaṭṭanā, q. v.

anvāvaṭṭati (or °vattati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + ā
+ √vṛt], to move after or along, to crowd on (gen.);
3 pl. ~anti, MN III 116,2 foll. (tassa tathā vūpakaṭ-
ṭhassa viharato ~ brāhmaṇa-gahapatikā, etc.; — anu-
āvaṭṭanti anu-saṁkamanti, Ps (Se anu-āvattanti)).anvāvaṭṭati

anvāvaṭṭanā, f. (from prec), Vibh 373,19 (Ee
anvaṭṭanā! see v. l. and Vibh-a 500,27); Ps I 64,22
= Mp I 32,25 (anvāvajjanā from Vibh-a 500,25).

anvāvatta, mfn. (pp. of next), crowding; MN III
116,3 foll.

(anvāvasati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. *anu + ā + √vas],
to be settled, dwell along (with); [3 pl. ~anti, Nidd
I 14,24 (w. r. for anvāssavanti, see anto above &
I anvāssavati below); abs. ~vasitvā, MN I 326,34 (v. l.
for anvāvisitvā, see anvāvisati)]; [anvāvasita, mfn.,
better anv āvasita, settled along; nadim anv ăvasitā
(anvāvasati)v. 4 — Sadd 883,20 (from Rūp (Ce) 85,39: anu ava-
sitā = Kāç 14,85) see avasita].

anvāvassa, mfn. — anovassa (q. v.); Ja V 317,15*
(devamhi vassamānamhi ~aṁ bhavaṁ akā (Bd ano-
vassaṁ); Ct.: = anu-avassaṁ, yathā devo na
vasssati tathā kataṁ; the original reading of the text
was prob, an-avāvassaṁ (blending of *an-ava-varṣa
& *an-ā-varṣa, cf. sa. nir-āvarṣa) in a pāda with 9
syllables ( ˇ ˇ - - , ˇ - ˇ - ), but already at the Ct'.s
time misread as anvāvassaṁ.

anvāviṭṭha, mfn. (pp. of next), possessed (as by
a demon); m. pl. ~ā, MN I 335,2 foll. (Dūsinā mārena;
= āvaṭṭitā, Ps); SN I 114,1 (Mārena pāpimatā; =
anu-pa-viṭṭhā, Spk).

(anvāvisati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + ā + | viç], to
enter, occupy, possess (as a demon); pot. 1 sg. ~eyyaṁ
(brāhmana-gahapatike), MN I 334,6; aor. 3 sg. ~visi
(do.), MN I 334,11 foll; Mil 156,30 foll.; Spk I 127,27
(tassa sarīre ~, — adhimucci); abs. ~itvā, MN I
326,34 (aññataraṁ Brahmapārisajjaṁ); SN I 67,1
(Veṭambariṁ devaputtaṁ; Spk); pp. anvāviṭṭha, see
(anvāvisati)

anvāsatta, mfn. (pp. of anu + ā + √sañj, sa.
*anvāsakta), ensnared, befallen, or overcome with
(instr.); Ud 35,24 (pāpakehi akusalehi vitakkehi ~o,
Ee anvāsanno (q. v.), v. l. ajjhāpanno (q. v.)) = AN
IV 356,18 (v. lI. °-sante, °-sattā, °-hatā; the plural
form, due to the influence of pāpakā akusalā vitakkā
in the preceding clause, has become the base of ex-
planation in the Ctt.; Mp (Se) III 326,20: anvāsattā ti
anubaddhā (Se anubandhā) samparivāritā (Mp-ṭ:
samparivāritā vokiṇṇā, attani garumhi ca ekatte pi
anvāsattalarly

anvāsanna, mfn. (pp. of anu + ā + √syand,
sa. *anvāsyanna); overflowed (by, instr.), only as v. l.
for anvāsatta (q. v.).

anvāssavati (sometimes spelt anvāsavati), pr. 3 sg.
anvāssavatiover; [3 pl. ~anti, Ud 35,24 (v. l.Ee p. 35 n.5,cf. anvā-
sanna & anvāsatta above)]; ty-assa anto vasanti ~anti
pāpakā akusalā dhammā, SN IV 136,14 (cf. 137,10),
so read for antassa vasanti (Ec; quoted Nidd I 14,24 (Ee
anvāvasanti; = kilesasantānaṁ anugantvā bhusaṁ
savanti anubandhanti, Nidd-a)); pot. 3 pl. ~eyyuṁ
(pāpakā akusalā dhammā), DN I 70,11 = III 226,2
(Ee anvāya ssaveyyuṁ) = MN I 221,7 foll; 346,13
= 1112,24 = SN IV 104,11 = 112,8 = 176,6 =
AN III 99,28 = Pp 20,28 = 58,30 = Dhs 1345 ( =
anuppabandheyyuṁ ajjhotthareyyuṁ, As 400,18) ≠
Ud-a 178,18; fut. 3 pl. ~issanti (do.), AN IV 167,1-12
≠ MN III 113,1-8.

anvāssava, m., verbal noun from next; Pj II
116,13 (kilesa-anvāssava-virahito = 'an-avassuto').

anvāssavati (sometimes spelt anvāsavati), pr. 3 sg.
anvāssavatiover; [3 pl. ~anti, Ud 35,24 (v. l.Ee p. 35 n.5,cf. anvā-
sanna & anvāsatta above)]; ty-assa anto vasanti ~anti
pāpakā akusalā dhammā, SN IV 136,14 (cf. 137,10),
so read for antassa vasanti (Ec; quoted Nidd I 14,24 (Ee
anvāvasanti; = kilesasantānaṁ anugantvā bhusaṁ
savanti anubandhanti, Nidd-a)); pot. 3 pl. ~eyyuṁ
(pāpakā akusalā dhammā), DN I 70,11 = III 226,2
(Ee anvāya ssaveyyuṁ) = MN I 221,7 foll; 346,13
= 1112,24 = SN IV 104,11 = 112,8 = 176,6 =
AN III 99,28 = Pp 20,28 = 58,30 = Dhs 1345 ( =
anuppabandheyyuṁ ajjhotthareyyuṁ, As 400,18) ≠
Ud-a 178,18; fut. 3 pl. ~issanti (do.), AN IV 167,1-12
≠ MN III 113,1-8.

anvāssavana, n. (nomen actionis from prec);
abl. ~ato, Pj II 177,28 (hīnadhammānaṁ vassanato
siñcanato + ).

anvāhata, mfn. (pp. of sa. *anu + ā + √han),
struck, perplexed; AN IV 356,18 (v. l. for anvāsatta);
— ifc. v. an-anvahata-ceta(s).

anvāhiṇdati, pr. 3 sg. (anu + ā + √hiṇḍ;
Buddh-sa: Mvu I 20,3; Divy 68,23, etc.); to wander
about (successively from one place to another, to search
through (acc.); 3 pl. ~anti (vihārena vihāraṁ), AN IV
374,13; part. m. ~anto (kevalakappaṁ Kapilavat-
thuṁ), AN I 277,3 (= vicaranto, Mp); SN IV 374,16
anvāhiṇdatiE

anvicchā, f. [ts., from anu + ḷ is], seeking for;
Sadd 447,21 (sense of √giles, punappunaṁ icchā ~ā).

anveta, mfn. (pp. of next), what has followed, etc.;
Ja I 389,8'-9' (bhayaṁ ~aṁ upagataṁ sampattaṁ).

anveti, pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + √i, possibly also anu
+ ā + √i], to go after or along, to follow (acc.); to pursue,
attack; Sadd 883,18 (Rūp; anugate ~eti, giving the sense
of prp. 'anu'); Sn 770 (tato naṁ dukkham ~eti nāvaṁ
. . . ivôdakaṁ, to enter); Dhp 1-2 (do. to follow; = anu-
anveti= anugacchati, Pj; = anugacchati anvāyiko hoti,
Nidd(= anu-eti, Nidd-a)); Dhp 71 (ḍahantaṁ [scil.
pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ] bālam ~eti; = ḍahantam
anugacchati, Dhp-a); 124 (nâbbaṇaṁ [scil. pāṇiṁ]
visam ~eti, to enter); Ja I 389,2* (vissāsā bhayam
~eti); III 133,29* (amitta-vasam ~eti, cf. vasânuga)
= 266,25* = IV 58,14*; V 259,21* (nāgaṁ poto ~eti
pacchato); 3 pl. ~enti (nindaṁ), Nidd I 306,4 (to incur,
= 'anvānayanti'); Pv 219 (subhāsitena ~enti; so with
v. l. and Se for anvesi; the original reading prob, anu-
nenti (see anu-neti); Pv-a reads anvesi = anu-esi; Ee
anu-desi prob, means anunesi); — imper. 3 sg. ~etu,
Ja III 138,13* (tassa sa vasam ~); VI 506,13* (sace
icchati ~); Sn 564 (= MN ch. 92; yo maṁ icchati ~);
3 pl. ~entu, Ja VI 21,23* (negamā ca maṁ ~); 579,17*
(do.); — aor. 3 sg. ~esi, Ja VI 510,31* (Sivimaggena;
= (taṁ) agamāsi, Ct.); — inf. ~etuṁ, Dhp-a III
28,16 (pāṇiṁ visaṁ ~ na sakkoti); — abs. anvāya
(q. v.; cf. anuvicca); — pp. ~eta (q. v.).

(anvesati), pr. 3 sg. [sa. anu + √iṣ], to search, to
seek (acc); part. m. (a ) ~esaṁ(?), MN I 140,1 (~aṁ.
nâdhigacchanti (çloka-Wiyt/im); Ps: ~ an ti anvesantā
gavesantā(!); cf. SN I 112,29* (~ aṁ . . . Māra-senā
nâjjhagā, do; f. sg.; = pariyesamānā, Spk); cf. Sadd
181,15 foll.; ~aṁ might be an abs., see Renou-Gγ.
§ 105 (d), quoting nirīkṣaṁ, Divy 413,8; — (b) ~esanto
(vaṭṭagataṁ maggaṁ), Cp III 11,7*; pl. ~esantā, Ps
II 117,12 (= 'anvesaṁ'); part. med. m ~esamāno; Pj II
573,3 (kusaladhamme ~o; = 'kusalânuesī'); m. pl.
~ā, Ap 296,23 = Tli-a (Ce) 332,3*; abs. ~aṁ(?), see
above; pp. ~ita (q. v.).

anvesana, n. [sa. anveṣaṇa], seeking for, search-
ing; sense of √mag, Dhātup 540; Sadd II 1322(524,9);
do. of √magg, Dhātup 21; 541.

anvesita, mfn. (pp. of anvesati), sought for; Abh
753 (maggita, pariyesita, ~, gavesita).

anha, m. = aha(n), v. l. for aṇha, ifc. (q. v.).
Cf. Tr. Notes p. 81.

an-ākappa-sampanna, mfn., not decently at-
tired; pl. bhikkhū . . . dunnivatthā duppārutā ~ā
piṇḍāya caranti, Vin I 44,1 (= na ākappena sam
pannā, samaṇa-sāruppâcāra-virahitā, Sp); 60,24;
II 213,1; 215,1; f. ~ā (thūlaṅgapaccaṅgā +), Ja I
420,24.

an-ākara, m., not a receptacle for (gen.); Ja V
122,29' (lābha-yasa-sukhānaṁ ~o = 'anāyatanaṁ';
v. l. anācāro; as to 'āyatana' = ākara see Sadd
577,3, etc., Mp II 278.1; 279,24).

an-ākiṇṇa, mfn., not lilted, not crowded; n. ~aṁ
(appasaddaṁ +), Ap 547,15; Mp ad AN VI 5,26
(= 'appakinnam'); m. pl. ~ā gahatthehi (scil. selā),
Th 1069.

an-ākula, mfn. [ts.], not beset, not crowded, not
confused; unembarrassed, calm, quiet; Abh 1035 ( =
ekagga); Sn 262 = Khp V 5 (~ā kammantā, 'a quiet
husbandry'; Th 1144 (~e tattha nage ramissasi);
Pj II 118,10 (rasa-visesesu ~o, explaining 'alolo');
Vin-vn 3 (~aṁ asaṅkiṇṇaṁ, scil. vinayassa viniccha-
yaṁ; cf. Pv-a 287,8*); As 429,20* (gen. pl. ~ānaṁ
an-ākula

an-āgata, mfn. [ts.], 'not come', i. e. (1) future
(opp. atīta; cf. nâgata); Sn 373 (atītesu ~esu; scil.
pañca-kkhandḥesu, Pj); Th 950 (~amhi kālamhi);
978 (~a[ṁ]- mahabbhayaṁ); ~o addhā, DN III 216,16
= It 53,21 (cf. addha(n), (b)); acc. ~am addhānaṁ,
an-āgata106,3; gen. ~assa dukkhassa, Mil 80,30 foll.; loc.
~amhi addhāne, Bv II 73—75; Mil 90,10*; ~e
addhāne, Mil 94,23; rakkheyyânāgataṁ bhayaṁ, Ja
III 35,14* = 399,18* (Ee nâgataṁ bhayaṁ); III
399,1* (Ee do.); ~aṁ vādapathaṁ, MN II 10,5
(opp. uppannaṁ; — āgamanakaṁ, Ps); yam
~aṁ taṁ patinissaṭthaṁ, SN II 283,33; ~ā dhammā,
Dhs (p. 2,14); 1039. — (2) not yet arrived; Th 547
(~aṁ); DN II 75,11 (~ā arahanto); AN I 84,9 (~aṁ
bhāraṁ; Mp); Mil 116,22 (~ā yācakā; opp. āgatā);
147,25 (ye ~ā sabbe te agaṇitā). — (3) not learnt,
not told, not known; see an-āgatatta and an-
āgatattha below. — (4) (according to Ct.) not yet
passed away; Ja VI 221,13* (purime yāme ~e; =
pariyosānam appatte anatikka[ma]nte, Ct), cf. Ja
I 496,11* (aḍḍharatte ~e). — n. (subst.), (a) the
future; nom. ~aṁ dutiyo anto, AN III 400,1; acc.
~aṁ, MN III 187,21*; Ja VI 25,6* ≠ SN I 5,6* (cf.
Ud-a 229,5*, read na ppajappam anāg°, see v. l.);
Mil 194,17; Ja V 378,9* (kacci nânāgataṁ dīghaṁ
samavekkhasi; Ct); loc. ~e, Sn 697; 851; Kv 313,12
(ñāṇaṁ); Dhp-a I 83,22. — (b) in gramm. = the
(sense of the) future tense; Kacc 423; Mogg V 68. —
Ifc. v. atītâ°, āgatâ°, dasâhâ°.

an-āgata-kālika, mfn., belonging to the future
tense; Sadd 49,31.

an-āgata-koṭṭhāsa, m., the future part of time;
As 393,4 (= 'aparanta')-

an-āgata-ppajappā, f., longings as to the
future; instr, (abl.) ~āya + atītassânusocanā, SN I
5,8* (= anāgatassa patthanāya, Spk) = Ja VI
25,8*.

an-āgata-pucchā, f., a question about the future;
Nidd I 340,19 (atīta-pucchā + ).

an-āgata-phala, mfn., who has not attained the
fruit; Sadd 491,25 (āgataphalo + ~o, scil sāvako).

an-āgata-bhaya, n., fear for the future, future
peril; MN I 305,24 (kāmesu ~aṁ); Ja IV 159,1 (~aṁ
anoloketvā); abl. ~ā, Ja III 35,15* (cf. anāgataṁ
bhayaṁ, ib. 14*; Ct. ib. iβ': dve ~āni diṭṭha-
dhammikañ c'eva samparāyikañ ca) = 399,19*
an-āgata-bhaya~āni, AN III 100,30 foll' ("Āraññikasutta" [Sutta-
saṅgaha ch. 84]; prob, alluded to in the Bhabra
Edict by the title Anāgatabhavāni, see Vin I p. XL
ni; JPTS 1896 p. 95—97;" R. Mookerji, Asoka

DN II 100,18; suññato phasso + ~o, appanihito,
MN I 302,22 ≠ SN IV 295,14; Nidd I 52,21 = 222,27
(Nidd-a); Dhs 506 (paṭhamam jhānaṁ . . . ~aṁ) =
524; 535; Paṭis I 60,16* (~aṁ sukhaṁ); 66,20 (~aṁ
pakkhandati); 91,27 (~o vihāro); — (b) unaccoun-

Ja IV 151,8 = Dhp-a I 355,1); abl. n. ~ato (adv.),

82,19 (sa-nimittā uppajjanti pāpakā akusalā dhammā,

DN III 146,20 = 177,12; — — — °-kata, mfn., of
which no decision has been made; Vin I 255,10 (~ena
atthataṁ hoti kaṭhinaṁ, cf. Vin Trsl. II 156,3); —

direction; f. ~ā (papaṭikā), Mil 181,4; — °-phala-
samāpatti, f., attainment of the fruit of the signless,
Mil 333,30 (suññata-phala-samāpatti +); — °-mag-
ga, m., the 'Signless Path', As 223,19 (cf. 290,5 foll);
— °-rata, mfn., delighting in 'the Signless', Ap 390,12
(suññatā-bahulo ~o) = Th-a (Ce) 506,33*; — °-vipas-
sanā, f., the insight to 'the Signless', As 223,7; —
°-vimutta, mfn., having attained the deliverance called

mfn., delighting in a°, AN IV 78,19 (~iṁ puggalaṁ);
